interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner Serafin, I am addressing you today as we enter a critical few days of the process of the negotiation of the European Union's next multiannual financial framework. The Council, under the steer of the successive Danish, Cypriot and now the Irish Presidency, has made the negotiations on the MFF all of our top priorities. There have been intensive discussions among Member States which has allowed fast and, I would say, substantial progress. The first negotiating box, with figures from June, as well as the Council's partial general approaches and the key legislative building blocks of the next budget, were milestones in this regard.

Similarly, I know that the European Parliament has been deploying all efforts to advance talks on this challenging file. Your interim report, adopted last April, is testimony to that, and I understand that work is in full swing for you to get negotiating mandates on all co-decision files by the November II plenary. In advance, and over the course of the presidency, I regularly met with the co-rapporteurs, Mr Mureşan and Madam Tavares, as well as the Budget Committee, Mr Van Overtveldt. They also joined us last month for a working session on the MFF at the informal GAC in Dublin. They have kept me informed of the work undertaken by the Parliament on the MFF and cooperation has been excellent. We plan to circulate the next negotiating box on Saturday morning. I will do a press conference in Brussels, and immediately after I will be very happy to brief the rapporteurs here in the European Parliament, if they so wish.

We really have one common objective, I think, and that is the timely implementation of the new MFF. This is paramount to ensure that there are no delays in the rollout of much‑needed funds, which will inevitably be felt more strongly by beneficiaries, such as farmers, companies, regions, researchers, students, citizens and communities, all of whom are driving forces of the Union and upon whom we rely on supporting our ambition to build a stronger, more competitive and more resilient Europe. Every effort has been made by successive presidencies in the Council to ensure a timely agreement, and it is the firm objective of our presidency, and indeed President Costa, to achieve political agreement at leaders' level by the end of this year. I do want to thank Commissioner Serafin and the Commission for their ongoing engagement with the Irish Presidency on this file. We certainly could not do it without you.

We have been working and continue to work relentlessly to support all of our common objective, and that is the reason that we put forward the revised negotiating box. Our aim with this is to take negotiations one step closer to agreement. We will seek to reflect as accurately as possible the balance of the positions around the table, from agriculture to cohesion, from competitiveness to security, defence and external action. Finding a balance entails difficult decisions. There are 27 Member States around the table. The European Parliament has to consent. That's a lot of people to keep on board, so we cannot satisfy everybody. We hope, though, that everybody will find something in the compromise for themselves. Our resolute objective is an outcome that is balanced, that coherently reflects our collective level of ambition and that we can have a timely agreement, which, as I said, is in our shared best interest.

It is our belief that new own resources will play a critical part in this effort, in parallel to volume. I know Parliament is also of this view, putting forward suggestions on potential new own resources to be considered, alongside those proposed by the Commission as well as the priorities on expenditure. Our work on this aspect has been, and will remain, guided by three key principles: any new own resources package must generate substantial funds; it has to get unanimity among the Member States; and it has to be implementable by 2028. Only this way can we build an ambitious, credible and sustainable budget. And I know that I can count on the commitment of the European Parliament as we work on this endeavour.

But beyond the upcoming negotiating box, we also have joint responsibility to ensure that all legal texts are in place in good time before January 2028. As you will know, the Council has adopted its position on the majority of sectoral files. This vast progress has been with the view to allow sufficient time to start negotiations with the European Parliament. And with that in mind. Our presidency is ready to begin this process with you once you receive your relative mandates. Our smooth cooperation will be instrumental in this task.

So let me assure you of the Irish Presidency's absolute commitment to a strong European Union budget to allow the European Union to sustainably and decisively act on all of its priorities in the interests of its citizens in a fiscally responsible manner. We do this for our citizens, their communities, and for future generations.
I certainly look forward to the debate and to the continued engagement with the European Parliament and with the European Commission.

interventions.speaker_label: Piotr Serafin, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, dear Minister Byrne, more than a year ago, the Commission put forward its proposal for the next MFF. We have proposed a budget that reflects the challenges Europe faces today, in particular when it comes to competitiveness, defence and security. We have proposed a budget that preserves the space we need to respond to the unknowns of tomorrow, a budget that continues to support treaty‑based long‑standing policies because they also contribute to competitiveness and security. Last but not least, we have proposed a budget that is financed to a substantial extent through new own resources.

Here, I would like to thank the European Parliament for your constant support. You have also pushed for new options and, importantly, you have continued to make the case for a budget that has solid sources of funding. We have also proposed a modern budget. The modernisation was not achieved simply by adding new bills to old ones. We have focused on those challenges that a single Member State often cannot address alone, and on things that have the biggest European added value with the lowest possible bill.

Some capitals continue to look at the EU budget like accountants look at balance sheets: 'How much do I put in and how much do I get out?' This approach was misguided in the past, but with our modern budget, it is entirely flawed because ultimately the Union budget cannot be captured by a simple, juste retour written logic. Our budget addresses common challenges: challenges that cannot be addressed by a single Member State alone. Even if each single Member State were to try to shoulder these challenges in isolation, the bill would most likely be much higher. By addressing those challenges together, we are exploiting economies of scale and synergy.

Ladies and gentlemen, I truly believe that, in these turbulent times, the European Union has become an anchor of stability also for our citizens. We need a timely agreement on the budget to preserve stability and predictability for our citizens in a world that is constantly changing – and changing for the worse. The ball is now in the camp of the co-legislators to take this forward, and the aim should be to find a timely agreement.

I want to recognise the Members of this House who have been working on the MFF from the very beginning. The many meetings, discussions and sometimes polemics that we have had are essential parts of shaping this budget and ensuring the democratic accountability of this process. All this brings me to the substance of the debate. I have not heard anyone questioning the priorities we have put forward for the next EU budget. So the question is not whether those investments are needed. The question is, rather, how much of that should we do together at European level, because it is cheaper and more efficient, and how much of that will be done at national level only.

The Commission will continue to accompany you along the road, as we have done from the very beginning of this process. We are also assisting the Irish Presidency in the preparation of the nego‑box. But what I want to add as well: we will play our institutional role, but we will also continue to defend our proposal because we think it is a good one and the one that brings a lot of value for money.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister, Commissioner, colleagues, look, the European Commission, one year ago, put forward a budget: 1.15 % of the gross national income of Member States. The current MFF, when it was put forward: 1.14 % of the GNI of Member States.

What the Commission did was to propose a budget at the same level as the current one, while we have more challenges. We, as a Parliament, saw that already the draft budget of the European Commission was insufficient, simply because we have to do more and we cannot do more with the same amount of money.

Any talk, Minister, in Council, to now further reduce the budget below the level of the Commission would weaken Europe. It would mean that we cannot support farmers enough. We cannot support local communities enough. We cannot invest in our security and defence as we have to. And we can also not invest in research, innovation, improve our competitiveness.

Let us see very clearly, Minister, any cuts to the budget which would weaken Europe over the course of the next years, will not be a basis for the consent of the European Parliament. This House will not approve a budget which would weaken Europe, which would not allow us to achieve our goals, which would affect our capacity to react when there are crises, when there are unexpected developments.

David Cameron was telling us all that the target should be 1 % of GNI of all Member States. We know where that ended: it ended with Brexit. We should learn from others' mistakes. We should not repeat those mistakes. And it is clear we have more challenges over the course of the next years. We have to equip the Union with the right budget.

At national level, in absolute numbers, over the course of the last seven years, national budgets have grown by 68 % in absolute numbers. Our EU budget has not grown like that. So, the perception that, at national Member States' level, governments have to consolidate their budgets, while Europe is doing more and more and the budget is growing, is not correct.

The reality is exactly the contrary. So, a situation in which Member States contribute less of their GNI and less of their national budgets to Europe, while expecting Europe to do more, would be wrong. This is why, Minister, let us work on own resources, which are the only way out to ensure a sufficient budget of the Union for the next years.
The Parliament has a mandate, the position for negotiations. It is high time that the Council, by the end of your Presidency, also reaches a common position so that we can start negotiations.

interventions.speaker_label: Carla Tavares, em nome do Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, Senhor Ministro, os desafios que a Europa enfrenta não se tornaram menores. Pelo contrário, são mais e diversificados. Não estamos perante crises temporárias, mas perante desafios estruturais, e a nossa resposta tem de ser igualmente estrutural e ambiciosa.

O valor proposto pela Comissão para o próximo quadro financeiro plurianual, de cerca de 2 biliões de euros, parece elevado, mas descontada a inflação, o aumento real é muito marginal. Por isso mesmo, o Parlamento Europeu assumiu uma posição clara no relatório que aqui aprovámos em abril. Não pedimos mais dinheiro. Pedimos que os recursos correspondam às responsabilidades e aos desafios da União Europeia.

Todos queremos uma Europa mais competitiva e coesa, com independência energética, segurança alimentar, mais investimento na defesa, no clima, na educação, na saúde, nas infraestruturas, na ajuda humanitária e nas tecnologias estratégicas.

Mas há no Conselho quem peça um orçamento mais pequeno e há quem recuse novos recursos próprios. Isto é querer uma Europa de primeira linha, com um orçamento de segunda linha. A ambição em matéria de despesa exige uma resposta credível em matéria de receitas. Um sistema de recurso próprio, genuíno, mais diversificado, alivia a pressão sobre as contribuições nacionais e traduz uma base mais sustentável àquilo que são as nossas prioridades comuns.

A escolha não é entre uma Europa barata e uma Europa cara, mas entre uma Europa subfinanciada, que vai de crise em crise, e uma Europa devidamente financiada, capaz de antecipar desafios e investir nas pessoas, nas empresas e, acima de tudo, moldar o seu futuro.

O quadro financeiro é o nosso instrumento político mais forte para enfrentarmos todos os nossos desafios comuns. Reduzir o orçamento não é uma solução. Financiá‑lo com ambição é crucial e não podemos, naturalmente, fazer mais com menos.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Julien Sanchez, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Ministre, Monsieur le Commissaire, vous osez appeler le débat d'aujourd'hui "Un cadre financier ambitieux pour une Europe forte et résiliente". Mais permettez-moi d'abord de vous demander où est l'Europe résiliente lorsque vous l'endettez pour des décennies. Car nous ne pouvons aborder ce débat sans vous rappeler votre gestion réelle. À cause de votre gestion, avec amateurisme, des emprunts NextGeneration de 800 milliards, le budget européen devra supporter pendant des décennies le remboursement de cette dette qui a dérapé et que nous paierons jusqu'en 2058.

Sur le prochain cadre financier 2028-2034, il est question de 149,3 milliards consacrés au remboursement NextGeneration. Une part importante du budget prochain qui sera jetée à la poubelle, et nous devrions faire semblant de croire que vous nous promettez une Europe résiliente et forte, alors que vous faites marcher l'Europe avec des béquilles.

Vous nous parlez ensuite de cadre financier ambitieux, mais ambitieux pour qui? Quels intérêts défend votre projet de budget? Pas ceux de nos concitoyens, en tout cas. Au lieu de réduire les mauvaises dépenses, de lutter réellement contre la fraude et de défendre les intérêts financiers de l'Union, vous nous proposez plus de dépenses, plus de dette, plus de taxes pour les entreprises et les particuliers et plus de centralisation.

Alors pour nous, c'est non. Mais notre ligne rouge, c'est la politique agricole commune. Vous voulez faire disparaître sa spécificité budgétaire en l'intégrant dans une architecture commune avec la défense, la gestion des frontières et d'autres politiques. Ce n'est pas une simplification, c'est un crime. Que vous ont fait les agriculteurs? Ils travaillent, ils produisent, ils nourrissent nos peuples. Ils sont garants de notre souveraineté alimentaire et notre santé publique. Et année après année, Bruxelles leur impose davantage de normes, de contraintes et de conditionnalité, des accords de libre-échange dévastateurs. Et maintenant, vous voulez également leur enlever la garantie d'un budget agricole clairement identifié et protégé. Quelle honte! Vous devez reculer sur ce sujet, et j'en appelle à mes collègues de tous bords politiques pour nous soutenir sur ce sujet et soutenir les agriculteurs.

Permettez-moi enfin de m'indigner du bouleversement très électoral du calendrier d'élaboration du CFP. Le précédent avait été négocié en 31 mois. Vous voulez approuver celui-ci avec quatorze mois d'avance. La France est un contributeur majeur au budget de l'Union européenne. Le président, que les Français choisiront en 2027, doit pouvoir peser pleinement sur les choix budgétaires qui engageront notre pays jusqu'en 2034. Si Emmanuel Macron n'a pas su ou voulu défendre les intérêts de la France pendant dix ans, je vous conseille d'intégrer qu'à partir du 2 mai 2027, la France sera ici de retour et pèsera de tout son poids. Vous aurez à la respecter. Il serait prudent d'intégrer dès maintenant cette donnée.

interventions.speaker_label: Bogdan Rzońca, w imieniu grupy ECR.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Nie powinniśmy dziś dyskutować tylko o tym, ile Unia będzie miała pieniędzy, ale jak wydaje swoje pieniądze. To jest istotna kwestia. I jakie ma priorytety, bo świat od 2020 roku bardzo się zmienił, sytuacja gospodarcza również. Bezpieczeństwo – tak. Unia będzie bezpieczna, jeśli będziemy szanować każde miejsce pracy w Unii Europejskiej. No, ale nikt nie chce dzisiaj się przyznać do tego, dlaczego mamy najdroższą energię na świecie. Dlaczego tak jest?

Konsekwencje zielonej transformacji są takie, że dziś, za chwilę, po południu będziemy głosować pomoc dla konających firm z Finlandii, Hiszpanii, Belgii. Musimy zatrzymać ETS oraz dyrektywę budynkową, bo mieszkańców Unii Europejskiej na nią nie stać. Unia po prostu, wprowadzając nowe podatki, obniża jakość życia jej mieszkańców i dzięki temu środowiska ekstremistyczne żerują na Unii Europejskiej. Tylko dobre centrum może dobrze poprowadzić Unię gospodarczą do sukcesów.

Musimy kupować nowe technologie w Ameryce, w Stanach Zjednoczonych, w Korei, a nie mówić o budowie fundamentów, żeby w przyszłości zbudować firmy produkujące broń. Putin jest u bram Unii Europejskiej, Nie wiadomo, co zrobi jutro. A my mówimy o tym, że trzeba budować ściany i sufity. Nikt w Unii nie sprzeciwia się wydatkom, tylko nikt nie sprawdza w Unii Europejskiej, jak wydatkowano pieniądze w Unii Europejskiej. Był plan Junckera. Kto sprawdził, jakie były sukcesy – w cudzysłowie – planu Junckera? Mamy New Generation EU. Kto sprawdza? Tylko Europejski Trybunał Obrachunkowy mówi, jak fatalnie wygląda sytuacja z wydatkami w tym akurat finansowym instrumencie.

Musimy obronić wspólną politykę rolną, spójność i politykę regionalną. Wtedy będziemy silniejsi. I liczę na to, że polski premier podczas najbliższej Rady nie poświęci rolnictwa, spójności i polityki regionalnej dla własnego stanowiska w Unii Europejskiej.

interventions.speaker_label: Fabienne Keller, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire Serafin, Monsieur le Ministre, cher Thomas Byrne, chers collègues, nous avons adopté, il y a quelques mois, dans cet hémicycle, avec une large majorité, la position du Parlement européen sur le prochain cadre financier pluriannuel.

Nous appelons à un budget à la hauteur de l'ambition européenne. Nous avons clairement déclaré que notre consentement à l'adoption du cadre financier pluriannuel, Monsieur le Ministre, ne se fera que s'il contient des ressources propres conséquentes.

Plusieurs États membres ont pourtant déjà appelé à des coupes, mais tous se tournent vers l’Europe pour plus d’investissements, alors que devrions-nous couper? Notre défense? Notre politique agricole commune? Notre compétitivité? Notre santé? Les citoyens demandent plus de l'Europe et nous devons être à la hauteur. Un budget européen conséquent est donc essentiel pour continuer à garantir les politiques européennes, mais aussi répondre aux enjeux à venir, comme la défense ou l'adaptation climatique.

C'est pour cela que j'appelle, Monsieur le Ministre, le Conseil à inclure dans la "nego-box" que vous nous livrez dans quelques jours un budget réaliste, avec des ressources propres conséquentes, un budget européen fort et à la hauteur des défis auxquels nous devons faire face.

interventions.speaker_label: Rasmus Nordqvist, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, a budget, as we talked about so many times, is simply a tool that plans our way ahead into the future. Our interim report from this spring called for a budget with the future in clear view, prioritising climate, nature, social justice and competitiveness with a clear global dimension, together with, of course, the continuing of the traditional areas.

The Council's reaction until now has been predictable. Same procedure as every year. Each country their priority. But what Europe needs is not 27 individual budgets. It is one European budget. We need to live up to our obligations, repay loans we have taken, and we need to deliver what is expected by Europeans: investments in youth, we need to invest, of course, in innovation, competitiveness, in our local communities, in food safety and health, in climate adaptation, biodiversity and the environment. This is what is expected of us.

In order to do that, we need the Council to work with us but we also need this House to work together. And here, I call on the pro-European parties: we have a task ahead of us. We need a strong budget, but we also need strong regulations around this budget. And here, the Performance Regulation is key. It's a simplifying tool. At the same time, it's a very strong tool that has a strong notion of the do no significant harm principle of green spending.
In order to have a strong budget and point our fingers at the Council, we point at ourselves and here we have a task to deliver on. I look forward to the job.

interventions.speaker_label: João Oliveira, em nome do Grupo The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: em nome do Grupo The Left

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário Šefčovič, senhor representante do Conselho Europeu, saiam à rua e digam às pessoas que estão a preparar um quadro financeiro plurianual, que é um orçamento milionário para a indústria do armamento e com cortes na coesão, cortes nos apoios aos agricultores, aos pescadores, nas verbas destinadas às regiões ultraperiféricas.

Saiam à rua, digam tudo isso às pessoas, ouçam aquilo que o povo vos tem a dizer e confrontem essas opiniões depois com a proposta de orçamento que estão a preparar. Vão constatar aquilo que temos dito desde a primeira hora. Esta proposta de quadro financeiro plurianual não serve os povos, não serve a resposta aos problemas sociais não serve a necessidade de garantir o desenvolvimento.

Esta proposta acentua assimetrias e desigualdades entre Estados, não apenas na forma que prevê para a distribuição dos fundos, mas também na forma como se prepara para compor o orçamento. Porque a discussão que está a ser feita a propósito dos novos recursos próprios da União Europeia vai obrigatoriamente acentuar assimetrias e desigualdades nos Estados, obrigando os Estados menos desenvolvidos a assumirem contribuições mais significativas para o orçamento da União Europeia.

É uma proposta de orçamento que sujeita os Estados‑Membros à imposição de políticas pela Comissão Europeia e à chantagem da lógica dos fundos pelas reformas, de os Estados só receberem os fundos a que têm direito se cumprirem as obrigações que lhes são impostas pela Comissão, do ponto de vista da imposição das políticas que devem seguir.

É um orçamento que é um «euromilhões» de fundos para a guerra e para a indústria do armamento, mas que sacrifica os fundos da coesão e as políticas que são necessárias para dar resposta às necessidades sociais e que secundariza as necessidades dos povos.

Concluo, Senhora Presidente, dizendo que é inadmissível dizer a um povo que só tem direito aos transportes, às comunicações ou ao investimento público na habitação, se isso corresponder também aos investimentos na guerra e no militarismo.

interventions.speaker_label: Siegbert Frank Droese, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Verehrte Kollegen, um es gleich vorweg zu sagen: Wir werden Deutschlands Zahlmeisterei beenden, weil diese EU nicht reformierbar ist. Die Verträge müssen neu verhandelt werden. Die entscheidende Frage lautet für uns: Soll die EU künftig über ein immer größeres Budget und neue Einnahmequellen verfügen? Unsere Antwort ist klar: Europa braucht die Souveränen Nationen vor allem in puncto Budgetpolitik.

Die EU hat übrigens kein Einnahmen-, sondern ein Ausgabenproblem. Und wer Haushaltslöcher mit EU-Steuern, Eigenmitteln, jahrelangen Gemeinschaftsschulden stopfen will, zieht aus dem jahrelangen Versagen der Eurokraten die falschen Schlüsse. Statt neue Belastungen zu erfinden, müssen endlich die Ausgaben auf den Prüfstand. Wir fordern deshalb im ersten Schritt eine deutliche Verkleinerung des Haushalts um mindestens 30 Prozent. Das Gleiche gilt für die Verwaltung: strikter Stellenstopp, Auflösung überflüssiger Behörden, ideologischer Förderprogramme für NGOs und schuldenfinanzierter EU-Fonds. All das muss weg. Es muss Schluss sein mit den Eigenmitteln. Wer einem EU-Budget mit Eigenmitteln den Weg ebnet, der entmachtet die Mitgliedstaaten. Das werden wir nicht länger zulassen. Budgethoheit ist nationale und politische Souveränität.

Frau Präsidentin! Verehrte Kollegen, um es gleich vorweg zu sagen: Wir werden Deutschlands Zahlmeisterei beenden, weil diese EU nicht reformierbar ist. Die Verträge müssen neu verhandelt werden. Die entscheidende Frage lautet für uns: Soll die EU künftig über ein immer größeres Budget und neue Einnahmequellen verfügen? Unsere Antwort ist klar: Europa braucht die Souveränen Nationen vor allem in puncto Budgetpolitik.

Die EU hat übrigens kein Einnahmen-, sondern ein Ausgabenproblem. Und wer Haushaltslöcher mit EU-Steuern, Eigenmitteln, jahrelangen Gemeinschaftsschulden stopfen will, zieht aus dem jahrelangen Versagen der Eurokraten die falschen Schlüsse. Statt neue Belastungen zu erfinden, müssen endlich die Ausgaben auf den Prüfstand. Wir fordern deshalb im ersten Schritt eine deutliche Verkleinerung des Haushalts um mindestens 30 Prozent. Das Gleiche gilt für die Verwaltung: strikter Stellenstopp, Auflösung überflüssiger Behörden, ideologischer Förderprogramme für NGOs und schuldenfinanzierter EU-Fonds. All das muss weg. Es muss Schluss sein mit den Eigenmitteln. Wer einem EU-Budget mit Eigenmitteln den Weg ebnet, der entmachtet die Mitgliedstaaten. Das werden wir nicht länger zulassen. Budgethoheit ist nationale und politische Souveränität.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, I believe we should come back to the basics. We are in a global race for new technologies and we are not winning it. We have a war next door. We desperately need investments in our regions and in the young generation. So I am mesmerised when I see Member States wanting to amputate EU budget when we need it most. This is not serious politics. What we decide now will have an impact for the decade to come.

Parliament wants a strong budget and we have put forward a solution to maintain its ambition by repaying our past debts. Three concrete new own resources are on the table. They will create a level playing field, bring more transparency and generate substantial revenues. It is now up to our leaders to be bold and to adopt them. Otherwise, they will have to explain to farmers, to people in our regions and to students why the funds are empty. And this will not be the responsibility of Brussels – this will be their own inability to take a decision.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señorías, seamos claros: sin nuevos recursos propios va a ser muy difícil acercarnos siquiera a la posición que ha mantenido el Parlamento Europeo respecto al marco financiero. No es realista pensar que, aumentando solo las contribuciones nacionales, se pueda cubrir la diferencia. Sin nuevos ingresos va a aprobarse un marco financiero que aumente los recortes en agricultura y cohesión —como han propuesto públicamente algunos países— mientras el gasto solo aumenta en defensa y control de fronteras.

Y al Consejo le quiero decir algo muy claro: este Parlamento dice «no» a esa Europa. Así que, escúchenme atentamente: más allá de las preferencias que cada país pueda tener sobre la propuesta concreta de cada recurso, el Parlamento solo va a aceptar un paquete de, al menos, 60 000 millones al año. Pueden hacerlo con la tasa digital, con el juego en línea o con la cesta de la Comisión Europea. Y si tienen una nueva idea, bienvenida sea. Pero lleguen a esa cifra.

Y lo decimos muy claro: el Parlamento no va a desligar la negociación del gasto de los ingresos, y el paquete de recursos propios va a ser una parte indispensable para que el Parlamento Europeo diga «sí» a la propuesta del marco financiero. Porque sí, queremos una Europa capaz de defenderse, pero también capaz de cuidar de su gente, y eso solo puede lograrse con un paquete de nuevos recursos propios. We cannot do more with less.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Már a Bizottság eredeti javaslata is túl alacsony főösszeget határozott meg, amelyen a Tanács tovább vágott. Érthetetlen módon Magyar Péter kormánya ehhez asszisztál. A Parlamentnek ragaszkodnia kellene az elfogadott álláspontjához, a 10%-os főösszeg-emeléshez. Hogy is mehetnénk neki ennyi új kihívásnak egy alacsonyabb büdzsével? El kell utasítani az agrárpénzek 20%-os visszavágását és a felzárkóztatási források csökkentését.

Nem kockáztathatjuk az európaiak biztonságos élelmiszer-ellátását, és a belső kohézió erősítése nélkül nincs összeurópai versenyképesség sem. Elfogadhatatlan továbbá, hogy az uniós pénzeket a Bizottság politikai alapon kénye-kedve szerint folyósíthassa a jövőben. Aki beáll a sorba, kap, aki nem, az üres kézzel távozik.

Az Európai Számvevőszék is felrótta a Bizottságnak, hogy átláthatatlanul kezelte a helyreállítási forrásokat. Most pedig az összes pénz politikai zsarolóeszközzé válna. Ezt el kell utasítani. A cél nem más, mint a szuverenista kormányok ellehetetlenítése. Nagyon egyértelmű. Végezetül úgy tűnik, hogy a Tanács új adókat is akar, a Bizottsággal és néhányukkal közösen. Kérem, ezt ne tegyék. Az európaiaknak nem kellenek új adók, azok csak elnyomorítják őket. A bevételekhez megvan az eddigi jól bevált módszer.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Ministro, signor Commissario, il Parlamento attende sabato la presentazione della prossima bozza negoziale e l'attende perché vogliamo comprendere fino in fondo se gli obiettivi che molti Stati hanno indicato saranno mantenuti nella proposta che a loro arriverà in sede di Consiglio.

Alcuni giorni fa l'Italia con il Presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni, la Romania e con loro altri 15 Stati dell'Unione europea hanno chiesto, in linea con quello che il Parlamento ha già detto, che la politica di coesione e la politica agricola non subiscano tagli nel nuovo quadro finanziario pluriennale. Ci attendiamo e speriamo che la bozza negoziale possa recepire questi obiettivi.

Abbiamo condiviso e condividiamo la necessità ambiziosa di un quadro finanziario che si occupi di competitività, di sicurezza e di difesa e riteniamo che debba finalmente affrontare, e da questo attendiamo risposta alla bozza negoziale, un diverso metodo rispetto a quello proposto alla Commissione per il rimborso di NextGenerationEU.
Ultimo tema: risorse proprie Non chiedete soldi alle imprese. Rispetto ad un anno fa, viviamo una condizione economica che questo non lo consente certamente.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, Europe is facing the most insecure times in generations. Russia is intensifying attacks on Ukraine. Our infrastructure is being targeted. China is rightly identified by this Parliament as an enabler of the Russia's war, and we can unfortunately no longer rely on American security guarantees.

People are afraid and people are scared. And what are we doing here? We are discussing the cuts of billions of euro to the common EU budget. People actually want more Europe. People are asking for this security.

So I really have one message for you guys as well: please go to the Council, go to your leaders, go to the summit and fight for a more ambitious Europe, a more ambitious budget. Find, even, own resources. Unblock it. This is not the time to cut our shield; it is time to actually strengthen it.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Keinen neuen Finanzrahmen zu haben, ist für Deutschland die mit Abstand günstigste Lösung – mit diesen Worten rennt der deutsche Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz gerade durch die europäischen Hauptstädte und probiert, Unterstützung für seinen Kürzungskurs zu organisieren. Ich will das ganz deutlich sagen: Mit solchen Aussagen macht Kanzler Merz Europa kaputt. Er ignoriert die Sorgen von Menschen, die am Ende des Monats Probleme haben, ihre Rechnungen zu zahlen, beispielsweise in der Wohnpolitik durch immer höhere Mieten. Er ignoriert die Proteste, die zu Recht auch hier in Frankreich auf der Straße stattfinden in der Bildungspolitik. Und er ignoriert den Frust über die wirtschaftliche Entwicklung. Und er schadet der Europäischen Union mit diesem Kürzungskurs.

Aber in einem Punkt hat Friedrich Merz recht, nämlich mit der Frage, wer eigentlich für den Haushalt die Rechnung zahlt. Aber anders als er wollen wir nicht, dass die junge Generation, dass Menschen, die von sozialen Projekten abhängig sind, oder dass die Landwirte die Rechnung zahlen, sondern dass die Digitalkonzerne, die Glücksspielindustrie und die Wettanbieter die Rechnung zahlen, indem sie mehr Eigenmittel zahlen. Deshalb setzen wir uns dafür ein, und wir wünschen uns, dass sich dieser Kurs durchsetzt.

paragraphs.text: Ich habe wenig Frage, aber viel Meinung gehört. Und das ist auch völlig okay. Ich will aber noch mal deutlich machen, dass ich glaube, dass es Wege gibt, dafür zu sorgen, dass die Mitgliedstaaten gar nicht viel höhere Beiträge zahlen müssen, aber wir auf der anderen Seite einen schlagkräftigen Haushalt bekommen. Und der Weg sind halt neue Eigenmittel. Und ich würde gerade von Mitgliedstaaten wie der deutschen Bundesregierung, aber beispielsweise auch der schwedischen Regierung, erwarten, dass sie sich dafür öffnen und den Weg einschlagen, auch im Bereich der Eigenmittel mehr Gerechtigkeit herbeizuführen. Das ist mein Appell hier aus dem Parlament an den Rat. Ich glaube, dass wir hier als Parlament auch gemeinsam gut aufgestellt sind.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Minister, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Um einen ehrgeizigen Finanzrahmen für ein starkes Europa soll es in dieser Debatte gehen. Die Frage ist nur: Was macht Europa stark? Über 2 Billionen Euro, die über die Brüsseler Kommissionsbürokratie gedreht werden sollen? Über 500 Milliarden Euro neuer vergemeinschafteter Schulden? Immer mehr Macht für die Kommission und immer weniger Mitsprache für das Parlament? Maßgeschneiderte Deals zwischen Kommission und Mitgliedstaaten statt einheitlicher Regeln für den Gemeinsamen Markt?

Ich befürchte, damit machen wir Europa nicht stark, sondern zu einem bürokratischen Apparat, der kaum noch kontrollierbar ist. Wenn wir Europa wirklich stark machen wollen, brauchen wir keinen Förderdschungel und keine bürokratische Regelungswut, sondern faire Wettbewerbsbedingungen, unter denen sich unternehmerische Initiative entfalten kann. Natürlich braucht Europa Geld: für die Verringerung des Wohlstandsgefälles in der Union, für die Sicherung unserer Außengrenzen und für die Gemeinsame Agrarpolitik. Aber mit diesem MFR-Entwurf, so befürchte ich, führt Frau von der Leyen Europa in den politischen und finanziellen Ruin.

Frau Präsidentin, Herr Minister, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Um einen ehrgeizigen Finanzrahmen für ein starkes Europa soll es in dieser Debatte gehen. Die Frage ist nur: Was macht Europa stark? Über 2 Billionen Euro, die über die Brüsseler Kommissionsbürokratie gedreht werden sollen? Über 500 Milliarden Euro neuer vergemeinschafteter Schulden? Immer mehr Macht für die Kommission und immer weniger Mitsprache für das Parlament? Maßgeschneiderte Deals zwischen Kommission und Mitgliedstaaten statt einheitlicher Regeln für den Gemeinsamen Markt?

Ich befürchte, damit machen wir Europa nicht stark, sondern zu einem bürokratischen Apparat, der kaum noch kontrollierbar ist. Wenn wir Europa wirklich stark machen wollen, brauchen wir keinen Förderdschungel und keine bürokratische Regelungswut, sondern faire Wettbewerbsbedingungen, unter denen sich unternehmerische Initiative entfalten kann. Natürlich braucht Europa Geld: für die Verringerung des Wohlstandsgefälles in der Union, für die Sicherung unserer Außengrenzen und für die Gemeinsame Agrarpolitik. Aber mit diesem MFR-Entwurf, so befürchte ich, führt Frau von der Leyen Europa in den politischen und finanziellen Ruin.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, europsko okruženje dramatično je različito nego što je bilo 2018. kada je predložen aktualni višegodišnji financijski okvir. Svijet 2034. izgledat će još više drugačije. Svjetska utakmica bit će brža jer ulazimo u opasnije, u nemilosrdnije vrijeme s borbom za tehnologiju, za energiju, za premoć, koja će biti još snažnija.

U takvom svijetu Europska unija može biti otporna samo ako sačuva zajedništvo, samo ako sačuva solidarnost koja je izgradila Europu i sposobnost da, kada je to potrebno, nadiđe uske nacionalne sebičnosti. Nema većeg testa za to od pregovora o višegodišnjem financijskom okviru, oko toga nema dileme, ali je također činjenica da ne možemo imati sigurnost, da ne možemo imati sigurnost naših granica, konkurentnije gospodarstvo i tehnološku neovisnost, a Europi dati manje sredstava za djelovanje.

Ako želimo biti relevantni potrebno je i ulagati u sigurnost. Potrebno je ulagati u vlastitu proizvodnju hrane, ali isto tako snažno potaknuti europsku industriju. Nove prioritete, međutim, nećemo moći i nema ih smisla financirati slabljenjem onoga što već dokazano djeluje. To znači da je ključno i da je imperativ očuvati snažnu kohezijsku i poljoprivrednu politiku, ali isto tako kroz nacionalne planove osigurati da dođe do stvarnog pojednostavljenja za sve.
Zato, za očuvanje Europe kakve poznajemo, za očuvanje Europe kakve želimo, treba nam jedinstvo ispred podjela i zajednički interesi ispred nacionalnih egoizama.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, j'entends dire que la présidence irlandaise du Conseil s'apprête à confirmer et amplifier la baisse drastique des fonds sociaux et de cohésion au prochain conseil.

Vous rendez-vous compte, Monsieur le Ministre, du message que vous allez envoyer aux Européens au moment où des centaines de milliers d'ouvriers perdent leur emploi, victimes de la mondialisation sauvage, au moment où des régions entières succombent au déclin démographique et au désespoir, vous allez leur dire: «Nous vous coupons les aides européennes»? Vous voulez vraiment laisser sombrer les services publics, les hôpitaux et les écoles dont ils dépendent? Il est grand temps que vous écoutiez enfin les parlementaires de tous bords dans cette chambre. Vous ne pouvez pas continuer à négocier comme si nous n'existions pas, car à la fin, il faudra compter sur nos voix.

Et vous savez très bien qu'aujourd'hui le compte n'y est pas. Sacrifier les politiques de cohésion n'est pas une option. Si vous décidez d'ouvrir de nouveaux champs d'action – défense, spatial, technologies propres, numérique – très bien, mais il faut les financer par de nouvelles ressources propres. Et si vous ne le faites pas, l'histoire retiendra que vous avez été les premiers à engager le déclin de l'Europe.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, vážení kolegové, kdyby se evropská konkurenceschopnost dala zachránit prohlášeními, byli bychom světovou velmocí. Když Komise představila nový víceletý finanční rámec, byl tento Parlament plný silných slov ‒ nepřijatelné, centralizace, ohrožení koheze, málo peněz a hlavně červené linie. Poslanci tohoto Parlamentu poslali přes 7 000 pozměňovacích návrhů. Jenže jakmile přišel skutečný politický tlak, červené linie začaly mizet. Jednou se bojíme politické krize, podruhé voleb. A příště se budeme bát čeho? Tak se ptám: Kdy přesně smí Evropský parlament hájit své vlastní stanovisko? Jen když nejsou volby? Když nehrozí politické důsledky? Když nás to nic nestojí? Protože červená linie, kterou posunete pokaždé, když začne být politicky nepohodlná, není červená linie, ale červený koberec pro Komisi. A nezapomínejme, proč tady sedíme. Nejsme tady proto, abychom chránili svoji vlastní politickou kůži. Jsme tady proto, abychom hájili zájmy občanů a podniků Evropské unie. A ti nepotřebují velká prohlášení, potřebují investice, železnice, silnice. Vypadá to, že největším problémem nebude nedostatek peněz, ale ohnutá parlamentní páteř.

paragraphs.text: Priekšsēdētājas kundze! Ministra kungs! Komisāra kungs! Šodienas debates temats skan lieliski – par ambiciozu daudzgadu budžetu, kas eiro padarīs stipru un noturīgu. Skan jau lieliski, bet vai tam var ticēt mūsu pilsoņi, globālie konkurenti un arī nedraugi? Nē, jo mēs tikai īstenībā runājam par nelielu naudas apjomu, kas ir tikai nedaudz vairāk kā viens procents no nacionālajiem produktiem un kuru vairākas valdības vēlas samazināt zem viena procenta un mainīt budžeta struktūru. Ar mainīto budžeta struktūru mēs pārliekam uz mazākām valstīm smagos lēmumus, kam nogriezt vairāk – zemniekiem vai kohēzijai vai varbūt nogriezt izdevumus Eiropas Savienības ārējās robežas sargāšanai?

Eiropas Komisija izveidoja lielisku programmu – Eiropas Austrumu robežas reģionu programmu. Tas ir valstīm, kas robežojas ar Krieviju, Baltkrieviju, Ukrainu. Bet naudas šajā daudzgadu budžetā tur nav. Ja tā paliks, tad šīm valstīm vēl vairāk būs jānoņem zemniekiem vai kohēzijai, vai arī, lai būtu kaut cik noturīgai un stiprai pret Krievijas veiktajām provokācijām – nenogriezt šiem jautājumiem. Tātad solidaritāte ir svarīga arī naudā.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, caro Commissario, le faccio una domanda: dove deve andare a partorire una donna quando l'ospedale chiude il reparto di maternità? A Valdagno, dove ho partorito, rischia di succedere per mancanza di fondi. Una donna incinta dovrà mettersi in macchina e sperare di arrivare in tempo in un reparto sovraffollato.

E non succede solo da noi. Succede in migliaia di territori europei cosiddetti "marginali". Chiude l'ospedale, chiude la scuola, sparisce l'autobus, e poi ci stupiamo se i paesi si svuotano. Ma nessuno se ne va per scelta. In Italia il 67 % dei giovani delle aree interne vuole rimanere. Non gli manca la voglia, gli manca tutto il resto. Non è il destino a svuotare i paesi, sono le scelte che facciamo e quelle che non facciamo.

Il prossimo bilancio europeo è nelle nostre mani e noi Verdi non abbiamo intenzione di lasciare nessuno ai margini, specie in luoghi dove vivono quasi cento milioni di europei. Chiediamo le che le aree rurali abbiano risorse certe e vincolate, che nessuno possa togliere, per ospedali, trasporti, scuole, case e per affrontare la crisi climatica, perché restare deve essere un diritto, non un privilegio.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, meine sehr verehrten Damen und Herren! Wir sind ja im Grunde da, wo wir zu diesem Zeitpunkt immer sind. Der Rat kann sich nicht entscheiden: Ist er frugal oder besteht er aus Freunden der Kohäsion? Wir im Parlament fordern mehr Geld, die Linken sogar sehr, sehr viel mehr Geld. Die rechte Seite möchte deutlich weniger ausgeben. Also alles wie immer. Und dann sollten wir uns an der Stelle mal fragen: Was passiert eigentlich, wenn jetzt nicht die Vernunft siegt?

Wir werden sektorale Verordnungen auslaufen sehen. Wir haben keine Rechtsgrundlage für neue Mittelbindungen. Das betrifft die Gemeinsame Agrarpolitik, das betrifft Horizont, das betrifft auch die Ukraine-Fazilität. Wir werden trotzdem die NextGenerationEU-Tilgung haben. Das wird Programmmittel verdrängen. Und schauen wir mal, was die Märkte vermutlich machen werden, wenn wir uns hier nicht einigen können. Wir werden eine Spread-Ausweitung haben. Wir werden die Ratingagenturen haben, die darauf reagieren. Wir werden sehen, dass Europa sein Safe-Asset-Narrativ verliert, als sicherer Hafen. Da ist auch nicht mehr viel mit souveränen Nationen übrigens, dann gibt es nur noch souveräne Banken.

Wir werden sehen, dass Forscherinnen und Forscher abwandern werden. Wir werden zwar weiterhin Europäerinnen und Europäer haben, die Nobelpreise gewinnen, aber eben weiter in den USA oder verstärkt in Zukunft in Asien. Wir werden sehen, dass wir Assoziierungsabkommen mit Dritten wieder neu verhandeln müssen. Wir werden sehen, dass es Renationalisierungstendenzen weiter geben wird. Es wird Unsicherheiten bei den Direktzahlungen geben, Bauernproteste – all das wird die Realität sein.
Und deshalb, meine Damen und Herren, sollten wir hier in der Mitte des Parlaments raus aus den Schützengräben. Wir sollten der Vernunft eine Chance geben. Dafür sind wir gewählt.

paragraphs.text: We are entering the decisive phase of negotiations on the next European long-term budget.
This is not only a debate about figures. Across Europe, people are concerned about their incomes, the rising cost of living and housing, and whether their children will have better opportunities.
The next European budget must respond to these concerns. Ahead of the European Council, our message is clear: Europe cannot do more with less.

The Irish Presidency will shortly present a revised negotiating box. We understand the need for compromise, but it cannot come at the expense of cohesion, agriculture or social investment. Seventeen European leaders have also stressed that they must remain central pillars of the next MFF, while security, competitiveness and civil protection should benefit from additional resources.
The Party of European Socialists also proposed a more ambitious budget that invests in people, and for that we need new own resources.

This is why we propose the European levy on online gambling and betting, while fighting illegal gambling, that can generate billions of euros to finance, in particular, education, health and youth. To be clear, we need a stronger budget that will fit the expectation that people have.

A tak je to aj v Írsku. Práve teraz rozhodujeme nielen o tom, či budeme mať konečne nové vlastné zdroje, ale aj o tom, či tieto eurofondy budú ďalej zlepšovať naše regióny. Ja preto presadzujem tri veci: skutočné partnerstvo s mestami a regiónmi, ich priamy prístup k európskym zdrojom a osobitnú podporu pre regióny na východnej hranici Únie. A apelujem zároveň na nás všetkých, aby sme mali na prvom mieste potreby našich občanov. paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, señor ministro, desde el Partido Popular tenemos muy claras las prioridades para el próximo presupuesto de la Unión.
Debemos reforzar la seguridad de nuestras fronteras para asegurar la libertad y la integridad de nuestros países, luchando contra el crimen organizado y la inmigración ilegal.

Tenemos que potenciar nuestra capacidad competitiva para atraer inversiones que generen oportunidades y la creación de empleo, evitando burocracia, facilitando la colaboración con la iniciativa privada y situando en el centro a las pymes.
Debemos apoyar al sector primario, porque es —y lo subrayo— inadmisible cualquier recorte a la política agrícola común.
Y, por supuesto, debemos apostar por la cohesión, la política de pesca y la excelencia educativa e investigadora.

Pero hay dos cosas que, para nosotros, son de vital importancia: la primera es que no nos gusta el diseño de los planes nacionales y la segunda es que no vamos a apoyar que se suban los impuestos a los europeos. No debemos trasladar las cargas del repago de la deuda NextGenerationEU a las empresas y a las familias. Por eso, apelamos a la responsabilidad de la refinanciación de la deuda.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, there are ministers who believe that we can do more with less. But just look around us. Today's geopolitical reality doesn't ask for less Europe, but demands a stronger, more resilient Europe.

Over the past decades, our dependency and strategic gaps have widened dangerously. Today, Europe faces an investment shortage of roughly EUR 800 billion for every single year. In the digital sector, private AI investments in the US are far, far higher than across the entire European Union. In defence, decades of fragmentation have left us, our militaries, dangerously reliant on outside suppliers. And in energy, past dependencies cost our households and industries hundreds of billions when price shocks hit.

For too long, we have relied on others for our critical raw materials. And meanwhile, China and the United States are pouring massive capital into their industries. Europe cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our competitors build the future. The proposed budget is not an expense. It's the bare minimum required to secure our strategic autonomy, all while preserving what makes Europe exceptional: helping people in need through the European Social Fund, supporting talent through Erasmus and empowering our best scientists with a robust research programme.

When fossil fuel giants rake in record windfall profits while ordinary families struggle to heat their homes, we cannot ask European taxpayers to foot the entire bill. My answer is clear to all austerity ministers: we cannot do more with less.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar, liebe Ratspräsidentschaft, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der Mehrjährige Finanzrahmen bedeutet für uns, dass wir einiges von dem, was die Kommission vorgelegt hat, natürlich auch korrigieren und als Parlament ergänzen, erweitern, ändern müssen. Es bedeutet, dass wir den Regionen eine eigene Kompetenz geben müssen, über ihre eigene ländliche Entwicklung zum Beispiel zu entscheiden und sie nicht den Hauptstädten zu überlassen, was derzeit nur im Rahmen einer Partnerschaft möglich ist und auch noch koordiniert werden soll. Ich bin mal gespannt, wie das funktionieren soll. Es ist bürokratisch, und es ist nicht effektiv.

Als Zweites, an die Mitgliedstaaten: Wir haben extrem viel nationalen Egoismus. Weshalb gibt es so wenig Nachdenken darüber, dass manchmal europäische Programme mehr Synergien schaffen als nur nationaler Egoismus? Gerade im Bereich der Verteidigung, gerade im Bereich sehr vieler wissenschaftlicher Projekte und Forschungsprojekte, die auf europäischer Ebene an der Spitze der Welt vorangetrieben werden.

Dann würde ich gerne eine Lüge aufklären: Ungarn hat nicht zugestimmt. Selbst wenn es mir als Deutsche in dieser Position dann vielleicht nicht passt, aber es ist blank gelogen, dass Ungarn bei der Kohäsion Kürzungen zugestimmt hätte. Frau Győri möge sich den Brief bitte selbst durchlesen. Ich habe ihn mir nämlich durchgelesen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the MFF in one minute, quite a challenge. The Commissioner knows that this is never business as usual. There is always something special. What is special now, apart from the centralised model in heading one, is the fact that this is the first ever wartime budget. And we have to repay a huge debt with probably new own resources.

Soon we are to hear from the Council. What is the state of play? Cuts are more than likely, and this is a real headache for this House, demanding more. A more general remark: the people of Europe don't understand and they are not interested in interinstitutional battles. They want us to deliver. Europe is an output democracy.

paragraphs.text: Само ден преди този дебат два кораба бяха ударени в Черно море, единият потъна, а екипажът е в неизвестност. Това се случи в изключителната икономическа зона на България. И без да бързам със заключения за тази атака едно нещо е много сигурно - Европа планира следващите седем години в среда, която се променя много по-бързо от нейните бюджети и от нейните програми.

Затова днес дебатът е не колко голям да е бюджетът, а дали е достатъчен за това, което искаме ние. Постоянно искаме Европа да е по-красива, да е по-сигурна, да е по-богата, да е по-конкурентна, даваме ѝ задачи, а не осигуряваме парите за това. Няма как да стане.

Като съавтор и вносител на националните регионални планове, които ще осигурят финансиране за нашите региони, аз трудно понасям разказа, че пет държави издържат Европа. Първо, защото когато Източна Европа печели проекти по нашите фондове, те си купуват влакове от същите тези пет държави, купуват скенери за болниците от същите тези пет държави, всички вкупом си държат парите в банки от същите тези пет държави и пазаруват в супермаркети от същите тези пет държави. Така че всички по веригата печелят. Нека спрем с това, защото не е истина.
И накрая, колеги, историята няма да помни колко часа сме дебатирали, колко компромиси сме направили, а дали сме имали куража да дадем сигурност тогава, когато са имали хората най-много нужда от нея.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, Senhor Ministro, caros colegas, o próximo quadro financeiro plurianual deve ser ambicioso, equilibrado e robusto, como foi dito por muitos de vós, para financiar as prioridades tradicionais, coesão e política agrícola comum, mas também para novas prioridades europeias.

A Europa quer fazer mais na defesa, na competitividade, na energia, na inovação, mas também na proteção das nossas fronteiras. Mas há uma verdade que temos que assumir: novas prioridades exigem novos recursos, mesmo que sejam moderados. Por isso, aos chamados países frugais, devemos dizer com clareza: é tempo de realismo.

Não podemos continuar a exigir mais da União Europeia, mas querer pagar menos por ela. E também não podemos continuar com o sistema em que alguns Estados‑Membros beneficiam de rebates e correções, porque uma Europa mais forte tem claramente um preço, mas uma Europa fraca custará certamente muito mais.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Es reicht. Friedrich Merz hat diese Woche ganz deutlich gesagt, dass keine Einigung im EU-Haushalt für Deutschland die günstigste Variante wäre. Das ist vollkommen inakzeptabel. Es schwächt die Handlungsfähigkeit der Europäischen Union. Vor allem schwächt das aber auch die eigene Bevölkerung. Denn ab dem 1. Januar 2028 bedeutet das dann, dass die Landwirtinnen und Landwirte keine Gelder mehr bekommen, dass Projekte einfach auslaufen. Das ist wirklich verantwortungslos und auch inakzeptabel.

Wir lassen uns als Europäisches Parlament diesbezüglich nicht erpressen. Wir wollen konstruktive Verhandlungen und da entsprechend auch vorankommen. Horizontale Kürzungen voranzutreiben und zu sagen, der EU-Haushalt muss weniger Mittel beinhalten, ist ebenfalls völlig inakzeptabel. Wir können nicht mehr Aufgaben erfüllen mit weniger Mitteln und dem Wegfall der Mittel. Ich fordere am Ende die Bundesregierung auf, wenn das ihre Position ist, diese Mittel im Bereich von Kohäsion, im Bereich von Agrar zu kompensieren. Es kann nicht sein, dass wir eine Umverteilung von den Schwächeren zu den Stärkeren haben. Das werden wir Kolleginnen und Kollegen hier im Europäischen Parlament nicht zulassen. Deswegen werden wir dem EU-Haushalt, so wie er vorgeschlagen wird, nicht zustimmen.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Alapvető problémánk van a hétéves költségvetési tervezettel kapcsolatban, ami az elmúlt évtizedek legnagyobb átcsoportosítását jelenti. Arról van szó, hogy úgy akarnak új programokat indítani, hogy arra nincs elegendő pénz. A tagállamok a járvány idején, majd a háborúfinanszírozással kiköltekeztek, az uniós kassza pedig kiürülőben.

Így hát hogyan teremtenék elő a hiányzó összeget? Hát úgy, hogy jelentősen megvágnák a kohéziós alapokat és az agrártámogatásokat. De ravasz módon összevonják az eddigi alapokat, hogy ne tűnjön fel, hogy mekkora vágásról is van szó. Ráadásul az eddigi alapokkal szemben olyan programokat indítanak, ahol nem lehet garantálni, hogy minden tagállam egyenlő arányban részesül majd belőlük.

Ha például felhizlalják a hadialapokat, az elsősorban azon országok gazdaságát pörgeti majd, amelyek jelentős hadiiparral rendelkeznek. Mindezek tetejébe új pénzbeszedési csatornákat is létre akarnak hozni. Ezt nevezik itt új saját forrásoknak. Kevesebb közvetlen támogatás, több sarc. Így hát ez a terv ebben a formában nem tűnik sem vonzónak, sem elfogadhatónak.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, geld groeit niet aan bomen. Wie meer wil uitgeven aan nieuwe prioriteiten, zal dus ook moeten durven schrappen in oude uitgaven. Maar in Brussel lijken we die werkelijkheid soms te vergeten. Bij iedere nieuwe wens komt er geld bij. De Commissie wil de nieuwe meerjarenbegroting met maar liefst 60 % laten groeien. Dit Parlement doet daar nog eens 10 % bovenop.

Dat is niet houdbaar. Daarom zeggen zes regeringsleiders ook terecht dat de begroting met honderden miljoenen omlaag moet, want Europa heeft niet meer geld nodig, we moeten betere keuzes maken. Zorg dat we investeren in onze veiligheid en defensie. Zorg voor grip op migratie. Versterk onze economie, ons concurrentievermogen en onze innovatiekracht. Want dit kan als we stoppen met de oude prioriteiten en de patronen die we altijd volgden. Dus durf keuzes te maken en durf te schrappen in de begroting, zodat we voorkomen dat de rekening bij de mensen thuis komt te liggen.

paragraphs.text: Imagine this: you throw euro banknotes into a fire. What happens next? Exactly. The banknotes burn. That's what the EU budget does today.

Right now, we are waiting for climate disasters to happen and then we scramble to pay the bill. That's us right there, funding preventable fire. As we debate the next long-term EU budget, every euro we spend – whether on transport, infrastructure, energy, agriculture – must follow a strict resilience-by-design principle.

When we know we are funding infrastructure that melts or floods or breaks, with climate change unfolding, we are wasting taxpayers' money. We need to stop paying for predictable disasters. It's time we build a resilient society and economy where everyone has a secure future.

When we know we are funding infrastructure that melts or floods or breaks, with climate change unfolding, we are wasting taxpayers' money. We need to stop paying for predictable disasters. It's time we build a resilient society and economy where everyone has a secure future.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, señor comisario Serafin, le he escuchado con sumo respeto y he visto que usted fija el reembolso de los NextGenerationEU en 24 000 millones de euros anuales, unos 168 000 millones en total calculados —y cito textualmente— sobre tipos forward actuales. Pero su propia comisión ha presupuestado 15 000 millones de euros de intereses para 2021-2027. O sea, ya vamos por 28 000 millones. Estamos hablando de un desvío de más del 87 %. Por eso me limito a hacerle dos preguntas.
La primera es: ¿qué tipo medio implícito asume usted? En fin, ¿asume esa cifra? Y ¿dónde está el análisis de sensibilidad de cien puntos básicos?

Y la segunda: si el Consejo no aprueba por unanimidad —que no lo parece— los nuevos recursos propios, que son unos 58 000 millones al año, ¿qué rúbrica va a recortar usted primero —se entiende que para pagar la deuda—?

Y para acabar: igualmente pienso que este presupuesto se lo van a comer la subida de tipos y la inflación teniendo en cuenta, como ha dicho un compañero, la enorme crisis energética que estamos viviendo desde hace menos de veinticuatro horas, ya que han atacado dos buques petroleros frente a Bulgaria en las costas del Mar Negro y esto tiene pinta de empeorar.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjereniče, kolegice i kolege, sljedeći europski proračun nije samo pitanje koliko ćemo novca imati nego, prije svega, u što ćemo ulagati. Europa danas mora istodobno jačati svoju konkurentnost, sigurnost i otpornost, ali pritom ne smijemo zaboraviti koheziju i poljoprivredu.

Danas gotovo 30 % građana Europske unije živi u regijama čiji je BDP po stanovniku ispod 75 % europskog prosjeka i zato ne smijemo stvarati izbor između novih europskih prioriteta i politika koje su desetljećima povezivale Europu. Novi proračun mora ulagati u inovacije i strateške tehnologije, ali jednako tako u prometnu i energetsku infrastrukturu, prekograničnu povezanost te razvoj ruralnih, otočnih i slabije razvijenih područja.
Europa će biti konkurentna samo ako raste zajedno.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, Comisión, Consejo, a estas alturas del debate sobre el marco financiero plurianual hay dos cosas claras:

La primera es que una mayoría de este Parlamento no está de acuerdo con la propuesta inicial —por tacaña y por sesgada— ni con las negociaciones, y sin el Parlamento no habrá marco financiero plurianual.

La segunda es que hay hipocresía entre la correlación de fuerzas en este Parlamento —escorada a la derecha como nunca— en su protesta contra la posición del Consejo —también escorado a la derecha—, que se niega a aceptar la cesta de recursos propios, servicios digitales, criptoactivos, comercio en línea... que permitirían financiar ese «más» que necesita Europa —y no se puede hacer más con menos— sin llevarse por delante ni la política regional, ni la política de cohesión, ni la ayuda a las regiones más necesitadas o alejadas, entre las que se encuentran las regiones ultraperiféricas.

Por tanto, el Consejo tiene que tomar nota, moverse claramente en la dirección del Parlamento Europeo y aceptar un paquete de recursos propios que importe las cantidades necesarias para financiar las ambiciones proclamadas.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the next seven-year EU budget is just around the corner. We are balancing major priorities: research, rural development, innovation, defence, education, young people. But underpinning all of these priorities is food security. Because without a secure and resilient food supply, we cannot have strong communities, a strong economy or a strong Europe. And that security starts with a properly funded common agricultural policy.

Colleagues, we are now negotiating against the clock. This budget must be ready for January 2028. Delayed payments for farmers cannot be an option. If a transitional period is needed, continuity must be guaranteed. Farmers cannot be left waiting while EU institutions negotiate, nor can they be held up by administrative delays. Whether it is 'new money, old rules' or a new CAP framework, payments must continue without interruption and the people putting food on our tables must have certainty from day one.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il prossimo quadro finanziario pluriennale deve essere all'altezza delle ambizioni dell'Europa. Per questo è necessario finanziare il nuovo bilancio pluriennale con l'1,27 % del reddito nazionale lordo, oltre il rimborso del debito di NextGenerationEU.

È importante quanto investiamo sul futuro dell'Europa, ma è importante anche come spendiamo le risorse. Per questo siamo contrari all'accorpamento dei fondi per la coesione, l'agricoltura e la pesca in un unico fondo. Perché non dobbiamo indebolire le politiche di coesione, non dobbiamo indebolire il ruolo del Parlamento e delle Regioni. Le isole e le aree interne, montane e periferiche hanno bisogno di politiche di coesione per garantire lavoro, alloggi, salute, scuole e servizi ai cittadini europei.

Dobbiamo garantire risorse per l'agricoltura e la pesca, fondamentali per le nostre comunità, per l'ambiente e per la sicurezza alimentare. La nostra idea è semplice: un bilancio con più risorse per un'Europa più coesa, più competitiva, più sociale e più forte.

paragraphs.text: Commissioner, to quote you: 'what we can do better and cheaper together, we must'. Thank you so much for sticking to this quote. It's two years old and I think you remember the situation.
Of course, defence and energy connectivity are the obvious things to do together, but also civil protection and areas of health such as rare diseases cease to be rare when we work together.

But we have homework to do, all of us here today. We have to go home and speak up and debate also in our home countries on precisely this issue. That is on our shoulders and it is on your shoulders to get this through on an ambitious level.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Dzisiejsza debata o nowym budżecie pokazuje, że jedni chcą osłabionej Europy i proponują cięcia, a drudzy chcą ambitnej, mocnej i silnej, jak proponuje jednocześnie Komisja Europejska.

To nie jest czas na cięcia, nie czas na oszczędności, to czas na inwestycje. Bo jak mamy mówić o bezpieczeństwie granic bez inwestycji w bezpieczeństwo? Jak mamy mówić o nowoczesnej kolei i połączenia do 2040 r. wszystkich europejskich stolic bez pieniędzy na kolej? Swoją drogą za dwa tygodnie w Polsce rozpoczynamy budowę kolei dużych prędkości.

Jak mamy mówić, że europejskie firmy mają brać udział w tym wyścigu technologicznym z Chinami, ze Stanami, bez inwestycji w fundusz konkurencyjności? Jak mamy mówić o dobrej żywności bez inwestycji w rolnictwo? Jak w końcu mamy mówić o taniej energii bez inwestycji między innymi właśnie w energię?
Tylko ambitny budżet. Trzymamy kciuki za Komisję Europejską, bo tylko w taki sposób możemy być w jakikolwiek sposób konkurencyjni z Chinami i ze Stanami Zjednoczonymi.

interventions.speaker_label: Piotr Serafin, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thank you for the debate. We are just a few days away from the publication of the position of the Irish Presidency. That is going to shape the negotiations on the MFF. It is quite obvious that, for the presidency, what matters is to build an agreement among the 27 Member States. But I do believe that the fact we have this debate today is also useful for the presidency because, in every step which is taken, be it on the Council side or be it on the European Parliament's side, we need to keep in mind that ultimately we will need to find an agreement between both institutions. Without that agreement, there will not be an MFF and that would be bad for Europe.

I would like to make three points. The first will be on timing: we should be aware of what is at stake when it comes to the timing. We need an agreement this year to make sure that there are investments funded by the European budget in 2028. Without agreement this year, there will not be investments funded by the European budget in 2028. Can we afford that situation? I believe not. That is why there is a need to work on the Council side on the overall MFF package, but also on the legislative package. And here I believe that both co-legislators have work to do, both in the Council and in the European Parliament. I know the timeline in the European Parliament. I hope it will be kept, and I also hope there will be an engagement in the process of negotiations between both institutions as early as possible.

The second point I would like to make is on the size. I am fully aware, and I was actually also making reference to that during our deliberations in the Council, that there are a lot of accounting tricks being used to demonstrate that the Commission has proposed a massive increase of the EU budget. This is simply not true. What we have proposed is an increase, but a moderate one. We have proposed to increase the budget to 1.26 % of GNI, from the level agreed in 2020 of 1.13 % of GNI. It is for sure not being increased by 60 %, and that is what we hear, and I have also heard it in this Chamber. This 1.26 % increase is done at a time when we know there are new challenges that we were not confronted with in the past, like defence, like security, like doubling down on competitiveness. So also the point that the Commission has proposed the MFF only by adding new bills to old bills is not true. We were trying to modernise the budget and find the space to fund also the new priorities, including the repayment of NGEU.

And the last point will be on the way in which we fund the EU budget because the debate on the MFF is not and cannot be only a debate on how to spend money. We also need to have a serious reflection on how to fund the European budget. Here there are two options: either we fund the budget through national contributions, or we fund the budget through the new own resources. The position of this Chamber is clear. Now the ball is in the court of the Council. I should even dare to say the European Council; based on what we have heard from President Costa, that would be one of the issues to be addressed at the level of the European Council.

At this point, I would like to repeat declarations that we have made also in the Council during the Council deliberations. Of course, the Commission stands by its own proposal, but we are open to new approaches, to new ideas that were presented by the European Parliament, and we are also ready to look at ways and means to fine‑tune and modulate the own resources package that has been put on the table. What matters at the end of the day is whether we find an efficient way to fund our common budget, and that should be the objective, which I have the feeling that the European Parliament fully supports.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, thanks to everybody for making their views known here today, and indeed to the co‑rapporteurs, particularly, for your ongoing engagement with the Council. There is one word that I say to Member States and I say to the European Parliament as well, and that is 'compromise'. I have to get 27 Member States to agree unanimously on every aspect of the overall package, and we have to get the European Parliament to consent. Nobody is going to get everything that they want, nobody.

But if we are to deliver for our citizens, for our communities, for everybody who benefits from the European budget, we have to compromise. That means compromising on the volume. It means compromising on people's priorities within the MFF, and it means compromising on the various own resources proposals that have been put forward, though I should say that there is no doubt that own resources will form a very significant part of our nego‑box and – I would predict as well – the ultimate conclusions of the MFF. But the word is 'compromise'.

We are aiming to bring us further towards a compromise by the circulation of the nego‑box on Saturday. I will engage with the European Parliament rapporteurs on Saturday if you wish, and we will continue to engage with the European Parliament as well on the sectoral files, because a lot of compromise will be needed on those as well as we work towards them. But our leaders are very conscious, and certainly the Irish Presidency is very conscious, of the European Parliament, of your role as representatives of the people of Europe. But the Member States have to first negotiate that among themselves, and we certainly bring the message home that we need to get European Parliament consent on this.
So the message is compromise. We want to bring you further towards that on Saturday. Let us see then how the leaders get on with you at the very end.

paragraphs.text: L'ordine del giorno reca la discussione sulle dichiarazioni del Consiglio e della Commissione su responsabilizzare gli europei per affrontare la crisi del costo della vita (2026/2906(RSP).

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner Jørgensen, honourable Members, across Europe, the issue of reducing the costs of living has evolved from a local market issue into a defining social, demographic and economic challenge. The pressures due to cost‑of‑living, financial and security, as well as broader macroeconomic challenges have further increased the risk of poverty. We have set a common ambition to reduce the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion by 15 million people between 2019 and 2030. But that ambition has been lacking pace, while the number of children at risk of poverty has slightly grown.

The European Union anti‑poverty strategy that the Commission put forward last spring sets a path towards achieving these targets. At the Council, ministers have recently discussed this critical subject twice. In March this year, ministers agreed that poverty is a multidimensional challenge. Often employment is not enough to break the poverty cycle, and so it should be accompanied with services tailored to the individual's needs.

In June, ministers discussed pathways for effective implementation of the anti‑poverty strategy. They concluded that well-functioning and accessible social systems are key to supporting people in need. Ensuring a life free from poverty requires a life-cycle approach with early intervention to break the cycle of intergenerational poverty at its root.

The cost‑of‑living crisis is affecting disproportionately the most vulnerable. The number of people experiencing, or at risk of experiencing, homelessness – the most extreme face of poverty – has grown. Against this backdrop, in a few days, the Council is expected to adopt a Council recommendation on fighting housing exclusion, including homelessness. This recommendation will provide Member States with a stronger framework to prevent and to combat homelessness, while promoting more coordinated and effective responses to housing exclusion.

This takes me straight to one of the major aspects of the cost‑of‑living crisis, which is the housing issue, which we already had the opportunity to address yesterday when you were debating the affordable housing act. Millions of our citizens – from young people trying to start their lives to families, essential workers and the elderly – are struggling to find adequate, affordable homes near where they work and live. Both the European Council and the Council of the European Union have recognised the need to shift the paradigm on housing across the continent and develop an ambitious and comprehensive plan for affordable housing.

These calls demonstrate a clear trajectory. The EU has to move from recognising housing as a growing crisis, to embedding it within Europe's broader competitiveness and social agendas. By aligning European Union financing mechanisms, reforming state aid frameworks for affordable housing, and streamlining urban planning rules, these political commitments provide the explicit backing needed to implement long-term solutions for European workers and communities. It is not possible to advocate for a robust European economy when young families, critical workers and students are unable to access the very cities that drive economic growth and give employment.

Madam President, Commissioner, honourable Members, in light of the ongoing situation, it is vital that we re-establish our dedication to providing real, tangible answers to our citizens at a time when the cost of living has become unbearable for too many of them. We should also recognise the key role of regional and local governments in finding suitable and concrete solutions, implementing what is done, and complementing what is done, at national and European level. The 2026 European Semester aims to address these challenges through coordinated reforms and investments aligned with the competitiveness compass and the European Pillar of Social Rights.
