interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, too many Europeans are struggling with the cost of living. They are struggling to pay their bills every month. This is despite the fact that we are living in one of the richest regions in the world. Two of the most important reasons for this are the price of housing and the price of energy.

If we look at housing first, house prices in Europe have gone up by approximately 60 % on average in the last decade, in Europe. This means that, for many people, it is impossible to buy a house. It is impossible to even find a house or an apartment where it is feasible that they can pay the rent. So we see young people staying with their parents often until they are 30. Now, if this is a choice and this is something you want, this is fine, of course. But if it is something that you need to do because you cannot afford to find somewhere for yourself, it is not only obviously a problem for the individual – not being able to start a family, not being able to get the education that you want because you have to move to get it, not being able to take the job that you are offered – but it is also a problem for us as societies.

Now, housing is much more than just walls and a roof. It is security in your life. It is having a base for your everyday living, for your family. It is what provides the possibility to live a life without worry. Somebody told me as a joke that, okay, if you have a house, you may have 99 problems. If you don't have a house, you only have one. I don't have a house. But even if you do have a house, even if you are able to pay the bills, your worries might not be over because energy prices are extremely high. And for most people in Europe, the second highest bill that they pay every month after the bill that they pay to pay their mortgage or the rent, is for energy.

Now, things have been going in the right direction. We would have paid much more for our energy had we not had the European Union. If we were not as connected as we are in our energy sector, we would pay more than EUR 30 billion more per year for our energy. Had we not deployed as many renewables as we have the last years – 89 GW last year: that's enough to supply renewable energy for at least 89 million homes, extra – had we not done that, we would have paid even more. That's good. But it still does not hide the bottom line, which is that, at the end of the month, for too many people, it is still too difficult to pay the bills.

So what to do? Well, these two challenges need to be at the core of our policies. We need to take it seriously, we need to act and we need to act swiftly. The problem with both of these problems is that many of the solutions that we need are long-term and structural. So how do we solve a problem that is here now, tomorrow, if what is really needed is long-term and structural solutions? It is not easy. But we need to do it.

So a combination of short-term measures, targeted and temporary, that does not undermine our long-term aims, is necessary. For the energy sector, we know that some Member States have chosen – and I can see why – to subsidise fossil fuels, because otherwise citizens wouldn't be able to pay to fill up the car and go to work, subsidise heating, because otherwise they will freeze. I understand that, but we need to make it temporary and targeted at those who really need it, because in the long term, subsidising something that we want to get rid of, something that is more expensive, is not a smart strategy.

We have paid more than EUR 100 billion more for our fossil energy since February than we normally do, without receiving one extra molecule. So obviously, the strategy needs to be to get away from this dependency, to use more energy efficiency measures, to use more renewable energy. And every time we do deploy these things, which is happening in many Member States, more electric heat pumps instead of gas and oil boilers, more electric vehicles instead of combustion engine cars, this is good in our fight against climate change, but it is also good for the economy of our citizens.

With housing, we need to all realise that this is going to be a long structural change. We need to build far more. We need to renovate far more. We need to use buildings that are used for something different today as houses for people in the future. We probably need to change some structural things in the way that we regulate the housing market. Lots of these solutions will be national, of course, but more and more countries are looking in this direction.

But this doesn't mean that we cannot do things in the short term. So for instance, we have in the Commission changed the State aid rules so that it is easier to build affordable homes. That can start tomorrow. We have put forward a proposal on affordable housing, which deals with the problem of short-term rentals. Short-term rentals, although they can be a good idea – for some actually, the ability to be able to rent out a room in your house or your whole house a couple of weeks a year, that can be the income that makes it possible for you to stay in that home, so that can be a good thing –, in far too many cases, we see that whole buildings are being bought with the sole purpose of only having short-term rentals or people being forced to leave their apartments or houses because there is better business to be made by just having short-term rentals. So we have created a system where we actually have shadow hotels where people could be living. This is why we now give the legal framework to the Member States and cities and regions to do something about this, to regulate this better. Same goes for second homes.

Now, we are not forcing any Member States to do this. This is not an attack on private property rights, by any means. But it is an attempt to look at what works in some countries that is not being deployed in other countries and give these tools. So this can work in the short-term. All in all, we need to realise that if people do not feel that politicians, decision-makers take it seriously that they are struggling every day, they will turn to somebody that they think will take their problems seriously. So this can, at the end of the day, be a threat to democracy, be a threat to the institutions that we believe in. And I could also maybe even be a little bit provocative. I can even understand people that lose faith in us if we don't manage to tackle the problems that are most important for them.

This is also why – and this will be my final point – some say that housing is not a European topic. That is just something for the Member States. I can understand it because, as many of you know, I used to be a Member of this House for almost ten years, and I don't remember us, from 2004 to 2013, ever discussing housing. It wasn't really on the agenda. In the last European Parliament election in many Member States, it was the number one topic. You could say that is maybe a little bit weird that citizens and media think that it should be so high on the agenda when it is not something that we deal with normally in the European Union. I don't see it like that. I see it as a very healthy sign in a democracy that when our citizens experience problems, they expect the decision-makers to act. And my opinion is, they don't really care on which level. They don't differentiate between local politicians, national and European. They just expect that the people they vote for help them solve their problems. And we need to do that, obviously respecting the subsidiarity principle, obviously respecting that there are things that are better done locally than on a European level. But we cannot just lean back and say: that Is up to the Member States. We need to act.

interventions.speaker_label: Markus Ferber, im Namen der PPE-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Ratspräsident, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Die Krise der Lebenshaltungskosten hat eigentlich eine einfache Ursache. Europa produziert zu wenig von dem, was die Bürgerinnen und Bürger wirklich benötigen: zu wenig Energie, zu wenig Wohnungen und – sorry – zu wenig Wettbewerb im Binnenmarkt. Subventionen und Preisregulierungen lindern die Symptome vielleicht für eine kurze Zeit, aber sie können keine dauerhafte Lösung sein, weil genau dieses Geld fehlt dann für die notwendigen Investitionen.

Wir sollten uns nicht bei den Symptomen aufhalten, sondern wir sollten die Ursachen der Probleme wirklich angehen. Und das bedeutet in einer sozialen Marktwirtschaft: Nur ein größeres Angebot senkt die Preise. Ich weiß, das ist schwer zu verstehen, aber ich wiederhole es: Nur ein größeres Angebot senkt dauerhaft die Preise. Beginnen wir mit der Energie. Unsere Unternehmen zahlen für Strom zwei- bis dreimal so viel – die Haushalte genauso – wie unsere Wettbewerber. Und das liegt auch daran, dass wir in der Energiepolitik nach wie vor 27 regionale Märkte haben, keinen europäischen Binnenmarkt. Herr Kommissar, Sie sind auch für Energie zuständig. Sie haben die Instrumente, um den Binnenmarkt durchzusetzen. Nutzen Sie diese Instrumente wirklich?

Wir haben gestern über die Wohnraumknappheit diskutiert. Auch hier geht es nicht darum, Mangel zu verwalten, sondern regulatorische Lasten abzubauen. Beschleunigen wir Genehmigungsverfahren! Eine Stromtrasse, ein Windpark, ein Wohngebiet braucht zehn Jahre bis zur Genehmigung. Das sind die Kosten, die uns wirklich behindern im Wettbewerb. Und der Binnenmarkt funktioniert hinten und vorne nicht. Auch darüber haben wir schon öfters diskutiert. Bringen Sie das zur Anwendung, dann sind wir in der Lage, dauerhaft den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern zu helfen.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Gabriele Bischoff, im Namen der S&D-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! The German Angst ist ein gängiger Begriff, auch in allen anderen europäischen Ländern. Wir haben in Deutschland eine neue Studie, die noch einmal zeigt, dass – ob es beim Einkaufen ist, bei der Miete, an der Tankstelle, wenn es ums Heizen geht – sechs von zehn Angst haben, dass die Lebenshaltungskosten weiter steigen und dass die Menschen nicht mehr mithalten können.

Und mit Blick auf das Wohnen: Jede zweite Person hat Angst, dass Mieten unbezahlbar wird und dass, wenn wir an die Tankstelle gehen, auch Subventionen nicht helfen, sondern dass wir sehen, dass die Preise immer weiter steigen. Und das bedeutet gleichzeitig, und die Studie verweist darauf, dass das Vertrauen der Menschen in die Politik sinkt. Und dann – Jørgensen hat das gesagt – ist es denen egal, auf welcher Ebene was gemacht wird, aber sie wollen, dass wir endlich Maßnahmen ergreifen, die wirklich auch lösen.

Der Affordable Housing Act ist da. Zur Kurzzeitvermietung – nach der Debatte gestern – würde ich noch einmal sagen, es gibt kein Silver Bullet, wir müssen alle, alle Anstrengungen unternehmen, auch hier zu regulieren, keine ideologischen Debatten, sondern Lösungen bereitstellen. Und dasselbe gilt auch für die Tankstellen und das Energieproblem. Wir brauchen eine Übergewinnsteuer, jetzt. Also alle denken, dass der Markt das irgendwie von selbst regelt, ob beim Wohnen oder an der Tankstelle. Das ist nicht der Fall. Die Unternehmen, gerade hier im Bereich von Benzin und Energie, verdienen sich eine goldene Nase. Wir müssen das stoppen. Es gibt jetzt auch eine entsprechende Unterschriftenaktion. Beteiligen Sie sich. Die Kommission muss hier handeln.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Jean-Paul Garraud, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, la situation économique de nos compatriotes est intenable. Face à l'explosion du coût de la vie les Français, champions du monde des prélèvements obligatoires, étouffent sous le poids des taxes, notamment celles qui frappent les carburants et l'énergie. Et pourtant, comme si cela ne suffisait pas, l'Union européenne prépare pour 2028 l'entrée en vigueur du SEQE2, un nouveau marché carbone qui s'appliquera notamment aux transports routiers. Une nouvelle mécanique fiscale qui fera grimper le prix des carburants jusqu'à quinze centimes supplémentaires par litre d'essence.

Cette fuite en avant doit cesser. Des solutions existent, comme celle de permettre aux États d'appliquer un taux réduit de TVA sur les carburants et les autres sources d'énergie. En France nous pourrions ainsi ramener la TVA de 20 % à 5,5 %. Il faut aussi cesser d'alourdir sans cesse la fiscalité au nom d'une écologie punitive et revoir en profondeur les règles du marché européen de l'électricité.

Certes, personne ici ne fixe le cours mondial du pétrole, mais nous pouvons décider de ne pas ajouter toujours plus de taxes aux taxes et de ne pas faire payer à nos compatriotes des choix politiques qui amputent chaque mois un peu plus leur pouvoir d'achat. Se déplacer pour travailler, chauffer son logement ou remplir son réservoir ne sont pas des luxes, ce sont des nécessités quotidiennes qu'il ne faut surtout pas oublier.

interventions.speaker_label: Charlie Weimers, on behalf of the ECR Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the ECR Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, do you know the story about the Midas touch? The Greek god Dionysus granted King Midas his wish: everything the king touched turned to gold. His food, his drink, even his daughter turned to gold.

Today, we have the Brussels touch: the power to make anything complicated, costly and scarce. Energy, fuel, food and housing have all become entangled in a Gordian knot of red tape, costly mandates and green regulation. And the left's solution? Brussels should touch more – madness.

So what happened to King Midas? Aristotle said he died of starvation. But a more hopeful version tells us that Dionysus heard the king's prayer for help and told him to wash away his curse in the River Pactolus. Might we wash away the regulations that have made Europe poorer, slower and less competitive? Hear my prayer: rid us of the Brussels touch.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, we had a similar debate yesterday on the Affordable Housing Act, Commissioner.

The cost of living is a real issue. It affects us both from a social perspective, but also our competitiveness as a Union. Young people can't afford rents. They never see hope in terms of being able to purchase a home. On a daily basis, we now see, quite evidently across Europe, escalating food costs, energy crisis and fuel crisis now as well, in terms of cost at petrol stations and diesel stations.

These are having a profound impact, Commissioner. You spoke very passionately some time previously this morning on what we must do, but we are all in this together. This is not just a Member State competency or European-wide competency, because this is fundamentally undermining and fraying away the cohesion of Member States and the European Union. They will turn to others for solutions if we do not provide meaningful opportunities.

I still believe, Commissioner, we have to look at short term and long term in terms of policy developments. Yes, energy costs are a fundamental issue at the moment. And obviously, Member States are bringing forward targeted and temporary measures. But longer term, the grids package is crucially important.

But also, the European Union has to look at the areas where it is still an impediment to Member States' planning and permitting. And whether we like it or not, there are some regulations that are there for good reason in terms of protecting the environment – the Habitats Directive and many other directives – but they are causing challenges in terms of Member States being able to grant planning permissions and permitting for infrastructure and housing projects in the time ahead. So that is an area that we do have to revisit urgently.

interventions.speaker_label: Diana Riba i Giner, en nombre del Grupo Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, la gente no vive de cifras macroeconómicas; vive de lo que le queda después de pagar el alquiler, la luz y la compra. La energía ha subido un 19 % en el último año; los alimentos, un 40 % en los últimos cinco años, y, la vivienda, un 60 % en los últimos diez años.

Mientras tanto, los salarios crecen a un ritmo ridículo, haciendo que la mayoría de la población sea más pobre cada año. ¿Y qué propone la Comisión ante esto?: multiplicar por cinco los fondos en defensa, como si la gente comiera balas o viviera en los tanques.

¡Ya está bien! Hay que parar a esta derecha que, con una mano, culpa de los males a los migrantes, al colectivo LGTBI y a las mujeres y, con la, otra saquea los bolsillos de las familias trabajadoras para llenar los de unos pocos —los de siempre—.
El ala progresista de esta Cámara tiene que pasar a la acción. Hay que poner ambición para garantizar vivienda pública, energía asequible, salarios mínimos y un Estado del bienestar robusto.

interventions.speaker_label: Manon Aubry, au nom du groupe The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: au nom du groupe The Left

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, cher commissaire, aujourd'hui le prix de l'essence avoisine encore les 2,5€ du litre. C'est du jamais vu. Partout, il faut se vider les poches pour faire le plein. Combien faudra-t-il payer demain pour avoir le droit d'aller travailler, d'amener ses enfants à l'école ou même de partir en vacances? Allez-vous faire quelque chose avant que l'on atteigne 3€ du litre?

Et il n'y a pas que l'essence: les courses, le loyer, les factures – les dépenses augmentent et les salaires ne suivent pas. Le peuple survit plus qu'il ne vit. Et il y a déjà une personne sur cinq qui est en risque de pauvreté. Alors qu'on ne s'étonne pas si la colère monte.

La convergence des luttes prend forme. Les lycéens se mobilisent pour réclamer des conditions d'études dignes. J'étais à leurs côtés, hier et ce matin encore, ici à Strasbourg. Ils demandent simplement plus de moyens, parce que la France est le pays de l'Union européenne avec les classes les plus chargées. Hier, ils criaient «De l'argent pour les lycées, pas pour l'armée». Et quelle réponse leur est apportée? La répression, les débordements, les mains arrachées, la méthode déjà éprouvée sur les gilets jaunes. Pendant que la jeunesse vise le bac, la BAC, elle, vise la jeunesse.

Mais on ne peut pas faire taire un peuple. Il voit bien que derrière la note qu'ils doivent payer, il y a un choix politique: celui de protéger les milliardaires à tout prix. Les raffineurs ont multiplié leurs superprofits par 7,5 depuis le début de la guerre. Mais hier, le centre, les macronistes, la droite et l'extrême droite ensemble, se sont alliés pour refuser de prélever une partie de ces superprofits pour aider le peuple. Six États membres l'ont demandé à la Commission européenne et je regrette que mon pays, la France, ne l'ait pas fait. Cela avait pourtant rapporté 26 milliards d'euros lorsque la Commission européenne l'avait mis en place en 2022. De quoi investir massivement dans l'éducation publique en France et partout en Europe.

Vous refusez également d'indexer les salaires sur l'inflation, alors même que cela existe dans certains pays européens comme en Belgique, ou même de bloquer les prix – rien qui pourrait contrarier les milliardaires, en somme. Vous préférez les cajoler, nous, on les fera enfin payer.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, les prix explosent et vous cherchez les coupables partout, sauf dans cette salle. Ce n'est pas vous qui avez fermé le détroit d'Ormuz, mais c'est vous qui avez ajouté vos quotas carbone aux prix du pétrole. Ce n'est pas vous qui avez asséché les champs cet été, mais c'est vous qui avez enseveli nos agriculteurs sous des milliers de pages de normes et ouvert nos marchés à ceux qui n'en respectent aucune.

Et chacune de vos lois a un prix. Votre directive sur les bâtiments: des logements plus chers. Vos quotas sur les carburants: le plein plus cher. Votre marché de l'électricité: le courant français payé au prix du gaz allemand. Vos obligations de reporting: des milliers d'heures perdues dans les entreprises et répercutées sur les prix. Ce prix, ce n'est jamais vous qui le payez, ce sont les Européens. Vous voulez améliorer leur pouvoir d'achat? Prenez des vacances.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, milí kolegové, v Evropě roste extremismus a radikalismus a my se ptáme proč. Proč? Protože příliš mnoho lidí má pocit, že my politici neumíme zlepšit jejich životy. Mladá rodina v Česku dnes jen těžko dosáhne na vlastní bydlení. U benzínové pumpy počítá, jestli si může dovolit víkendový výlet s dětmi za babičkou a dědečkem. Paní Jana, důchodkyně ze Slaného, zase sleduje, jak se jí zdražuje každý další nákup. A pak si otevřou noviny a čtou o miliardových ziscích rafinérií, energetických firem nebo velkých zemědělských podniků Nedivím se, že důvěra v politiku klesá a preference extremistů a populistů rostou. Evropa ale má nástroje, jak tady toto změnit. Můžeme zdanit mimořádné zisky, udělat z nich příjem evropského rozpočtu a peníze vrátit lidem třeba investicemi do dostupného bydlení, do zlepšení života lidí. Protože lidé nebudou Evropu posuzovat podle počtu směrnic, budou ji posuzovat podle toho, jestli se jim v ní žije lépe. A to přesně musí být náš úkol.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, se lever tôt chaque jour pour aller travailler et pourtant être incapable à la fin du mois, de faire face à l'explosion du coût de la vie. Ne pas avoir accès à un logement décent, ne pas pouvoir payer ses factures d'énergie ou nourrir correctement sa famille, c'est la situation de millions de travailleurs et surtout de travailleuses à travers l'Europe.

Les salaires stagnent et les factures explosent, est-ce que vous trouvez ça normal ou acceptable? Et ici, je m'adresse particulièrement à une droite et à une extrême droite, de plus en plus décomplexées et qui prétendent défendre ceux qui se lèvent tôt, mais qui en réalité ne font rien pour eux.

Il est donc urgent d'adopter un cadre européen pour renforcer la qualité des emplois avec de bons salaires, une négociation collective forte ou une garantie d'accès à la formation. Il nous faut répondre à ces besoins cruciaux maintenant. Sinon, pas de surprise si les Européens et les Européennes ne croient plus en nous, les politiques, ou même en la démocratie.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Harmincmillió európainak okoz nehézséget, hogy befizesse a számláit. Ezt az energiaügyi biztos jelentette ki még márciusban. És valóban: az Eurostat számai szerint a fogyasztói energiaárak 19%-kal nőttek egyetlen év alatt. Még brutálisabbak a számok, hogyha a gázszámlákat nézzük. A családok 75%-kal fizetnek többet, mint öt évvel ezelőtt. Mindezért a von der Leyen-féle Bizottság egész biztosan felelős.

Először is a kötelező zöld szabályokkal megnövelték az energiatermelés költségeit. És ezt súlyosbítják azzal, hogy levágják Európát a keleti energiaimportról úgy, hogy minden alternatív beszerzési mód drágább. Közben a tagállamok különböző eszközökkel próbálják védeni a családokat, például fixálják az árakat. Ezeket a megoldásokat a Bizottság folyamatosan támadja. Ezért egyes kormányok végül visszavonják ezeket az intézkedéseket. Így tesz a magyar kormány is.
Kérem, ne tegyék ezt! Ha már nem segítenek, legalább azt ne akadályozzák, hogy a családok védelmet kapjanak, s leginkább hozzák vissza a józan észt az energiapolitikában.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, il costo della vita è diventato il costo di sopravvivere. Viviamo in un momento straordinario: guerre, crisi energetica, instabilità economica, e il prezzo lo pagano famiglie e imprese.

L'Europa deve capirlo. Non possiamo affrontare una situazione eccezionale con le solite regole. Basta vincoli e restrizioni. Servono flessibilità e risorse vere, come ha chiesto Giorgia Meloni. Perché con le parole non si pagano le bollette, con le parole non si fa la benzina, con le parole non si arriva a fine mese.

Se l'Europa non comprende come questo momento storico sia drammatico, è inevitabile che cresca la sfiducia dei cittadini. O l'Europa cambia passo, adesso, e aiuta davvero la sua gente, oppure rischiamo di mettere in ginocchio milioni di famiglie ed imprese. E allora sarà troppo tardi.

Se l'Europa non comprende come questo momento storico sia drammatico, è inevitabile che cresca la sfiducia dei cittadini. O l'Europa cambia passo, adesso, e aiuta davvero la sua gente, oppure rischiamo di mettere in ginocchio milioni di famiglie ed imprese. E allora sarà troppo tardi.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, bij de kassa toch maar een item terugleggen. De verwarming lager zetten ondanks de kou. Of niet naar familie gaan om die volgende tankbeurt toch nog even uit te stellen. Voor steeds meer Europeanen is dit geen doemscenario, maar de dagelijkse realiteit. Het leven wordt knap onbetaalbaar.

Juist dan moeten we ons hier afvragen: maken we het leven nog wel goedkoper of maken we het hier juist duurder? Want terwijl mensen thuis iedere euro omdraaien, stapelen wij in Brussel de regels op. Bedrijven betalen niet alleen hoge energierekeningen, maar ook steeds hogere compliancekosten. Ondertussen lopen de rentelasten op, omdat de begrotingsregels hier niet worden gehandhaafd.

Dus ik wil voorstellen: we maken minder regels, de begrotingsregels gaan we handhaven en we gaan kritisch kijken naar onze eigen EU-uitgaven. Want als de mensen thuis scherpe keuzes moeten maken, mogen ze dat ook van ons verwachten.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, komissaari, yksinhuoltaja joutuu valitsemaan lapsen iltaruoan ja omien lääkkeidensä välillä. Tämä ei ole vahinko, tämä on poliittisten valintojen seurausta. Tänä talvena miljoonat eurooppalaiset perheet valitsevat lämmityksen ja ruoan välillä. Tämä ei ole sattumaa, tämä on poliittinen epäonnistuminen.

Suomessa me näemme juuri nyt, mihin tämä johtaa: hinnat nousevat, hallitus leikkaa sosiaaliturvasta, asumisesta ja koulutuksesta ja samaa tekevät kaikki oikeistohallitukset ympäri Eurooppaa. Nämä hallitukset tarjoavat ihmisille nälkää, suuryritysten johtajille veronkevennyksiä ja fossiiliyhtiöille lisää voittoja.

Tämä ei voi jatkua näin. Verotetaan siis äärimmäistä vaurautta, luovutaan fossiilitalouden tuista, investoidaan kohtuuhintaiseen uusiutuvaan energiaan ja taataan kaikille kunnollinen vähimmäistulo ja koti, johon on varaa. Fossiilitalous on tullut tiensä päähän. Nyt on ihmisten vuoro.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dalla Francia alla Spagna e all'Italia, migliaia di persone protestano perché sono sempre più povere, precarie e senza futuro. La disperazione di chi non ha un lavoro o una casa grida, ma i governi nazionali rispettano più l'austerity che i loro cittadini.

Eppure l'Europa fa pochissimo. Ho ascoltato con attenzione, Commissario Jørgensen, quello che ci ha detto, ma le misure come la strategia anti-povertà, promessa dalla Commissione, o il fondo per il clima sono una goccia nel mare. Servono molti più soldi per le case pubbliche, energia a prezzi equi, salari dignitosi e una redistribuzione della ricchezza. Serve, insomma, un totale cambio delle politiche di von der Leyen e di chi la tiene al potere.

Lo dico soprattutto ai socialisti e alle forze progressiste che sostengono la Commissione: quando la smetterete di essere complici di questa strategia contro la povera gente? Denunciare la povertà è solo ipocrisia, se poi si sostiene chi la alimenta insieme alla guerra. Deponiamo gli attuali governanti europei prima che la furia popolare e le destre depongano l'Europa.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Kissé humoros, hogy megoldási javaslatokat kínálnak azokra a problémákra, amelyeket a kudarcos politikájukkal okoztak. Nevetni mégsincs kedvünk. Értelmetlen identitáspolitikai harcokkal palástolják, hogy a migrációs áradat bedöntötte a szociális ellátórendszereket, és a szankciós csomagjaikkal soha nem látott energiaválságot generáltak.

Mégis számolatlanul öntik a pénzt Ukrajnába, és ész nélkül fegyverkeznek, ezzel háború felé sodorva Európát. Javaslataikkal csak olajat öntenek a tűzre. Új adók kivetése, megszorítócsomagok, az agrártámogatások és a regionális fejlesztések megkurtítása. És mindezt azért, hogy még több pénzt küldhessenek Ukrajnába.

Ebből nem kérünk, Ha segíteni akarnak az embereken, alapjaiban kell megváltoztatni a politikájukat. Migráció helyett családtámogatásra, segélyek helyett munkahelyekre, zöld átállás helyett racionális energia- és iparpolitikára, háború helyett pedig békére van szükség.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, πενήντα εκατομμύρια άνθρωποι φέτος θα επιλέξουν ή να ζεσταθούν ή να έχουν φαγητό στο τραπέζι. Αυτή είναι η Ευρώπη που Νέα Δημοκρατία, ΠΑΣΟΚ, Τσίπρας και λοιπά κόμματα μάς καλούν να γίνουμε.

Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση —που σε όλα τα κράτη μέλη της γίνονται μεγάλες κινητοποιήσεις για το υψηλό κόστος ζωής, το κόστος στέγασης, ενέργειας, ενάντια στους πλειστηριασμούς, στις περικοπές στην παιδεία— παίζει τα ρέστα της για τον πόλεμο. Απαιτεί πρωτογενή ματωμένα πλεονάσματα, επιβάλλει δημοσιονομικά ταβάνια για τις λαϊκές ανάγκες με άγρια φορολογία, μείωση κατανάλωσης για τον λαό, αλλά για τους πολεμικούς και ενεργειακούς ομίλους, εγκρίνετε ρήτρες διαφυγής. Αυτόν τον δρόμο ακολουθούν και τα κοστολογημένα προγράμματα των αστικών κομμάτων.

Γι' αυτό λέμε ότι για να κερδίσει ο λαός πρέπει να χάσει το μεγάλο κεφάλαιο. Οι εργαζόμενοι πρέπει να παλέψουν για κατάργηση ειδικών φόρων κατανάλωσης και ΦΠΑ σε καύσιμα και ρεύμα, στα είδη λαϊκής κατανάλωσης, για πλαφόν στις τιμές και στα κέρδη των ομίλων, για συλλογικές συμβάσεις εργασίας με ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις στους μισθούς. Κόντρα στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, στο κεφάλαιο και τις κυβερνήσεις τους, να προβάλουν τη δική τους διέξοδο με την οικονομία και την εξουσία στα δικά τους χέρια.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, en las últimas elecciones europeas, el coste de la vida, la subida de los precios y la situación económica fueron las principales preocupaciones de los ciudadanos. Y eso debería decirnos algo muy sencillo: el crecimiento económico solo sirve si los ciudadanos lo notan en sus bolsillos.

España es un buen ejemplo. Comprar una vivienda: su precio ha subido otro 12,2 % en apenas un año. Alquilar —pagar una renta— es un 50 % más caro que hace ocho años. La cesta de la compra ha subido un 42 % desde 2018 . Y a todo esto: los salarios reales siguen todavía un 2 % por debajo de los de 2021.

Sin embargo, el Gobierno de Sánchez presume de crecimiento. Ese es el problema: gobernar mirando el Excel del PIB mientras los ciudadanos miran el saldo de su cuenta corriente. Porque crecer no es prosperar. Si la vivienda se dispara, los salarios pierden poder adquisitivo y llegar a fin de mes cuesta cada día más. Y quizá la mejor prueba de que el triunfalismo del Gobierno no se sostiene es que, después de ocho años, hasta los sindicatos han descubierto que hay motivos para salir a la calle. Ah, no, que es el propio Gobierno el que ha convocado una huelga general en España. Qué casualidad que haya sido justo antes de las elecciones.
Señorías, hagamos que trabajar vuelva a merecer la pena en España y en Europa.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar Jørgensen, situația prețurilor la energie electrică a devenit o preocupare majoră pentru cei mai mulți dintre cetățenii europeni.

În țara mea, în România, prețurile în ultimii patru ani au crescut de aproape trei ori și acest lucru pentru că lipsesc măsurile concrete. Faimosul interconector dintre Austria și Ungaria, nu vrea nimeni să-i mărească capacitatea, ceea ce a făcut ca toată Europa de Sud-Est să fie prizonieră, să fie prizonieră și suntem prizonierii unor prețuri extraordinar de mari.

În același timp, ceea ce înseamnă partea de manipulare, de înșelătorie, de măsuri care ar fi trebuit luate în conformitate cu Directiva REMIT lipsesc ‑ 440 de cazuri în investigație, 20 rezolvate. Acest lucru arată că trebuie să luăm niște măsuri urgente. Dumneavoastră, pe o parte, să luați măsurile pentru ca ACER să își facă treaba, iar pe de altă parte, bursa europeană de energie. Vreți să știm cine sunt responsabilii? Vreți să știm care este transparența, să știm cine vinde, cum vinde și să fie cineva care să-i verifice?

Ultimul lucru, ieri ați anunțat că veți amâna intrarea directivei privind emisiile de metan în vigoare. Domnule comisar, dacă nu se amână și pentru producători, România, cu 50 % dintre puțurile în funcțiune, vechi de 170 de ani, va fi într-o situație de catastrofă economică. Vă rog să vă uitați la această situație, pentru că situația este extrem, extrem de gravă.

În țara mea, în România, prețurile în ultimii patru ani au crescut de aproape trei ori și acest lucru pentru că lipsesc măsurile concrete. Faimosul interconector dintre Austria și Ungaria, nu vrea nimeni să-i mărească capacitatea, ceea ce a făcut ca toată Europa de Sud-Est să fie prizonieră, să fie prizonieră și suntem prizonierii unor prețuri extraordinar de mari.

În același timp, ceea ce înseamnă partea de manipulare, de înșelătorie, de măsuri care ar fi trebuit luate în conformitate cu Directiva REMIT lipsesc ‑ 440 de cazuri în investigație, 20 rezolvate. Acest lucru arată că trebuie să luăm niște măsuri urgente. Dumneavoastră, pe o parte, să luați măsurile pentru ca ACER să își facă treaba, iar pe de altă parte, bursa europeană de energie. Vreți să știm cine sunt responsabilii? Vreți să știm care este transparența, să știm cine vinde, cum vinde și să fie cineva care să-i verifice?

Ultimul lucru, ieri ați anunțat că veți amâna intrarea directivei privind emisiile de metan în vigoare. Domnule comisar, dacă nu se amână și pentru producători, România, cu 50 % dintre puțurile în funcțiune, vechi de 170 de ani, va fi într-o situație de catastrofă economică. Vă rog să vă uitați la această situație, pentru că situația este extrem, extrem de gravă.

Okay, let's do it in English. It's easier. Anyway, I agree totally with you, like when we talk about energy prices, or when we talk about huge prices for fuels. But I have to remind you that it's the result of overregulation and taxation. That's what happens.

But just last Friday, I sent, with over 20 colleagues from here, a letter to Ursula von der Leyen questioning whether it might not be a good idea to give back the freedom to the Member States to reduce the VAT tax on motor fuels, because since 2022, since the directive, it is now banned. It is not possible for the Member States to reduce that tax on motor fuels. And four years ago it was a part of the green ideology. paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, negli ultimi dieci anni, secondo i dati della stessa Commissione europea, il prezzo delle case è aumentato del 60 %, i trasporti del 30 %, le bollette sono esplose. Non sono opinioni, sono i dati di Bruxelles.

Ci dicono che dobbiamo responsabilizzarci, ma non sono i cittadini a dover risolvere la crisi energetica. Non sono le piccole imprese a dover risolvere le problematiche climatiche o a pagare le conseguenze della sostenibilità. I cittadini vanno tutelati e questo è il dovere di chi fa politica e di chi governa.
Basta monetizzare le ideologie. Non servono slogan, né politiche dal nome rassicurante. Servono risultati misurabili nella vita delle persone.
Negli ultimi dieci anni, altresì, le politiche europee hanno aggravato la vita dei cittadini con obblighi e divieti. E dal 2027 ne arriveranno di nuovi, grazie anche al gas importato.
Il costo della vita non è una fatalità, è una scelta politica e noi dobbiamo scegliere di stare dalla parte dei cittadini, riducendo la burocrazia e non imponendo nuovi vincoli.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Rozmawiamy dzisiaj o tym, jak pomóc Europejczykom w związku ze zwiększeniem kosztów życia. Dobrze wiemy, że te koszty nie rosną tylko i wyłącznie ze względu na zrządzenie losu, na wojny czy inne kryzysy, które się odbywają wokół nas. One rosną też dlatego, że w Unii Europejskiej przyjmowane są przepisy, które powodują właśnie wzrosty kosztów życia.

Mówimy tutaj chociażby o systemie ETS, planowanym systemie ETS2, różnego rodzaju regulacjach dotyczących budowy budynków, inwestycji infrastrukturalnych i tak dalej. Jeżeli my chcemy naprawdę na poważnie podejść do tego, w jaki sposób obniżyć koszty życia, to popatrzmy również na legislację, która powstaje w Brukseli, w Strasburgu. Wyciągnijmy z tego wnioski.

Apeluję w szczególności do lewej strony sali, aby faktycznie przejrzeli na oczy i zobaczyli, co się będzie działo po przyjęciu systemu ETS2, jeżeli chodzi o paliwa. Co się będzie działo, jeżeli wdrożymy wszystkie przepisy dotyczące dyrektywy budynkowej. Jak wzrosną koszty budowy mieszkań czy właśnie nowych inwestycji. Dlatego apeluję przede wszystkim o przegląd naszych rozwiązań, a nie na patrzenie dookoła i zwalanie winy tylko na to, co się dzieje gdzieś indziej.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, siamo in una tempesta perfetta: bassa produttività, salari reali bassi, bassa crescita, prezzi dell'energia esorbitanti, l'inflazione che torna e diversi paesi europei esposti al debito.

Dobbiamo chiederci perché il modello sociale europeo non funziona più e perché la democrazia liberale non ha mantenuto le sue promesse di prosperità e servizi pubblici universali. Questo è un humus perfetto per l'esplosione di partiti populisti e partiti antisistema che offrono soluzioni semplici e soffiano sulle paure delle persone.

Noi di fatto abbiamo due fenomeni che non si erano mai visti da tempo, molto pericolosi, e cioè una recessione democratica, con tendenze illiberali ovunque, e la polarizzazione economica, con diseguaglianze crescenti.

Come si risponde? Completando il progetto europeo, un mercato unico dell'energia, e soprattutto semplificando, dando fiducia, deburocratizzando, spingendo la crescita e la competitività, perché solo così riusciremo a redistribuire.

paragraphs.text: You work the full month, you do overtime, sometimes you even work with a cold, to then hand over 70 % of your salary just to have a roof over your head – and you haven't even bought groceries yet. All while conservatives and the far right block emergency housing protections to protect speculators. That's not just a headline in Spain, it's the reality crushing an entire generation from Warsaw to Lisbon, Tallinn or Rome.

Everywhere you look, working people are being squeezed until they break: rent stealing their futures, grocery bills climbing, energy costs soaring. We don't need more hollow words from conservatives who refuse to take on the landlords and corporate giants. We need public housing people can actually afford, a Europe-wide cap on corporate greed and a system that puts human lives before profit. Stop making excuses for the markets; make markets answer to the people.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, es la hora: hay que proteger la vida de la gente trabajadora frente a la subida de los precios de la luz y el gas, de la cesta de la compra, de la gasolina, pero, sobre todo, de la vivienda. Porque detrás de cada subida de precios hay alguien que sufre, pero también hay alguien que se beneficia.

Por eso ha llegado la hora de tomar partido, señorías. En España, mientras subíamos un 66 % el salario mínimo, el alquiler se convertía en una aspiradora de rentas, traspasando el dinero del bolsillo de las familias al bolsillo de los especuladores.

Ha llegado la hora de ser valientes, y la gente de mi país lo está siendo poniendo el cuerpo en la calle. paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, при всяка криза властимащите в Брюксел се държат сякаш те нямат нищо общо с това, но тази криза е създадена тук.

Първо: парите. Погледнете моята страна България. Влязохме в еврозоната, а на народа беше отказан референдум. Българите получават най-ниските заплати в Съюза. Минималната работна заплата е 620 евро, а това са чисто около 470 евро, а плащат западни цени. България е шампионът на Европа по поскъпване на жилищата: 14% и отгоре за последната година. Едно младо семейство в България днес само може да мечтае за собствен дом. Попитайте тези хора колко им струва еврото.

Второ: енергията. Зеленият курс на Брюксел направи европейската енергия една от най-скъпите в света, а сега Европейският съюз спира и руския арктически газ, и изпраща още пари в Киев. Уж еврото щеше да ни направи по-богати, а сега идва зима, в която хората ще броят всяко евро за храна и отопление.
Уважаеми граждани, ако търсите виновника, погледнете към Брюксел.

paragraphs.text: Vážená pani predsedajúca, predstavte si, že si zakladáte rodinu alebo máte malé deti. Bývate natlačení v malom byte s rodičmi a starými rodičmi. Aj takto žije približne tretina ľudí na Slovensku. Len na potraviny zároveň minú Slováci mesačne viac ako štvrtinu rodinného rozpočtu. A to nehovorím o situáciách rodín, ktoré sa starajú o seniorného príbuzného alebo majú dieťa so zdravotným znevýhodnením. Riešenia vedia a musia ponúknuť hlavne členské štáty. A týmto ich vyzývam, aby zakročili v prospech našich občanov. Ale pomoc tu vieme ponúknuť aj na európskej úrovni. V prvom rade prestaňme pretláčať ideologické politiky, ktoré ničia náš priemysel a pracovné miesta. Systémy ETS, ako aj návrh o povinných firemných elektrovozidlách musí byť zmietnutý zo stola. V druhom rade musíme vytvoriť priaznivé podnikateľské prostredie a znížiť byrokraciu. Iba tak podporíme tvorbu kvalitných pracovných miest. Prvoradým cieľom politiky je slúžiť občanovi. Prestaňme sa skrývať za frázy a urobme konečne konkrétne kroky, aby sa našim ľuďom žilo lepšie.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, svuda možete čuti: Cijene divljaju, cijene divljaju! A što ako vam kažem da može biti još gore? Zamislite, cijene mogu divljati, a da vi živite u istočnom dijelu Europe.

Još je puno gora situacija ako vam je plaća 900 eura, a mlijeko košta dva eura, komad mesa 15 eura, šampon 6, dezodorans 5, a stanarina 800 eura. Ne daj Bože da ste bolesni, lijekovi su još i skuplji kod nas. Minimalna bruto plaća u Hrvatskoj je ispod tisuću eura, dok je u Njemačkoj ili u Belgiji preko dvije tisuće. Vjerujte mi, to čini svu razliku na svijetu.
Plaće su i dalje višestruko niže nego na zapadu Europe, ali cijene hrane, energije i stanovanja su slične. Inflacija možda usporava, ali cijene se ne vraćaju na staro.
Kako onda mlada obitelj može kupiti stan? Kako umirovljenik treba platiti režije?

Europa mora vratiti ono najvažnije – osjećaj građanima da od svoga rada mogu živjeti dostojno. Jer nije problem u tome koliko košta mlijeko. Problem je koliko košta litra mlijeka, a koju možete kupiti za svoju plaću.
Pitam Komisiju: kako, kada će naš rad vrijediti jednako? I hoće li građani Europe desetljećima čekati da njihove plaće sustignu cijene koje su već stigle sa Zapada?

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar! Immer mehr Europäer können sich das Leben nicht leisten. Und Ihnen fällt kurzfristig dazu überhaupt nichts ein. Sie wissen doch, wer der größte Preistreiber zumeist überhaupt ist. Nehmen wir mal den Benzinpreis her. Beispiel Österreich: Es wird ja in der Europäischen Union überall dasselbe sein. Am Benzinpreis sind in Prozenten gerechnet 9 Prozent CO2-Bepreisung – das ist der Green Deal, von Ihnen, von der Europäischen Union vorgegeben –, 17 Prozent Umsatzsteuer, 33 Prozent Mineralölsteuer. Übrig bleibt ein Nettopreis – es sind 41 Prozent. Einfach gerechnet: Wenn das Benzin an der Tankstelle 2 Euro kostet, dann kassiert der Staat 1,16 Euro. 0,84 Euro kostet das Grundprodukt. Und dann gehen Sie heute her und sagen, die Staaten subventionieren kurzfristig den Preis. Ja, Herr Kommissar, was machen die Staaten? Sie geben Peanuts an die Bürger zurück und der Moloch Staat kassiert ohne Skrupel. Das ist das Problem. Denken Sie einmal über das nach. Entlasten Sie die Bürger und geben Sie weniger Geld für die Kriegswirtschaft aus.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, recent, inflația nominală în România a atins pragul de 6,3 %, cea mai mare din Uniunea Europeană. Tensiunile geopolitice au împins în sus prețurile energiei în România. TVA-ul a crescut, deficitul bugetar s-a adâncit, moneda națională a slăbit, importurile s-au scumpit și singurii care plătesc factura pentru instabilitatea politică și pentru conflictele care ne înconjoară sunt cetățeni.

Pentru o familie din România, criza costului vieții nu este o dezbatere academică sau politică, este alegerea între chirie și factura la energie, între mâncare și medicamente, între a rămâne acasă, la muncă în România și a pleca la muncă în străinătate. Astăzi, simplul fapt că ai un loc de muncă nu te protejează neapărat de sărăcie.

Când Comisia vorbește despre empowering Europeans și strategia antisărăcie, întrebarea nu este dacă avem strategii sau nu. Întrebarea este dacă aceste strategii schimbă realitatea unei familii românești la sfârșitul iernii. Traiul decent nu cere privilegii, cere respect pentru oameni, pentru oamenii care muncesc, plătesc taxe și țin această economie în picioare.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, fossil energy is like a toxic ex: super unstable, and way too hard to get rid of. Luckily, I want to help Europe move on. Move on from expensive gas and petrol bills, move on from dependence on Russia, move on from polluting the global climate. Moving on from fossil fuels will also make everyday life cheaper for Europeans, and that matters now more than ever.

Lower prices will not come from short-term fixes. We need solutions that tackle the problem at its root. That means building stronger electricity grids, investing in more clean and more home-grown energy. It means cutting emissions, lowering our dependence on imported fossil fuels, and giving European businesses and citizens access to cheaper and more secure energy. Because the energy choices we make today will determine the prices that Europeans pay in the future.
Renewables are already the cheapest source of new power in many parts of Europe, and driving electrics is already cheaper than driving on petrol. What are we waiting for? Europe needs to move on.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, if you're living in Dublin and getting up every morning, packing the school bags and heading off to work to provide for your family, you hear constantly that Ireland has a strong economy, but let's be honest, that means very little if you're not feeling the benefit of it.

If you work hard, you absolutely should feel the benefit of a thriving economy and that's why, this week, Fine Gael and our Government partners brought forward Budget 2027 to help with that. We're cutting income tax rates, we're raising the minimum wage, we're reducing childcare costs, supporting renters and managing, or at least trying to manage, energy costs this winter. We're also looking forward to the future. Our new investment account will give Irish families a tax-free threshold of up to EUR 50 000 just to be able to invest in their own future.

But we have to be honest about these things. The pressures are not just unique to Ireland. We cannot control every war, every global crisis or every energy shock, but we can control how we respond to them. And that is why Europe must step up. We absolutely must do more. Controlling and supporting energy costs have to be our absolute priority, Commissioner.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, solo en el segundo trimestre, la energía y los lubricantes agrarios han subido un 22 % y, los fertilizantes, un 13,4 %. Pero, a pesar de esas impresionantes subidas, los precios de venta de los agricultores han bajado de media un 5,8 %. Son datos de Eurostat. A la vez, ocurre que el precio final de la cesta de la compra está por las nubes y no para de subir.

¿Qué está ocurriendo? El agricultor está vendiendo a pérdidas y el ciudadano está perdiendo nivel adquisitivo, y todos sabemos quién se lo está llevando: aquellos que juegan con las materias primas para que unos pocos se hagan ricos. Urgen respuestas europeas.
La primera: gravar los beneficios caídos del cielo.

La segunda: ayudar a los ciudadanos y a los agricultores —tal y como está haciendo, por cierto, el Gobierno de España con más de 12 000 millones de euros para ayudar a quienes se ven afectados por la subida de los precios— y, por supuesto, tomar medidas fiscales.
La tercera: reducir nuestra dependencia exterior. Es muy importante que impulsemos de verdad la producción europea de fertilizantes y el autoconsumo energético de las explotaciones.

Y por último: impedir que los agricultores sean, como siempre, los grandes perjudicados, porque hay que reforzar su papel en la cadena de valor y exigir transparencia en los precios también en el destinatario final.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señorías, la vida es cada vez más cara, lo que dificulta a nuestros compatriotas prosperar, formar una familia y tener un hogar. Es un hecho. Y la violencia política que la izquierda ejerce en nuestras calles no puede tapar las nefastas consecuencias de sus políticas.

La sobrerregulación y la inmigración masiva son sinónimo de pobreza, una fórmula letal para nuestras sociedades, a las que se asfixia con impuestos mientras el Estado abandona sus funciones básicas —como son la seguridad, la defensa y la justicia— para dedicarse a imponer la ingeniería social y sus delirantes políticas.

Lo hemos visto y lo vemos en Ceuta, donde el Gobierno socialista —pese a contar con información previa— permitió la invasión y dejó indefensos a los ceutíes. Y lo vemos en el resto de España, donde, tras ocho años de Pedro Sánchez y todos sus socios de coalición, los españoles no pueden acceder a una vivienda.
Para recuperar la prosperidad, la alternativa pasa por: prioridad nacional, desregulación y remigración.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, je ne me remets pas de ce titre. En fait, je ne me remets pas du fait que dans l'une des plus fortes puissances économiques mondiales, un continent dont l'objectif était l'économie sociale de marché, était la prospérité, on soit aujourd'hui en train de discuter du coût de la vie. C'est une honte et c'est une alerte.

Et pourquoi on discute du coût de la vie? On est devenus pauvres dans ce continent? Non, on est riches, on est profondément riches. Ça veut dire qu'il y a un problème de répartition. Et aujourd'hui, il y a des gens qui se font de l'argent, qui se font de l'argent sur la guerre. Ce sont des profits indécents. Et ces profits non mérités doivent être, d'urgence, redistribués aux Européens. Aux Européens qui n'arrivent plus aujourd'hui à se déplacer – comment on peut supporter une telle situation? paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjereniče, kolegice i kolege, troškovi života danas su jedna od najvećih briga europskih građana, naših mladih ljudi i gotovo polovica potrošnje europskih kućanstava odlazi samo na tri stvari: hranu, stanovanje i energiju te prijevoz.

Cijene stanova u Europskoj uniji porasle su više od 60 % od 2013. godine, a značajno su porasli i troškovi prijevoza. Europa i dalje 57 % energije koju troši dobiva iz uvezenih fosilnih goriva, a samo prošle godine na njihov smo uvoz potrošili oko 340 milijardi eura.

Građanima koji su najviše pogođeni moramo pomoći ciljanim mrežama i mjerama. Europa prije svega mora povećati ponudu stanova, više graditi, brže graditi i prenamijeniti zgrade i mobilizirati investicije za priuštivo stanovanje za naše mlade ljude.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, am să încep cu o întrebare direct către dumneavoastră. Noi dezbatem capacitatea europenilor pentru a face față crizei costurilor vieții. Din intervenția dumneavoastră am reținut doar vreo 20 de „trebuie”, „trebuie”, „trebuie”. Dar care ar fi măsurile concrete? Pentru că dacă rămânem cu „trebuie”, eu nu mă pot duce în țara mea să le spun „Am dezbătut în Parlamentul European și iată care sunt soluțiile”.

Poate vă gândiți, domnule comisar, de exemplu, să scoateți din deficitul bugetar pe care îl impuneți statelor membre costurile pentru investiții în apărare, costurile pentru locuințe sociale sau ‑ de ce nu? ‑ subvenția la energie pe perioada sezonului rece pentru persoanele vulnerabile. Pentru că altfel, doar dezbatem aici și situația cetățenilor europeni, asta ați spus-o și dumneavoastră, se înrăutățește. Avem copii în sărăcie, avem în mediul rural persoane adulte în sărăcie, avem oameni fără acoperiș și nu putem să continuăm doar cu politica „trebuie”.
De aceea mi-ar plăcea să veniți, domnule comisar, cu niște răspunsuri concrete către noi, către Parlament.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, Suomen Autoliitto kertoo meille, mikä on EU:n ongelma. Suora sitaatti: "EU-sääntelyllä nostetaan ensin fossiilisen energian ja liikkumisen kustannuksia, minkä jälkeen rakennetaan uusi tukijärjestelmä lieventämään sääntelyn aiheuttamia haittoja."

Se on täsmälleen näin päätöntä, miten Autoliitto sen kuvaa. Mutta mitä tekee EU? Kiristää päästökaupan ulottumaan myös liikenteeseen vuoden 2028 alusta. Polttoaineiden hintoihin se voi tarkoittaa noin 20 tai 30 sentin litrahinnannousua.

Tämä on EU:lta likainen isku energiakriisissä kärvisteleville kansalaisille. Niille EU-päättäjille, jotka tämän päästökauppapommin takana ovat, haluan vielä lähettää toisen Autoliiton sitaatin lopputerveisinä: "Liikenneköyhyyden tehokkain ehkäisykeino on huolehtia siitä, ettei välttämättömästä liikkumisesta tehdä alun perinkään liian kallista". Miettikääpä sitä.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, las facturas energéticas han aumentado un 35 % en cinco años y los precios de los alimentos casi se han duplicado desde el año 2015. El Banco Central Europeo nos está diciendo que la inflación va a llegar al 3 % en 2026, y esto va a ocurrir en Navidades, por lo que millones de ciudadanos europeos ya no es que sientan o vean la crisis como una amenaza, sino que la notan en sus bolsillos día a día. Y claro, es que los salarios no aumentan en la misma proporción, y todavía —hoy mismo— leemos en prensa que las empresas siderúrgicas vascas afrontan un sobrecoste del 70 % en la factura eléctrica, y ahí quiero poner el foco.

Yo sé que este debate es, a veces, un poco frustrante, porque las medidas son en el largo plazo —y son necesarias y hay que establecerlas—, pero nos afecta demasiado todo lo que ocurre en Oriente Medio y las decisiones que toman otros líderes internacionales.

Lo que pedimos a la Comisión Europea, por tanto, es que trabaje en una guía de diez acciones de impacto en el corto plazo, para que las personas y las empresas sientan que nos estamos preocupando por ellas y que somos capaces de combinar la estrategia en el medio y en el largo plazo con la acción inmediata del corto plazo.

paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, evo, na kraju ove debate ne mogu se prestati čuditi kako se i dalje dobar dio naših kolega čudi kako su sada cijene goriva visoke i priča o nekakvoj energetskoj krizi, pogotovo kolege s desnice. Ali, budimo realni, ovo nije energetska kriza. Ovo je kriza fosilnih goriva, onih goriva za koje ste vi slavili pobjedu Donalda Trumpa i otvarali šampanjce kada je pobijedio, a pitam se da li sada otvarate isto šampanjac kada dođete na benzinsku stanicu i morate plaćati visoku cijenu ovog goriva?

Kolege, možda vas moram još jednom podsjetiti: Europska unija nema fosilnih goriva. Europska unija ima sunce. Europska unija ima vjetar. I pred nama je sada situacija da možemo postati energetski neovisni i napokon smanjiti cijene energenata. Molim vas i pozivam vas da prestanete biti opstrukcija tome putu.
A povjereniče za vas: što možemo učiniti u našem sljedećem proračunu Europske unije da novac ne ide ponovno u nova fosilna goriva i ponovno u dizanje cijene stanova?

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, εκατομμύρια Ευρωπαίοι πολίτες δυσκολεύονται να αντεπεξέλθουν στη συνεχή αύξηση της ενέργειας και του κόστους ζωής. Στην Ελλάδα, σε έξι στα δέκα νοικοκυριά το εισόδημα δεν φτάνει μέχρι το τέλος του μήνα, και τρεις στους δέκα Έλληνες είναι στα όρια της φτώχειας. Οι μικρομεσαίες επιχειρήσεις ασφυκτιούν, η κοινωνία φτωχοποιείται, οι αγρότες αγωνίζονται για την επιβίωσή τους και χιλιάδες πολίτες χάνουν τις περιουσίες τους.

Κύριε Επίτροπε, ενδυνάμωση των πολιτών σημαίνει αντιμετώπιση της ακρίβειας, σημαίνει ότι η εργασία θα εξασφαλίζει μια αξιοπρεπή ζωή, ότι η κατοικία θα αντιμετωπίζεται ως δικαίωμα, σημαίνει ότι η ενέργεια και τα τρόφιμα θα είναι προσιτά σε όλους. Χρειαζόμαστε άμεσα οριζόντια ευρωπαϊκά μέτρα, να θεσπιστεί μια φιλόδοξη πράξη για ποιοτικές θέσεις εργασίας, να αντιμετωπιστούν τα ολιγοπώλια, τα καρτέλ και τα υπερβολικά περιθώρια κέρδους, να φορολογηθούν τα έκτακτα υπερκέρδη και να εξασφαλιστεί ισχυρή ευρωπαϊκή χρηματοδότηση για την καταπολέμηση της φτώχειας και την κοινωνική συνοχή.

paragraphs.text: Питам аз европейските ръководители докога ще се правят, че не виждат слона в стаята? Докога ще отричате основната причина за повишаването на цените на енергията, а оттук и повишаването на всички цени?

Главната причина за ценовия скок в Европа е доброволният отказ на Европейския съюз от евтиния руски тръбопроводен газ и замяната му с много по-скъпия втечнен газ от Съединените щати и други места. Вместо да погледнете реалността в очите, Брюксел продължава със самоубийствената си русофобия, решавайки окончателно да прекрати вноса на руски газ. Никакви фондове и никакви компенсации няма да помогнат на хората да устоят на ценовия удар. Европейските държави се нуждаят от достъпна енергия. Само така можем да се справим с лавинообразното поскъпване на всичко, защото без евтина енергия няма конкурентноспособна икономика, няма силна индустрия и няма висок жизнен стандарт.

Урсула фон дер Лайен се похвали наскоро, задето сме се били освободили от токсичната руска енергийна зависимост. Всъщност ще можем да се поздравим едва тогава, когато се освободим от токсичното брюкселско управление.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, Συμβούλιο και συνάδελφοι, στέγη, ρεύμα, καύσιμα, τρόφιμα, όλα ακριβότερα. Χαμηλοί μισθοί, υπερφορολόγηση για παραγωγή υπερπλεονασμάτων, δισεκατομμύρια σε στρατιωτικούς εξοπλισμούς και ιδιωτικοποίηση κάθε δημόσιας υπηρεσίας, υποδομής και περιουσίας. Τα πάντα μεταφράζονται ως εμπόρευμα, ως επενδυτικά προϊόντα, και εσείς μιλάτε για ανταγωνιστικότητα, ιδιωτικές επενδύσεις, και πάνω από όλους και από όλα οι αγορές.

Το πρόβλημα δεν είναι ότι ο καπιταλισμός, με τον οποίον ταυτίζεστε, δεν λειτουργεί σωστά. Λειτουργεί ακριβώς όπως είναι δομημένος να λειτουργεί. Ο πλούτος συγκεντρώνεται στους λίγους και οι πολλοί πληρώνουν τον λογαριασμό. Και αυτός ο φαύλος κύκλος δεν θα κλείσει με λίγο καλύτερη ρύθμιση της ίδιας αγοράς, θα κλείσει όταν οι κοινωνίες αποφασίσουν ότι οι ανάγκες των ανθρώπων είναι πάνω από τα κέρδη και απομακρύνουν από τις θέσεις εξουσίας τους θιασώτες του καπιταλισμού. Γιατί σήμερα ο σοσιαλισμός είναι πιο επίκαιρος από ποτέ.

Και αυτός ο φαύλος κύκλος δεν θα κλείσει με λίγο καλύτερη ρύθμιση της ίδιας αγοράς, θα κλείσει όταν οι κοινωνίες αποφασίσουν ότι οι ανάγκες των ανθρώπων είναι πάνω από τα κέρδη και απομακρύνουν από τις θέσεις εξουσίας τους θιασώτες του καπιταλισμού. Γιατί σήμερα ο σοσιαλισμός είναι πιο επίκαιρος από ποτέ.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, 47 million people – almost one in every ten European citizens – struggle to adequately pay their heating bills in a normal winter. That is obviously totally unacceptable. Now, we know that this winter is going to be tough. We know that because of the present crisis in the Middle East, energy prices are going to be even higher than they normally are.

So we need to act. We need to act in the short term, we need to deploy whatever we can of measures that will help the most vulnerable groups, do it in a targeted and in a temporary way. And we need to also stay on course in the strategy that we know is the only one that will work long term: structural change that will lead to more home-grown cheap renewables, more energy efficiency to get us out of our dependency on fossil fuels.

Now, a lot of you have mentioned taxes. I think actually that's one of the things that has united this House. Some, maybe most on this side of the room (the speaker gestures to the right of the House), think that taxes should just be lowered in general. Others, maybe on this side of the room (the speaker gestures to the left of the House), think that it needs to be more targeted. I have one suggestion that might unite us.

This is something that Member States can do tomorrow. They don't have to wait for Brussels. They don't have to wait for us coming with a proposal, co-legislation, months of negotiations – they can do it tomorrow. They can lower tax on electricity. Lower tax on electricity: that will make it easier for their citizens to have the economy get by and it will help us electrify our economy.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, this debate has been very interesting indeed, and I set out at the start some of the actions and the discussions that the Council is having at the moment, working with Parliament and with the Commission.

But I can also mention the multiannual financial framework and the competitiveness agenda. They are all about making Europe more competitive and getting more good jobs into our economy. The work we're doing this week on the grids package is designed to make our energy systems better and therefore more affordable for our citizens around the European Union.

We will continue to work on this issue as a Council and, of course, as the Commissioner says, as national governments, to ensure that we can deliver for our citizens, whether it is through the European institutions or through our national institutions.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, siamo al voto su un dossier che sembrava un semplice adeguamento tecnico dell'eurovignetta ai nuovi standard di CO2 per camion e autobus, ma che ha richiesto un confronto politico vero.

L'accordo del 30 giugno scorso è un buon accordo e rispecchia in larga misura le priorità del Parlamento. Il principio di fondo è chiaro: chi meno inquina, meno paga il pedaggio. Ringrazio i relatori ombra per la collaborazione leale e costruttiva di un accordo che riguarda principalmente due punti.

Il primo: sui rimorchi manca ancora una metodologia armonizzata. Abbiamo ottenuto una clausola di revisione che impegna la Commissione a presentare entro il giugno 2029 una valutazione basata anche su progetti pilota e, se necessario, una proposta legislativa.

Il punto due: sul regime transitorio, rafforziamo gli incentivi per i veicoli pesanti a basse emissioni. Gli Stati membri che già applicano un'esenzione ai veicoli a zero emissioni potranno aumentare lo sconto sui pedaggi fino al 75 %. Per i veicoli a zero emissioni l'esenzione totale resta possibile fino al 2031, con una riduzione al 75 % dopo quella data.

Senza accordo gli Stati membri avrebbero dovuto riclassificare tutti i veicoli, con un pesante aggravio per autorità e imprese. Con l'intesa evitiamo questo costo e garantiamo una transizione ordinata. Mi auguro quindi un voto a larga maggioranza.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, sea turtles have crossed our oceans for over 100 million years. They know no borders and no single country can protect them alone. That is why today's vote matters. By empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles, we enable cooperation with the countries of the region to protect nesting beaches and habitats, reduce by‑catch, and fight illegal trade.

I would like to thank my co-rapporteur, Ms Camara, and all shadow rapporteurs for the excellent and constructive cooperation from the first meeting to the final vote. We came from different political families, yet the text was adopted unanimously in committee, because protecting biodiversity is not a left or right issue; it should be a shared responsibility.
Let us confirm that unanimity today, and we speak with one voice for nature, and for sure turtles will appreciate it.

interventions.text:
Madam President, colleagues, sea turtles have crossed our oceans for over 100 million years. They know no borders and no single country can protect them alone. That is why today's vote matters. By empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles, we enable cooperation with the countries of the region to protect nesting beaches and habitats, reduce by‑catch, and fight illegal trade.

I would like to thank my co-rapporteur, Ms Camara, and all shadow rapporteurs for the excellent and constructive cooperation from the first meeting to the final vote. We came from different political families, yet the text was adopted unanimously in committee, because protecting biodiversity is not a left or right issue; it should be a shared responsibility.

Let us confirm that unanimity today, and we speak with one voice for nature, and for sure turtles will appreciate it.

paragraphs.text: – Before the vote:

interventions.text: – Before the vote:

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, gracias a este Fondo, 400 trabajadores gallegos despedidos del sector de la automoción volverán a encontrar un trabajo. Este Fondo es una muestra de la solidaridad europea, pero también nos obliga a preguntarnos hacia dónde vamos, porque ayudar a quien pierde un trabajo es imprescindible, pero evitar que Europa pierda industria y oportunidades también lo es.

Lo digo porque, hace poco, recibimos una carta de algunos Gobiernos europeos exigiendo más recortes, y a eso lo llamaban «preparar a Europa para el futuro». ¿En serio? ¿Vamos a recortar la PAC y vamos a crear un fondo de compensación para agricultores que abandonen los campos? A los jóvenes, que nos piden un plan de vivienda, ¿les vamos a crear también un fondo como perdedores frente a los fondos de inversión y fondos buitre? ¿De qué sirve blindar nuestras fronteras si dentro solo quedan fábricas cerradas, campos abandonados y plazas llenas de jóvenes y tiendas de campaña porque no pueden encontrar una casa?

Desde luego, hay muchos Gobiernos que parece que son mucho más valientes para apretar a su propia ciudadanía que, por ejemplo, para aprobar una tasa frente a las grandes empresas tecnológicas, que están ganando miles de millones de euros gracias a nuestro mercado único y aún se atreven —por cierto— a influir en nuestros procesos electorales.

Por eso este Fondo es muy importante, porque nuestros trabajadores gallegos claro que merecen nuestro apoyo y nuestro respeto; pero, sobre todo, merecen que no nos resignemos a que su historia se repita y que estos fondos de compensación sean una mera disculpa por la Europa que pudimos construir y que no nos atrevimos a defender. Porque iniciamos este proyecto para defender y construir nuestro futuro, no para administrar nuestra decadencia.

paragraphs.text: – After the vote on Amendment 69:

interventions.text: – After the vote on Amendment 69:

paragraphs.text: Madam President, a new and terrifying Chinese law came into force last Thursday. The Chinese army will be in charge of all technology, all data and all software of Chinese companies – also here in Europe – when President Xi would decide to mobilise its army. So let that sink in, colleagues. Companies bound by law to serve China's military then cannot be a trusted supplier of Europe's critical infrastructure.

I therefore propose an oral amendment to paragraph 1, point aa) by adding: 'condemns China's revised National Defence Mobilisation Law, which came into effect on 1 October 2026 and brings all Chinese technology, all data and software under direct authority of China's military leadership in the event of mobilisation; highlights the urgent need to de-risk critical ICT supply chains;'.
I hope I can count on your support.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, Monsieur le représentant du Conseil, chers collègues, les Européens payent cher le prix de vos choix politiques. Ils le payent à la pompe, ils le payent à la caisse, ils le payent parfois de leur vie, parce que vous avez refusé d'agir contre dérèglement climatique, les polluants éternels ou les pesticides chimiques.

Voilà pourquoi nous, les écologistes, avons demandé ce débat aujourd'hui sur la taxation des superprofits des superpollueurs pour protéger la santé et le pouvoir d'achat des Européennes et des Européens, et pour, au fond, vous poser une question simple: quand donc préférerez-vous les Européens aux dividendes de la finance?

Prenons l'exemple des géants du pétrole. Ils ont accumulé plus de 7 milliards d'euros de profits en moins de six mois, juste dans l'Union européenne. Mais hier, vous vous êtes à nouveau opposés à la taxation de leurs superprofits. Qu'ont-ils donc fait pour être ainsi exonérés de toute responsabilité dans l'explosion des prix à la pompe, de la précarité ou du dérèglement climatique? Pire encore, le patron de la plus grande entreprise pétrolière européenne, TotalEnergies, revendique désormais préférer un monde en bouleversement plutôt qu'un monde en paix.

Chers collègues, taxer les superprofits est possible. L'Espagne le fait, plusieurs États le réclament. Une telle taxe rapporterait 6 milliards par an à l'Europe. Comment peut-on s'en passer quand il manque encore 750 milliards pour financer la transformation énergétique et alléger les factures des ménages? Et laissez-moi vous dire que c'était en réalité peu demander, car ces entreprises écocidaires devraient être mises hors d'état de nuire à notre économie et à notre population. Elles devraient passer sous contrôle public européen afin qu'elles cessent de polluer, d'alimenter les guerres et de vider les portefeuilles des citoyens.

Mais malheureusement, la liste des pollueurs ne s'arrête pas aux portes des énergies fossiles. Parce que vous voulez aussi donner un blanc-seing aux producteurs de pesticides – Bayer en tête, qui vend aussi des médicaments, comme si Bayer avait besoin d'aides de l'Europe pour engraisser encore ses actionnaires.

Là encore, nous vous invitons à faire le choix des gens. Le choix de Théo Grataloup, dont la maman Sabine, femme courage, comme son fils, viendra ici vous interpeller contre ces pesticides responsables de la maladie de son enfant. Le choix de Laure Marivain, fleuriste, qui a perdu sa fille après avoir manipulé, enceinte, des fleurs traitées aux pesticides. Le choix de Paul François, agriculteur intoxiqué par un produit de Monsanto.

Mais à ces familles, que répondez-vous? Les firmes des pesticides ont menti et menti encore. Elles ont caché des études scientifiques aux autorités européennes. Elles devraient au fond se voir interdites de vendre et pesticides et médicaments. Elles le font pour des profits jamais partagés, mais vous les soutenez encore et toujours. Cela doit cesser.

Enfin, les polluants éternels. L'Europe doit les interdire, tous, maintenant. Et si nous avons utilisé notre niche écologiste pour organiser ce débat aujourd'hui, c'est parce que vos groupes politiques ont toujours refusé de le mettre à l'ordre du jour. Pourquoi? Craignez-vous donc d'assumer publiquement votre position allant à l'encontre de la santé des citoyens?

Je pourrais vous parler de Jean-René qui travaille dans la chimie le jour et pompier volontaire le soir, le corps imbibé de PFAS toute la journée pour protéger nos vies; des «Mamme No PFAS» comme Cristina Guarda en Italie, tellement inquiètes pour la santé de leurs enfants; ou des ouvriers de Solvay-Salindres, licenciés sèchement après avoir été exposés à des niveaux hyperélevés de polluants éternels. interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, many thanks to Ms Toussaint and thank you very much to the European Greens for putting this forward. Congratulations indeed to the co-chairs of the party who were elected, I think, in their group yesterday.

Due to recent developments in the Middle East – the honourable Members all know this, the Commission knows this, the Member States know this – the price of fossil fuel has steadily been rising. The cost of living, which is a major theme of the plenary this week, if I may say, has significantly increased for households across the European Union, and that has led us all to consider what can be done to mitigate the negative consequences for citizens.

The idea of taxing those energy companies for whom the current conditions generate windfall profits has been floated as a possible measure to compensate for the burden placed on consumers. Therefore, it's a very timely debate to have.

It's a topic that, of course, is also on the minds of governments around Europe, reflected in the joint letter sent to the Presidency in August by six Member States, which called for an EU-wide framework to tackle windfall profits of energy companies.

I am sure we all remember the situation in autumn 2022, when we had a very strong spike in energy prices after the illegal invasion of Ukraine by Russia and its ongoing aggression. Back then, the Council adopted an exceptional temporary emergency measure in the form of a minimum solidarity contribution on surplus profits of energy companies in 2022 and 2023. So we have done this already.

The Irish Presidency is fully aware that equally today taxing windfall profits of large companies is among the tax measures that could be considered to respond to the concerns related to the rising cost of living that we are experiencing today.

The Presidency, of course, has every intention to allow for Member States to exchange views and best practice on this, to deepen our understanding and to adjust the relevant policies. As a Presidency, we do count on the Commission and Commissioner Jørgensen to help us in this regard by monitoring closely the energy prices and especially the data on excess profits in the energy sector.

It is within the Commission's remit to carefully assess whether the conditions are in place that would warrant an initiative similar to the one we took before in 2022, and I am sure that's exactly what Commissioner Jørgensen is about to reassure us on. The Commission's AccelerateEU package of April 2026 recognises that Member States are free to take action on such measures and, of course, the Commission will respect the decisions of Member States and help them provide best practice.

The measures that Member States have taken are already generally fully in line with the strategic priorities of the EU and indeed the principles of EU law, such as 'polluter pays', as well as the overarching aim to decarbonise and pursue the electrification of our economies.

The Presidency will keep the debate flowing on this and, of course, we are ready to play our role. I should say that the topic of windfall taxation will be discussed this week at ECOFIN under the Irish Presidency.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, today's debate takes place against the backdrop of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and price evolutions in the energy commodity markets. In response to these developments, the Commission presented the AccelerateEU communication in April this year. The communication provides a dynamic response to the challenges of high energy prices. It supports Member States' efforts to protect consumers and industry from high price shocks. In July, we also published our proposal on future‑proofing electricity bills. With the proposal, we aim to help Member States in tailoring their energy taxation systems so that they can stimulate electrification and move away from expensive imported fossil fuels.

On windfall taxation specifically, the Commission is of the view that Member States can take measures on taxation of windfall profits to ensure social fairness. Corporate taxation falls mainly in the realm of national competency. Some Member States have come forward with domestic measures to tax windfall profits. Others have prolonged existing domestic measures. The Commission will respect Member States' decisions. We will assist their efforts, provide best practices on national measures and assess their impacts on the single markets.

As energy prices continue to rise, we must stand ready to deploy additional tools to protect consumers if needed. As President von der Leyen mentioned yesterday, our role is to give Member States the tools and flexibility to respond. In this respect, we will prolong and possibly amend the temporary State aid framework. We will extend by one year the flexibility on methane to exports. We will launch a strategic dialogue on European refineries and set up a new task force to bundle energy demand. This will cater for the specific energy mix in Member States. These actions, combined with the measures set out in the AccelerateEU, provide us with a comprehensive toolbox to reduce energy bills and support citizens.

interventions.speaker_label: Markus Ferber, im Namen der PPE-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Herr Ratspräsident, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen, liebe Kollegen! Eine Übergewinnsteuer senkt keine einzige Energierechnung. Sie ändert nichts an hohen Energiepreisen. Sie löst das Problem nicht, sondern es ist reine Symbolpolitik. Das Geld landet zwar in Haushalten, aber in den öffentlichen Haushalten, nicht bei den Bürgerinnen und Bürgern. Wer Verschmutzer zur Kasse bitten will – das tun wir doch alles längst! Im Emissionshandel, in vielen Gesetzgebungen zwingen wir den Unternehmen Kosten zu Recht auf, um Verschmutzungen zu reduzieren.

Und das, diese Investitionen brauchen wir. Denn hohe Preise sind ja auch ein Marktsignal. Es fehlt Angebot. Die Gewinne finanzieren neue Speicherterminals und Netze und auch Wind und Solarparks. Wer diese Gewinne wegbesteuert, sobald es knapp wird, verhindert genau diese Investitionen, die dringend notwendig sind, um die Knappheit zu überwinden.

Was ist überhaupt ein Übergewinn? Im Jahr 2022 galt als übermäßig, was 20 % über dem Durchschnitt der Vorjahre lag. Das ist doch eine willkürliche Grenze. In Deutschland laufen Gerichtsverfahren deswegen gegen den Staat, weil er keine klare Definition für Übergewinn vorlegen konnte. Wer in schlechten Jahren Verluste schreibt, bekommt ja auch nichts zurück. Wer gut gewirtschaftet hat, der wird bestraft. Und wer nicht weiß, welche Gewinne morgen als Übergewinne gelten könnten, der wird auch nicht investieren. Wer die Energiepreise senken will, braucht mehr Angebot, besser ausgebaute Netze, niedrigere staatliche Abgaben auf Energie. Dazu gehören auch mehr Investitionen in erneuerbare Energieträger. Die gibt es aber nur, wenn Gewinne nicht abgeschöpft werden. Wer Investitionen bestraft, bekommt keine billigere Energie. Er bekommt weniger Energie. Deswegen ist eine Übergewinnsteuer keine Idee, die die EVP-Fraktion unterstützen kann.
