interventions.speaker_label: Silvia Sardone, a nome del gruppo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, non avevamo dubbi, per la sinistra la soluzione è sempre una: nuove tasse. Ma dobbiamo dire ai cittadini europei la verità: l'unica vera tassa per famiglie, imprese, consumatori e agricoltori siete voi.

Voi con il Green Deal avete portato più tasse, più oneri per le imprese, più costi per i consumatori, bollette più costose. Voi con la direttiva sulle case green volete che i proprietari di casa spendano migliaia di euro per rinnovare le proprie abitazioni. Voi, sempre voi, criminalizzando gli agricoltori e gli allevatori, li avete resi più poveri. Voi, con assurde regole ambientali, state facendo chiudere migliaia di aziende. Voi, con la vostra ideologia, state affossando l'Europa.
Quindi, non solo non vogliamo nuove tasse, che per voi è una ricetta rodata, ma non vogliamo nemmeno continuare a subire le vostre assurde politiche.

interventions.speaker_label: Pascal Canfin, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, je suis frappé que dans ce débat, il y ait une très grande polarisation sur le sujet. Quand on regarde les six États membres qui ont fait en sorte qu'il y ait ce débat, maintenant, au Conseil, vous avez l'Italie qui n'est pas spécialement un gouvernement gauchiste, vous avez l'Allemagne dans lequel il y a justement du centre droit et du centre gauche, vous avez le Portugal qui n'est pas un gouvernement gauchiste non plus.

Donc il y a différents pays, y compris l'Espagne socialiste. Donc cela veut dire qu'au Conseil, il y a des pays qui sont gouvernés par des forces politiques très différentes, qui pensent que c'est une bonne idée. Donc, ce débat doit avoir lieu.

Ça ne fait pas des entreprises concernées des salauds. Ça ne fait pas de ces entreprises concernées des profiteurs de guerre. Ça fait simplement de ces entreprises concernées des acteurs économiques qui sont assis sur une rente qui fait qu'ils gagnent des dizaines de milliards d'euros sans faire un seul investissement de plus, sans avoir fait une seule chose pour justifier ces dizaines de milliards de profits.
Ce débat ne doit pas être moral, il doit être économique; il est justifié, il doit avoir lieu aussi dans cette instance.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, this summer, Belgium had its biggest wildfire ever. Farmers drove tractors full of water to the firefighters and volunteers brought them food and water. This same summer, the five biggest oil companies made 6 000 dollars in profit every second. We need to tax them, and we need to use that money to protect people against extreme weather.

We've done it before. When Russia invaded Ukraine, energy prices went through the roof, and oil giants were making huge profits just like now. So Europe made them pay. Guess what? We can do that again. We can use it so our care homes and our hospitals actually stay cool, so our kids' schools have shade. That's the Europe where protection against the next heat wave is paid for by the companies that actually profit from it. So by the time I finish this 60‑second speech, those five companies will have made another 360 000 dollars. So let's tax it, and let's use it to keep our people alive.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Die Angst deutscher Regierungsvertreter, sich mit den Energiekonzernen anzulegen, ist wirklich unfassbar. In Deutschland lagen im September die Übergewinne aus dem Verkauf von Diesel und Benzin bei 46 Millionen Euro täglich – Geld, das die Konzerne auf dem Rücken der arbeitenden Bevölkerung und der Familien machen. Der deutsche Finanzminister Klingbeil hat jetzt die Forderung nach einer Übergewinnsteuer bei den Linken abgeschrieben. Das finde ich gut, die Krisenprofiteure zur Kasse zu bitten, damit das Leben für die Menschen bezahlbar wird. Ich finde das absolut richtig. Also ran an die Energiemultis und runter mit den Energiepreisen, ran an die großen Rüstungskonzerne, die dank Aufrüstung und Krieg in Geld schwimmen.

2022, während der letzten großen Energiekrise, hat Deutschland 2,5 Milliarden Euro von den Extraprofiten der Konzerne einkassiert. Noch jetzt bleiben Kanzler Merz und sein Finanzminister tatenlos und lassen die Leute gnadenlos im Stich. Dabei – haben wir heute auch gehört – sind die rechtlichen Voraussetzungen für die Besteuerung der Krisengewinne der großen Konzerne schon längst gegeben. Aber Lars Klingbeil kann sich gegenüber Merz und den Marktfetischisten von der Union natürlich nicht durchsetzen. Die führen lieber einen sogenannten Tankrabatt ein, der den Leuten nicht wirklich hilft und die Extragewinne der Konzerne unangetastet lässt. Wieder scheitert die Große Koalition an sich selbst, wieder liefert sie nicht. Schluss mit diesem Rumgestümper! Schluss mit dieser organisierten Verantwortungslosigkeit! Wir brauchen eine Übergewinnsteuer – jetzt. Die Energiepreise müssen jetzt runter.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, io me lo immagino il piacere che ha provato la sinistra nel comporre il titolo di questo dibattito. C'erano le parole e le espressioni che ama: "tasse alle imprese". Noi invece amiamo qualcos'altro, cerchiamo di aiutare le imprese a fare il loro lavoro, a produrre occupazione, a cercare di evitare tutte le storture che nel corso della scorsa legislatura questo Parlamento ha imposto.

Non ha senso imporre nuove tasse alle imprese, perché sottrarremmo loro liquidità. Non ha senso continuare ad immaginare un ETS come è stato costruito in questo Parlamento. I danni che sta facendo questo tipo di tassazione sono inenarrabili nei confronti delle imprese. Inoltre, sta costringendo molte di queste aziende a doversi delocalizzare. C'è una deindustrializzazione diffusa, una delocalizzazione, purtroppo, delle emissioni e del lavoro fuori dall'Unione europea.

Allora dobbiamo essere consapevoli che l'ETS sta danneggiando il tessuto produttivo europeo e dobbiamo essere intenzionati a modificarlo. Dobbiamo essere intenzionati a cambiarne gli standard. Questa è la vera battaglia, questo è il dibattito che vorremmo affrontare seriamente, anziché immaginare nuove tasse da imporre a coloro che non fanno altro che produrre posti di lavoro.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Colegas, Senhor Comissário, sejamos claros, a guerra no Médio Oriente é obra de Trump e Netanyahu, mas quem paga é o cidadão comum. Enquanto famílias e pequenas empresas fazem um esforço extra para atestar o depósito, às empresas petrolíferas saiu o Euromilhões. As oito maiores empresas do setor tiveram lucros extraordinários de mais de 7 mil milhões apenas no primeiro semestre deste ano. A portuguesa Galp, só na primeira metade deste ano, já lucrou quase o dobro do valor total de 2021. É nosso dever, a nível europeu, chamar estas empresas a contribuir para apoiar as pessoas. E isso significa tributar de forma pesada lucros extraordinários.

Senhor Comissário, não podem ser sempre os mesmos a pagar a fatura. E lamento aqui os jogos do Partido Social Democrata, porque enquanto em casa o governo anuncia uma taxa de solidariedade, aqui os seus deputados votam e posicionam‑se contra. Como defensor de uma economia de mercado, valorize o mérito, Senhor Comissário, só não há mérito quando as receitas sobem em flecha por causa de guerras. Se queremos um mundo de paz, não podemos normalizar dividendos de guerra.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, un impôt sur les bénéfices exceptionnels des pollueurs: le mot est séduisant, la mesure est illusoire. Taxer des entreprises capables de délocaliser leurs capitaux, leurs sièges et leurs emplois en quelques mois, ce n'est pas faire payer les pollueurs, c'est faire fuir les contribuables. Et au bout du compte, la facture retombe toujours sur les mêmes: les ménages, les retraités et nos entreprises.

Oui, en temps de crise, chacun doit prendre sa part de l'effort collectif, et les grands groupes de l'énergie ne font pas exception. Moralement, cela va de soi. Mais ne nous trompons pas de combat, ce n'est pas avec un impôt de plus que nos concitoyens retrouveront du pouvoir d'achat. La vraie solution, nous la connaissons depuis longtemps: baisser les taxes qui pèsent sur l'énergie, renégocier les traités – ce marché européen absurde qui indexe le prix de notre électricité sur celui du gaz –, rendre aux États la liberté de baisser leurs taxes sans demander la permission de Bruxelles.
Moins d'impôts, plus de liberté, plus de souveraineté, voilà comment on protège à la fois la santé des Français et des Européens, et leur portefeuille.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, mentre famiglie e imprese cercano di resistere al caro energia, da quest'Aula arriva sempre la stessa risposta: una nuova tassa. Ma se chiediamo alle compagnie di assumersi una responsabilità, dobbiamo assumerci anche la nostra.

Non possiamo chiedere di contenere i prezzi, mentre continuiamo a imporre obblighi che rendono più costoso produrre in Europa. Non possiamo invocare sacrifici e lasciare intatte le scelte che aggravano le difficoltà di chi lavora. Dobbiamo rivedere radicalmente l'ETS e gli obblighi insostenibili del Green Deal, prima che l'ostinazione nel difenderli mandi sul lastrico l'economia europea.

Nessun obiettivo politico giustifica l'indifferenza davanti a imprese che chiudono e posti di lavoro che si perdono. Per abbassare le bollette dobbiamo riconquistare autonomia energetica, produrre di più e dipendere meno dall'estero. E per questo servono tutte le fonti, dalle rinnovabili al nucleare, fino alle fossili. Basta demonizzarle per ideologia e rinunciare agli strumenti che possono garantire energia accessibile.

E, soprattutto, non accettiamo lezioni sull'ambiente da chi considera una fabbrica chiusa un successo della transizione. Se produzione ed emissioni si trasferiscono altrove, l'Europa perde lavoro e non salviamo neanche il pianeta.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, 'I prefer the world of disruption to the peaceful world. And this disruption gives us plenty of opportunities.' This is a quote from the CEO of TotalEnergies in yesterday's newspaper, and I think it's very difficult to find one single European citizen who could agree with this cynical philosophy.

These so-called 'opportunities', and consequently the super-profits, are not the result of some brilliant entrepreneurship – it is pure luck to them. And I am not against pure luck myself, but the super-profits are at the expense of people, businesses and public finances.
So yes, let's use these super-profits made by the oil giants to invest it in compensation for poor people and to finally become energy independent in Europe.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Ich habe mich heute entschlossen, nicht über Prozentpunkte und Milliardengewinne zu reden, sondern über die Realität, die dahintersteht. Stellen Sie sich eine ältere Dame vor. Nennen wir sie Renata. Sie sitzt im Winter in ihrer Wohnung. Ihre Hände sind kalt. Sie könnte die Heizung aufdrehen, aber sie hat Angst vor der Rechnung. Während ihre Heizung kalt bleibt, verkünden fossile Konzerne auf ihren Aktionärsversammlungen Milliardengewinne.

Das ist eine politische Entscheidung, denn diese Krise hat Gewinner und Verlierer. Gewinnen tun die fossilen Konzerne. Verlieren – verlieren tun wir alle. Wir bezahlen die höheren Rechnungen. Wir leiden unter der Klimakrise, und wir sind abhängig. Aber wir könnten das richten, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, mit einer Übergewinnsteuer, mit erneuerbaren Energien und mit Mut, damit die Energierechnung von Renata billiger wird. Also entscheiden wir uns. Stehen wir auf der Seite von Renata, stehen wir auf der Seite von denen, die gerade verlieren, oder von denen, die unsere Zukunft zerstören und damit Gewinne machen?

paragraphs.text: Mr President, more and more people no longer have enough money to cover the cost of their everyday life.

Once again, also ordinary Europeans are paying the bill for the United States' actions. Our dependence on fossil fuels and our dependence on the US, Russia and the Middle East has driven up the cost of transportation, food and heating homes.

Oil companies are taking advantage of this situation, reaping billions in extra profits. And normal, hard-working people are paying the price: first through higher energy bills and then as victims of climate crisis, while the wealthiest profit from the situation.

The Commission must immediately present a proposal for an EU-wide tax on unfair windfall profits. Revenue from this tax must be used to help people in acute need and to speed up the green transition so that we can be independent and end poverty.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, kolegyně, kolegové, je třeba urychleně zdanit mimořádné zisky nadnárodních korporací – a nejenom těch energetických a ropných. A hlavně tak, aby to zase neobešly jako minule. Nicméně proč tady tu debatu vůbec vedeme? Současná energetická krize je vyvolávána geopolitickým konflikty, které vedou naši tzv. spojenci a současná politika Evropské unie je dále prohlubuje. Je to krize, kterou si EU způsobila sama. Sama se odstřihla od levných energií, sama si naordinovala Green Deal, emisní povolenky a sama EU poslušně panáčkuje před Spojenými státy. Pouze tak sklízíme plody politiky předsedkyně von den Leyenové a její pravé ruky Kallasové. Výnos těchto daní musí jít lidem a snížit účty domácnostem. Už je načase zastavit šmelení s elektřinou na Lipské burze a říct stačilo emisním povolenkám pro domácnosti. Není možné podporovat z těchto peněz pouze tzv. obnovitelné, nebo možná spíš občasné zdroje energie. Léta vám tady říkám, že pro země jako Česká republika totiž nejsou řešením. Je naopak nutné podpořit výstavbu konvenčních zdrojů, které udrží Evropu v zimě v teple za rozumné peníze, jako jsou například jaderné elektrárny.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, while families across Europe will soon have to choose between heating and eating or simply putting on an extra sweater, big fossil fuel companies are making extra profits – profits made not through innovation, but through crisis. And who pays? Ordinary people.
They pay through higher energy bills, polluted air, floods, fires and heatwaves. This is not just unfair; it is unsustainable.

I therefore call for a tax on the extraordinary profits of polluters done at European level. Without it, we risk fragmentation of the single market and profit shifting. We need to raise revenue that can be used to lower the bills for our households, and we need it now.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, notre addiction au gaz et au pétrole est un désastre climatique, sanitaire, social, géopolitique. Ce désastre, les citoyens en souffrent, mais les multinationales des fossiles en vivent. Il y a ceux qui meurent pendant les canicules, ceux qui morflent chaque fois qu'ils font le plein, et il y a ceux qui s'enrichissent. TotalEnergies a gagné 11 milliards d'euros au premier semestre 2026, simplement grâce à la guerre en Iran. C'est la définition même des superprofits.

Six gouvernements ont demandé à taxer ces superprofits: l'Allemagne, l'Italie, l'Espagne, le Portugal, la Pologne, l'Autriche. Où est la France? La France n'a pas signé et c'est une honte. Chez nous, dans notre gouvernement, un ministre déclare qu'il ne veut pas embêter Total. Eh bien, nous, nous avons envie d'aider ceux qui ne peuvent plus se chauffer, ceux qui n'arrivent plus à boucler leurs fins de mois. Et si pour ça il faut embêter Total, et bien nous embêterons Total. Nous sommes les élus du peuple, pas des actionnaires de TotalEnergies. Et nous n'avons peur d'embêter personne quand il s'agit de défendre l'intérêt général.

Ce désastre, les citoyens en souffrent, mais les multinationales des fossiles en vivent. Il y a ceux qui meurent pendant les canicules, ceux qui morflent chaque fois qu'ils font le plein, et il y a ceux qui s'enrichissent. TotalEnergies a gagné 11 milliards d'euros au premier semestre 2026, simplement grâce à la guerre en Iran. C'est la définition même des superprofits.

Six gouvernements ont demandé à taxer ces superprofits: l'Allemagne, l'Italie, l'Espagne, le Portugal, la Pologne, l'Autriche. Où est la France? La France n'a pas signé et c'est une honte. Chez nous, dans notre gouvernement, un ministre déclare qu'il ne veut pas embêter Total. Eh bien, nous, nous avons envie d'aider ceux qui ne peuvent plus se chauffer, ceux qui n'arrivent plus à boucler leurs fins de mois. Et si pour ça il faut embêter Total, et bien nous embêterons Total. Nous sommes les élus du peuple, pas des actionnaires de TotalEnergies. Et nous n'avons peur d'embêter personne quand il s'agit de défendre l'intérêt général.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, suprataxarea companiilor europene este apoteoza delirului progresismului verde. Mâine-poimâine vor vrea taxă și pe respirația umană, pentru că reduce oxigenul din atmosferă.

Reality check, economia europeană este aproape de colaps. Avem inflație galopantă, calitatea vieții europenilor a scăzut față de generația precedentă. Și ce propun verzii și stângiștii? Taxe, taxe și iar taxe. Este iluzia banilor gratis care sunt de fapt banii celor care inovează și produc. Se dorește uciderea cu orice preț a tot ce a mai rămas din industria UE. Este fix cum spunea Reagan: „Dacă se mișcă, taxează-l. Dacă continuă să se miște, reglementează-l. Iar dacă nu se mai mișcă, subvenționează-l”. Acesta este drumul spre iadul economiei europene lăsate în urmă în competiția globală cu America și China.

Eu aș vrea să ne întâlnim măcar o dată în acest forum și să discutăm cum sprijină UE statele membre să scadă taxarea companiilor, cum facem să nu mai fim în situația nebunească de acum, cu prețul gazelor de 7 ori mai mare în Uniunea Europeană decât SUA sau cu prețul combustibililor dublu.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, la crise du prix du carburant, ce n'est pas une crise de l'énergie, c'est une nouvelle crise de l'énergie fossile. C'est avant tout la responsabilité des conservateurs qui nous empêchent de sortir de nos dépendances. Cette crise le montre une fois de plus: les climatosceptiques sont les fossoyeurs du pouvoir d'achat.

Mais c'est aussi une crise du marché. Le droit européen de la concurrence et la lutte contre les abus de position dominante sont des fondements de notre union. Quand le marché fonctionne, laissons-le fonctionner. Mais quand la crise est l'occasion, pour ceux qui bénéficient d'une rente de position, de s'enrichir sans rien faire au détriment des citoyens et des entreprises, il faut agir. Nous devons capter une partie de cette rente de crise.

Ce n'est pas une question idéologique, c'est une question de fonctionnement de marché. L'Allemagne, l'Espagne, l'Italie, la Pologne, le Portugal et l'Autriche nous demandent d'avancer. Alors avançons et faisons-le au niveau européen.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Fast 26 Milliarden Euro – so viele Profite haben die großen fossilen Energiekonzerne in den letzten drei Monaten gemacht. Das ist eine extrem hohe Summe. Und die Profite der Energiekonzerne? Ja, das sind die hohen Rechnungen für unsere Bürgerinnen und Bürger an den Tankstellen, in den Wohnzimmern, wenn sie den Blick in die letzte Energiekostenabrechnung werfen.

Und ich finde es wirklich unfassbar, dass wir es bisher nicht geschafft haben, unsere Bürgerinnen und Bürger gegen diese Profitgier der großen Konzerne zu schützen. Ich finde es unfassbar, dass die EU-Kommission, obwohl es inzwischen eine Initiative von sechs Mitgliedstaaten gibt, nach wie vor nicht handelt. Ich will hier einmal ganz deutlich sagen: Verstecken Sie sich nicht hinter technokratischen Argumenten. Es gibt Modelle, wie wir europaweit die großen Profite besteuern können. Es gibt Modelle, wie wir feststellen, was ein Übergewinn ist. Wir haben es vor einigen Jahren schon gemacht.

Woran scheitert es? An dem politischen Willen von zu vielen Abgeordneten in der EVP-Fraktion, die auch gestern unseren Antrag abgelehnt haben, und von zu vielen Mitgliedstaaten und EU-Kommissaren. Handeln Sie jetzt!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, as a direct result of President Trump's idiotic and illegal war in Iran, anxiety is growing in many homes as we head into the winter. Will it be another year of choosing between heating and eating?
Households are at their limit, yet fossil fuel companies are raking it in: billions of windfall profits, cashing in on the crisis.
There is a way to shift the balance back: tax these super profits. We have done it before as the EU. But, if the EU won't act, Member States can, and we have just had that confirmed once again.

For months we have been calling for the Irish Government to act: introduce a windfall tax on fossil fuel super-profits. We were told we had to wait for the EU to act. Well, Minister Byrne, you've heard it loud and clear here today. There is no hiding behind the EU. The ball has, and always will be, in the government's court. Tax the mega-polluters and put the profits back into people's pockets.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, yo estoy encantado con este debate. Oye, y animo a los verdes, que cuantos más debates de estos presenten, mejor, porque así se están hundiendo todos los Gobiernos de izquierda de Europa.

¡Dejen ya! ¿No tienen una solución un poquito más imaginativa que subir los impuestos? ¿No tienen alguna otra solución para acabar con los especuladores —para controlar todo esto, claro; estamos todos de acuerdo— y con los que abusan del mercado? Pero ¿es que no pueden proponer otra cosa que no sea subir impuestos? ¿Ustedes pisan la calle? ¿Ustedes están viendo las colas en las gasolineras por buscar precios mejores?, ¿a los agricultores y a los pescadores que están en estos momentos sufriendo todo este tipo de políticas de una antigua ideología absolutamente obsoleta en esta Unión Europea?

Adáptense a la nueva realidad. Ni siquiera son capaces de formular una propuesta coherente. ¿Cómo pretenden que lo entiendan los ciudadanos? Los europeos no necesitan más eslóganes engañosos; necesitan energía asequible, seguridad de suministro y una industria que no huya de Europa. A ver si pueden ayudar un poco con eso. Menos impuestos ideológicos y más sentido común.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, la actual crisis fósil de precios no ha caído del cielo. Miren, esta es la secuencia: Trump y Netanyahu provocan una guerra ilegal en Irak que iba a durar dos semanas y ya vamos para ocho meses, la extrema derecha y la derecha apoyan esta guerra y lo que tenemos es precios elevados de gasolina, diésel y electricidad. Se produce, al mismo tiempo, un atraco a los bolsillos europeos —que ya asciende a 100 000 millones de euros— y, ahora, las familias y las empresas pagan y unas pocas compañías se forran.

Y claro, la ultraderecha y la derecha no quieren hablar de ello —porque saben que son culpables de esta situación— ni tampoco de las soluciones: ni a medio y largo plazo —la energía limpia, autóctona y soberana— ni a corto plazo —poner impuestos a los disparatados beneficios extraordinarios de la industria fósil—. Siempre igual: cada vez que hay que aliviar la carga de los ciudadanos —como ocurre en España— la derecha apoya los fondos buitre y los desahucios de señoras mayores.
Miren, la competitividad y la soberanía europea van en sentido contrario al de Donald Trump. A ver si se enteran, a ver si se enteran.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Commissioner and the Council, first of all, I think that every idea that is proposed by the Greens or Socialists is ridiculous. And I think two years ago, the voters showed very clearly what they think about you, because the Greens were the biggest losers here in the European Parliament. But after all, if there are bigger and bigger problems in the economy because of the overregulation, taxation and so on, the only solution the Greens can propose is, 'We need a new tax. We need a new enemy.'

I was checking during the debate the backgrounds of most speakers. They have never ever been working in the private sector. They haven't produced anything in their life. The main speaker, the French MEP from the Greens, who was the first speaker, she started her career when she was 18 as a young activist in the Greens. Perfect career. But if you really care about the average people in European countries – and you talk about the elderly people – the taxpayers who are actually company owners producing works, I just have to remind you that all of us here are earning almost EUR 15 000 per month, together with all the daily allowances, and so on. If you really care about those average people, actually you are super rich. And coming here, never ever been working in the private sector, never done anything useful in their life, and saying, 'No, but the company owners. They are bad. We have to punish them.' Come on! Go to work.

Na Slovensku máme rafinériu Slovnaft, ktorá aj vďaka európskej výnimke stále môže spracúvať ruskú ropu. A máme zákony, ktoré hovoria, že sa o nadmerné zisky musí podeliť so štátom. No lenže neplatí nič a slovenská vláda mlčí a nič s tým nerobí. Kým od ľudí vie Robert Fico vybrať každé euro, pri stovkách miliónov z jednej z najväčších a najziskovejších firiem na Slovensku zrazu roky čaká. Takto ochrana ľudí pred dôsledkami energetickej krízy naozaj vyzerať nemôže. Ak na energetickej kríze niekto mimoriadne zarobí, ľudia z toho musia mať svoj podiel. A úlohou vlády je túto daň vybrať a nie sa prizerať, ako sa jej veľká firma účtovnými trikmi vyhýba. Áno, pri nadmerných ziskoch potrebujeme konať ako Európa. Ale konať musia v prvom rade členské štáty.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Den rikaste promillen i Sverige släpper ut i genomsnitt 198 ton koldioxid per år. För vanlig svensk skulle det ta 30 år att komma upp i samma nivå. Det är orimligt. Det är orimligt och det är orättvist att några få miljardärer och megaföretag står för enorma utsläpp, samtidigt som du betalar kostnaden för den ökade klimatkrisen i form av dyrare elräkningar, förorenad luft och vatten som det inte går att bada i.

Det är hög tid att de som släpper ut mest också ska ta störst ansvar. På så sätt kan vi finansiera en fungerande järnväg, bättre vård och billigare kollektivtrafik och stöd till de mest utsatta. Det är dags att räkningen skickas till dem som står för de stora utsläppen.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, Europe is facing a climate crisis, an energy crisis and a social crisis. We cannot address one while ignoring the others.

That's why we need a fair and effective tax on the super-profits of major polluters. When energy prices rise, families should not be forced to choose between heating their homes and paying their bills, while fossil fuel companies make extraordinary profits.

This Parliament has already recognised that those benefiting from windfall profits should contribute to addressing the consequences of the energy crisis. The revenues from such a tax should go where they are most needed: protecting vulnerable households, tackling energy poverty, improving energy efficiency and investing in affordable renewable energy. That is exactly what a socially just green deal should look like.
So let us make the principle clear: those who have profited most from pollution should contribute most to ending our dependence on it. And no European should be left behind in the transition.

Koncerny paliwowe zarobiły na kryzysie w Zatoce krocie. Więc co zrobiliśmy? Opodatkowaliśmy ich nadzwyczajne zyski do 60% i Polacy tankują taniej z dnia na dzień o ponad złotówkę na każdym litrze.
Czy było łatwo? Oczywiście, że nie. Zakochana w wielkich koncernach prawica rzucała nam kłody pod nogi. Prezydent wetował, blokował, straszył, odwlekał, a ceny na stacjach rosły.

Ale my wiemy, po czyjej stronie stoimy. My stoimy po stronie Polaków. Nie miliarderów, nie korporacji, ale Polaków. Zabraliśmy koncernom, daliśmy Polakom. Kierowcom ciężarówek, rolnikom, rodzinom. I niech Europa bierze przykład z Polski.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Was sind Übergewinne? Das sind Profite ohne Leistung. Die sind möglich gemacht durch Kriege, durch Krisen. Und deshalb schnalzen unsere Stromrechnungen, unsere Gasrechnungen, unsere Energierechnungen in die Höhe. Die fossilen Konzerne befeuern die Klimakrise und verdienen auch noch daran, wenn Europa brennt. Und die Löscharbeiten, die bezahlen wir alle. Familien müssen zwischen Heizen und Essen entscheiden, während Energiekonzerne Gewinne einstreichen – gewaltige Gewinne.

Sehr geehrte Vertreter der EVP, der Rechten in diesem Hause! Wollen Sie das, dass nicht durch Innovation, nicht durch Investitionen, nicht durch Leistung, sondern durch Krisen diese riesengroßen Gewinne erzielt werden? Und deshalb brauchen wir eine dauerhafte Übergewinnsteuer, weil wir das alles nicht wollen. Wenn – und deshalb wende ich mich jetzt an Sie, Herr Jørgensen, und natürlich auch an den Rat, Mister Byrne – wir in der Europäischen Union gemeinsam handeln, dann sind wir immer stärker. Wenn das einige wenige Mitgliedstaaten machen, dann ist das gut, dann ist das super. Aber das ist viel zu wenig. Und deshalb sollten wir gemeinsam handeln. Deshalb sollte die Kommission hier ganz besonders engagiert sein, besonders phantasievoll. Wir haben die Argumente gehört der Gegenseite. Die sind hanebüchen. Wir müssen handeln. Wir brauchen eine Übergewinnsteuer.

paragraphs.text: Dit is mijn eerste toespraak in dit Parlement. Ik zal hier staan in solidariteit. Ik zal me uitspreken voor mensen, voor gezondheid en tegen oneerlijke verdeling van welvaart en lasten.

De wereld staat in brand. Ons water en onze lucht zijn vies en ongezond en de grote vervuilers vullen hun zakken met geld. Veel geld. Geld dat verdiend wordt dankzij de arbeid van mensen. Zij krijgen daar een torenhoge energierekening en een ongezonde leefomgeving voor terug.

Door de hoge energieprijzen maakten de acht grootste Europese oliebedrijven tijdens de eerste maanden van de illegale oorlog tussen de Verenigde Staten en Iran zo’n 7,5 miljard EUR aan extra winsten, bovenop de grote winst die ze al maakten. De energierekening voor de mensen in Nederland en in Europa stijgt nu al met zo’n 500 EUR per jaar en de winter moet nog beginnen. De fossiele industrie profiteert en moet dus bijdragen.

paragraphs.text: Hr. Formand! Millioner af almindelige mennesker over hele Europa frygter for fremtiden. Frygter for ikke at have råd til at varme deres hus denne vinter eller ikke have råd til medicin og mad til dem og deres børn.

Vi har været igennem en sommer, der var så varm, at flere mennesker end nogen sinde før døde af varmen i Europa. Samtidig høster de store energiselskaber profitter som aldrig før. Profitter på at gøre situationen værre.

Det må stoppe, og en af de ting, vi kan gøre, er en ekstra profit, en ekstra skat på deres overnormale profiler, ligesom vi gjorde så sent som i 2022. En skat, der kan bruges på klimatiltag og på at forbedre situationen. På at gøre mad og energi billigere. Ikke for store virksomheder, men for helt almindelige mennesker. Det er det mindste, vi kan gøre.

paragraphs.text: Г-н председател, темата за данък свръх печалба е много деликатна. Трябва много да се внимава с такива идеи, защото предприемачите инвестират, поемат риск, развиват бизнес модели и в крайна сметка искат да печелят. И да, искат да печелят много, да реинвестират. Така работи бизнесът, така се създава богатството.

Рискуваме с този дебат, с популизма в него, да изпаднем в положението на българското правителство, което предлага данък свръх печалба за малки фирми с 5 магазина например, но не предлага данък свръх печалба за огромна петролна рафинерия. И когато говорим за горивата, трябва да признаем, че това е друг случай. Това е различен казус, защото в днешния свят горивата не са стока, а геополитическо оръжие. Но и тук трябва да мислим за мерки за свиване на печалбата и намаляване на цената преди да мислим за увеличаване на данъка, защото свиването на цената има антиинфлационен ефект, докато увеличаването на данъка лесно увеличава инфлацията.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, mentre milioni di famiglie faticano a pagare le bollette e a fare il pieno di benzina, i colossi dell'energia continuano ad accumulare miliardi di extraprofitti immorali. E questa, guardate, non è crescita. Questa è una vera e propria ingiustizia sociale, ed è per questo che serve un'azione coraggiosa da parte dell'Europa.

Ma la responsabilità è anche degli Stati nazionali, perché la Commissione europea è stata chiara e ha detto praticamente che i governi possono agire ora. Eppure, in Italia, il governo di Giorgia Meloni non ha fatto nulla. Giorgia Meloni ha preferito lasciare intatto il tesoretto delle multinazionali per non disturbare le grandi lobby, mentre il prezzo del gasolio continua ad aumentare.

Proprio ieri, qui, la maggioranza del governo Meloni, assieme a tutte le destre, ha bocciato una proposta dei Socialisti e Democratici per tassare gli extraprofitti. Questo è la dimostrazione che la destra non è mai sociale. La destra sta sempre con i poteri forti. Infatti, in Italia, in questi anni, il governo Meloni è stato forte con i deboli e purtroppo debolissimo con i forti.
Allora, noi chiediamo che ogni euro recuperato dagli extraprofitti venga investito per aiutare famiglie e imprese. Ma non domani, questo bisogna farlo subito.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, pendant des années, nous n'avons pas pris suffisamment au sérieux les politiques environnementales. Aujourd'hui, nous subissons les conséquences. La pollution environnementale et le changement climatique nuisent à notre santé d'une manière que nous ne pouvons plus ignorer. Ils augmentent les risques de maladies, ils mettent des vies en danger.

Notre dépendance aux énergies fossiles a également comme conséquence une hausse des factures d'énergie, une augmentation du coût de la vie et une précarité énergétique. Pourtant les ultra-riches continuent à polluer alors que nous tous, nous payons le prix. C'est tout simplement inacceptable.

Taxer les surprofits n'est pas seulement une nécessité environnementale, c'est une question de justice sociale. Et avec cet argent, nous pourrions réduire les factures d'énergie, investir dans des énergies propres et renouvelables et protéger la santé de nos citoyens.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, ¿usted ha visto las movilizaciones por la vivienda en mi país? ¿Ha visto las acampadas, las movilizaciones masivas? ¿Ha visto a los jóvenes estudiantes franceses movilizarse?

Yo creo que ustedes pensaban que la gente trabajadora iba a tragar, tragar y tragar —y si no, que con unos cuantos palos de la policía iba a servir— a pesar de que ustedes gobiernen cada vez más en contra de sus intereses. ¿Pensaban que iban a aceptar que unas energéticas se aprovechen de las guerras ilegales que ustedes apoyan para subir la factura de la luz, subir el precio de la gasolina y subir el coste de la vida con unos beneficios extraordinarios? ¿Que iban a aceptar que unos pocos fondos buitre acaparen cada vez más viviendas vacías para que solo les quede vivir debajo de un puente? ¿O que iban a aceptar, por ejemplo, que se privaticen las pensiones —que es lo que propone VOX en mi país—, que otra vez hagan negocio unos buitres o que les roben el tiempo para estar con sus familias a cambio de unos salarios que son una miseria y que no dan para el coste de la vida?

Yo creo que no, que los pueblos, aunque tarden un poco más, al final despiertan, y los pueblos de Europa están despertando y no van a aguantar. No van a tolerar que ustedes sigan gobernando en contra de sus intereses y a favor de unos buitres.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Herr Kommissar, Herr Minister! An jeder Tankstelle in Europa sieht man gerade, wer diese Krise zahlt und wer daran verdient. Familien müssen jeden Euro umdrehen. Handwerksbetriebe können ihre Rechnungen nicht mehr zahlen. Und, liebe Kollegen von der Linken, wenn Sie dann sagen: „Ja, der Tankrabatt in Deutschland, der bringt ja gar nichts“, ich glaube, dann haben Sie wirklich nicht im Blick, wie knapp es bei einigen in der Kasse ist.

Aber wer verdient denn daran, an diesem Krieg? Wer verdient denn an der Knappheit von Öl? Es sind die Ölkonzerne. Ja, das Angebot ist verknappt. Aber die Preisanstiege, die gehen doch weit darüber hinaus. Das hat doch damit nichts mehr zu tun. Das ist viel, viel höher gestiegen. Es sind da Übergewinne entstanden, und wir kennen das Phänomen. Wir kennen es von 2022/2023. Damals hat Europa einen Solidaritätsbeitrag geleistet. Das haben wir alle gemeinsam gemacht, und das hat auch geholfen. Und das hat geholfen, um auch die Menschen zu entlasten. Und wenn die Kollegen von der EVP hier sagen: „Ja, aber das senkt ja keine einzige Energierechnung“ – natürlich tut es das. Wenn man das zugunsten der Menschen umverteilt, dann können diese Mehreinnahmen eben bei den Menschen ankommen. Deswegen brauchen wir eine gemeinsame Lösung. Herr Kommissar, ich erwarte auch von der Kommission, dass sie da jetzt endlich einen Vorschlag macht. Wir haben die Frage von sechs nationalen Finanzministern auf dem Tisch. Und wir brauchen eine gemeinsame Lösung wie 2023. Das können wir wieder. Wir können den Menschen helfen.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la vostra Europa sta scaricando la crisi del petrolio sulla pelle delle persone.

In Italia, 5,3 milioni di cittadini vivono in povertà energetica. Intanto, l'azienda Eni potrebbe fare addirittura quattro miliardi e mezzo di profitti, extraprofitti. Mentre le persone comuni dovranno presto scegliere tra scaldarsi e mangiare, Eni guadagna miliardi grazie alla crisi energetica. Sono extraprofitti, guadagni extra dovuti solo alla crisi e all'aumento dei prezzi.

E il governo Meloni che cosa fa? Invece di tassarli, fa propaganda. Eni annuncia uno sconto sulle bollette di 200 euro all'anno, ma la notte prima alza i prezzi e lo sconto lo applica sul prezzo già gonfiato. Alle famiglie alla fine resteranno 2 euro di risparmio l'anno: una vergogna! E sui carburanti, lo stesso gioco.

Non possiamo lasciare le multinazionali arricchirsi e i cittadini impoverirsi. Chiediamo alla Commissione e agli Stati membri una tassa europea sugli extraprofitti delle aziende fossili: 161 miliardi accumulati da marzo. Questa è la nostra Europa: chi inquina e guadagna sulla crisi energetica deve pagare.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Wir sprechen über eine Übergewinnsteuer für Klimazerstörer, was ein unterstützenswertes Anliegen ist. Und das hängt ja von der konkreten Ausgestaltung ab, ob es überhaupt einen Beitrag, einen nennenswerten Beitrag geben kann dabei, um die Klimakatastrophe aufzuhalten. Nichtsdestotrotz, unterstützenswert!

Was mich aber massiv stört, ist, dass der Fokus auf dem Energiesektor liegt. Der Bereich Landwirtschaft und Lebensmittelerzeugung wird leider fast immer außer Betracht gelassen, was daran liegt, dass es immer heißt: 10 bis 15 Prozent macht dieser Bereich lediglich aus. Das stimmt aber nicht. Es ist rund ein Drittel, denn man muss es richtig berechnen. Wenn man das tut, kommt man eben auf ein Drittel, wenn man zum Beispiel mit in Betracht zieht, dass der Regenwald gerodet wird für Weiden und für Futtermittelimporte. Der Europäische Wirtschafts- und Sozialausschuss hat auch ausdrücklich bestätigt, dass in dem Bereich eine sehr hohe Konzentration vorliegt und Übergewinne vorhanden sind. Das heißt, wir haben die Fakten auf dem Tisch liegen und sollten hier auch handeln.

In einer Welt, in der hauptberuflich kommerziell mit Klimazerstörung und Tierausbeutung Geld verdient wird, während die Tierschützer und Umweltschützer ehrenamtlich arbeiten, ihr Bestes tun, brauchen wir nicht nur die Übergewinnsteuer, sondern auch sofort wirksame, effektive Maßnahmen, um Klimazerstörung, Umweltzerstörung und Tierleid aufzuhalten. Ich hoffe, da kommen wir in den nächsten Jahren voran.

In einer Welt, in der hauptberuflich kommerziell mit Klimazerstörung und Tierausbeutung Geld verdient wird, während die Tierschützer und Umweltschützer ehrenamtlich arbeiten, ihr Bestes tun, brauchen wir nicht nur die Übergewinnsteuer, sondern auch sofort wirksame, effektive Maßnahmen, um Klimazerstörung, Umweltzerstörung und Tierleid aufzuhalten. Ich hoffe, da kommen wir in den nächsten Jahren voran.

Var läggs bördorna? Var hamnar vinsterna? Vanliga löntagare får betala mer för att värma sina hem, köra till jobbet, få vardagen att gå ihop. Då gröper bolagen guld med soppslev för att vi sitter i ett beroende av fossila bränslen.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, Europe will pay hundreds of billions of euros more this year for its addiction to fossil fuels – and apart from some luscious bonuses for all executives and a bit of investment in some football clubs probably – most of that cash will flow out of our continent. When desperate European governments subsidise fuel prices at the pump with money they don't have, we can borrow it back at ever-higher interest rates, for which our taxpayers will pay with yet more suffering.

If it sounds like a scenario for a movie about drug addicts and their dealers, that's because it is. So let's break that vicious circle, colleagues: rather than make our people pay the speculators, let the speculators pay to help our people and let's invest in a way out. The transition that Mario Draghi proposes actually costs less than what we pay today for our oil and gas. If you don't want to call it green, maybe just call it rehab or call it common sense.

I would hope that the Commission would lead the way a bit more than it does today, because leaving it to the Member States apparently does not lead to common sense all over Europe, and that is what we need.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, six pays, comme vous le savez, appellent à la taxation des superprofits. Ce sont des pays de couleurs différentes, politiquement.

Il y a un pays qui s'oppose, et ce pays s'appelle la France. Et donc j'ai une question: est-ce que la France a sincèrement les moyens, aujourd'hui, budgétaires – regardez les spreads encore aujourd'hui – de se passer de revenus fiscaux? Je ne le crois pas. Donc j'aimerais une explication sur ce point.

Ensuite, on nous explique que la taxation des superprofits, ça ne marche pas très bien en France. Je tiens à rassurer le gouvernement français: on peut tout à fait travailler sur l'assiette, s'il y a besoin. C'est une question technique.

Ensuite, on nous dit «mais regardez, si on taxe Total» – parce que c'est ça en réalité le sujet – «si on taxe Total, ils vont moins innover». Je tiens à rassurer, là aussi, le gouvernement français: Total a d'ores et déjà décidé de faire des rachats d'actions. Donc je pense qu'ils ont largement de quoi faire.

Donc il y a deux solutions: soit on taxe les superprofits, soit Total donne un prix préférentiel à l'ensemble des Européens, à l'ensemble des distributeurs. Je n'ai pas l'impression que ce soit leur direction artistique du moment. En tout cas, la France doit clarifier immédiatement sa position car l'Europe la regarde.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Honourable Members, Member States are best placed to tax windfall profits based on the domestic specificity of their own energy sector and local operators. The Commission will respect Member States' decisions if they take recourse to windfall taxes. We stand ready to support Member States with the best practices on national measures. Speaking more broadly, it is vital that all of our policies and tax systems at European and national levels support low‑carbon investment so that we can reach our climate commitments for 2040 and 2050. This strategy will not only contribute to mitigating climate change globally, it will also help us reduce our dependence on imported fossil fuels. Ultimately, this will lower energy costs and increase security of energy supply.

Apart from the revenue side, we should also have a look at public expenditure in this debate. The Commission recently published a fitness check of the 'polluter pays' principle in EU policies. There is scope for improvement. Applying this principle helps to achieve the EU's climate and environmental goals more efficiently. Environmentally harmful subsidies are particularly relevant, as they send the wrong incentive to polluters. This is also reflected in the European Semester cycle, where country‑specific recommendations provide an opportunity to put forward targeted reforms focused on addressing environmentally harmful subsidies. For example, in 2025 and 2026, several Member States received country‑specific recommendations highlighting the importance of phasing out fossil fuel subsidies.

Last but not least, addressing Honourable Member Toussaint's introduction. Protecting health is the foundation for us as citizens and for our economy. It is also not one‑dimensional. It spans from every level of governance to various policy fields. When it comes to food on our table, food in Europe must be safe, and our legislation is among the most comprehensive and stringent in the world. EU law protects human health from risks related to contaminants and pesticide residues in food. Maximum levels for contaminants and pesticide residues are set out in legislation, following risk assessments by the European Food Safety Authority. Protecting people against toxic substances ultimately comes down to one objective: preventing harm before it happens.

interventions.text: The next item is the debate on the oral question to the Commission on the upcoming EU anti-corruption strategy, tabled by Javier Zarzalejos on behalf of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (O-000031/2026 – B10-0016/26)(2026/2790(RSP)).

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, corruption is not simply another form of crime. It's an attack on the institutions that citizens are supposed to trust. Fighting corruption requires consistency; there can be no culture of integrity if corruption is prosecuted on the one hand, while accountability is weakened on the other, because the perception of impunity can be as damaging to democratic legitimacy as corruption itself.
Corruption diverts public money, distorts economic competition, weakens the rule of law and undermines confidence in democracy.

Increasingly, corruption is also a security issue. It enables organised crime to penetrate our economies and our institutions. It facilitates money laundering and the concealment of criminal assets, and it creates opportunities for hostile actors to exercise influence over our democratic decision-making process.

The figures illustrate the scale of the challenge: almost seven out of ten European citizens believe that corruption is widespread in their country. The economic cost of corruption in the European Union is estimated at hundreds of billions of euros every year. And almost 60 % of known criminal groups use corruption as part of their activities.

These are not abstract figures. This is money that should be financing our public services, supporting our economies and improving the lives of European citizens. This is why the LIBE Committee welcomes the Commission's decision to present the first comprehensive EU anti-corruption strategy.
But our message today is also clear: Europe does not need another strategy that merely describes the problem. We need a strategy capable of changing the reality on the ground.

We already have important legislation; earlier this year, we adopted the new Anti-Corruption Directive. What we need now is effective implementation, proper enforcement and the political determination to ensure that the rules apply in practice.

Prevention must be at the centre of this effort. We need stronger safeguards where corruption finds opportunity: in public procurement, in the management of public and European funds, in lobbying and political financing, in conflicts of interest and revolving doors. Transparency is not bureaucracy. It is one of our strongest safeguards against corruption.

But prevention alone is not enough. When corruption takes place, it must be investigated and prosecuted effectively. That requires strong and independent judicial authorities, prosecutors and specialised anti-corruption bodies with the resources and independence necessary to do the job. There can be no credible fight against corruption if those investigating corruption can be pressured, weakened or politicised.

We must also recognise that corruption no longer stops at national jurisdictions, so organised crime networks move money, assets and activity across European countries. Corruption, money laundering and organised crime increasingly reinforce each other. Our European response must therefore be equally interconnected. Let me highlight the importance of Europol, Eurojust, the European Public Prosecutor's Office and OLAF, and our anti-money-laundering architecture to be able to cooperate effectively to detect corruption, follow the money, recover criminal assets and protect the Union's financial interests.

Europe, obviously, must apply the same standards to itself. The credibility of our action depends on strong rules on integrity, transparency and accountability, not only in the Member States, but also within the institutions of the European Union. This strategy must therefore come with measurable objectives, adequate resources, and effective monitoring – because adopting this strategy is not the objective, delivering results is.

Tomorrow, Parliament will vote on the resolution agreed by the LIBE Committee. It sets out our ambitious position on prevention, transparency, integrity, effective investigation and prosecution, stronger action against the links between corruption and criminal and organised crime, and proper monitoring of the implementation. Against this background, on behalf of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, I would like to ask the Commission three questions.
First, how will the upcoming strategy strengthen prevention and help build a genuine culture of integrity, transparency and accountability across the European Union?
Second, how will the Commission ensure that the recently adopted Anti-Corruption Directive is transposed correctly, implemented effectively and enforced in a timely manner by all Member States?

Third, what concrete measures will the Commission propose to safeguard the independence of judicial authorities, prosecutors and specialised bodies responsible for investigating and prosecuting corruption?

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, can I begin by thanking honourable Member, Javier Zarzalejos, on behalf of the LIBE Committee for tabling this important oral question.

Corruption is not just a criminal matter. It threatens our democracies, the rule of law and the very fabric of our societies. It erodes trust in institutions, distorts fair competition, and undermines the proper use of scarce public funds. The recently adopted Directive on combating corruption marks, I believe, a turning point. For the first time, the Union has a common, comprehensive legal framework to fight corruption, and that achievement owes a great deal to this House. And I again thank all of you for the immense work that you put into that project.

Parliament's ambition throughout the negotiations is clearly reflected in the final text. But adopting rules is only the first step. Citizens will indeed judge us by results: whether corruption is prevented, detected, investigated and sanctioned, and whether the rules apply equally to everyone. This is why the Commission will present the first ever EU anti-corruption strategy before the end of this year. Building on the directive, it will provide a common framework for tackling corruption in the years ahead, bringing together public authorities, businesses, civil society and citizens in a whole-of-society approach.

Corruption is not confined to one sector, institution or Member State, and the context in which it operates, we know, is changing fast. It is increasingly now a security challenge, too. Corruption enables organised crime to infiltrate public authorities and hostile actors to undermine our democracies. New technologies and complex cross-border financial flows create new risks, but also new tools to fight against corruption. And citizens expect results: 75 % of Europeans and 65 % of companies consider corruption to be widespread in their country.

The directive gives us a common rulebook. It harmonises the main offences. It sets minimum levels of penalties and, for the first time, establishes European standards for prevention. Its success will depend on effective transposition, implementation and enforcement, and the Commission will actively support the Member States in their efforts.

The Commission's rule of law reports show that legal frameworks are strong in most Member States, but gaps remain in areas such as lobbying, asset declarations, and revolving doors. The strategy is our chance to set a long-term course in the fight against corruption. We want prevention, detection, investigation and enforcement to reinforce one another and action at a local, national, European and international level to be better connected. New technologies can help us to detect corruption and support integrity. We can also build on the cooperation that already exists, such as the EU Network Against Corruption, and make that cooperation more operational.

The objective is not simply about more action, but that our efforts are better coordinated, more coherent and more effective. That should be the central goal of the upcoming strategy, and I look forward to hearing the views of the honourable Members and responding.

Its success will depend on effective transposition, implementation and enforcement, and the Commission will actively support the Member States in their efforts.

The Commission's rule of law reports show that legal frameworks are strong in most Member States, but gaps remain in areas such as lobbying, asset declarations, and revolving doors. The strategy is our chance to set a long-term course in the fight against corruption. We want prevention, detection, investigation and enforcement to reinforce one another and action at a local, national, European and international level to be better connected. New technologies can help us to detect corruption and support integrity. We can also build on the cooperation that already exists, such as the EU Network Against Corruption, and make that cooperation more operational.

The objective is not simply about more action, but that our efforts are better coordinated, more coherent and more effective. That should be the central goal of the upcoming strategy, and I look forward to hearing the views of the honourable Members and responding.

paragraphs.text: Sur President, Sur Kummissarju, Irrid nirringrazzja, l-ewwel nett, lil Javier Zarzalejos u l-kollegi li kellu miegħu li ħadmu fuq ir-riżoluzzjoni li ser nivvutaw fuqha nhar il-Ħamis.

Aktar kmieni din is-sena, il-Parlament adotta liġi Ewropea ġdida b'saħħitha kontra l-korruzzjoni. Kburi li kont qed immexxi dawn in-negozjati f'isem il-Partit Popolari Ewropew. Imma l-liġijiet waħedhom mhumiex biżżejjed. Iridu jitħaddmu, iridu jkunu infurzati u f'kull Stat Membru.

Nagħti żewġ eżempji: f'Malta, pereżempju, nafu sew x'jiġri meta l-istituzzjonijiet ifallu. Daphne Caruana Galizia ġiet assassinata waqt li kienet qed tinvestiga l-korruzzjoni. Disa' snin wara, ir-rakkomandazzjonijiet ewlenin tal-inkjesta pubblika għadhom ma ġewx implimentati. U l-ħelsien riċenti fil-każ tal-assassinju tagħha, reġa' qajjem mistoqsijiet serji dwar ir-responsabilità u l-impunità li hemm f'Malta. U Malta mhux każ waħdu, jekk inħarsu lejn Spanja, pereżempju, taħt Pedro Sanchez l-iskandli ta' korruzzjoni wasslu sal-qalba tal-poter: fil-partit tiegħu, fost l-eqreb nies tiegħu, saħansitra, fil-familja tiegħu. U Sanchez ma jistax jibqa' jaġixxi bħallikieku, dan kollu m'għandux x'jaqsam xejn miegħu.

Meta l-korruzzjoni tasal daqshekk viċin, prim ministru għandu responsabilità politika u dan hu eżattament għaliex l-Ewropa trid tkun soda. U mhux f'Malta u Spanja biss, iżda kull fejn hemm korruzzjoni, kull fejn hemm l-abbuż tal-poter. Ir-regoli jridu japplikaw bl-istess mod. Il-liġi l-ġdida tagħna tatna għodod ġodda, tatna għodod ġodda u issa rridu naraw li dawn jitħaddmu tassew, bl-istess serjetà. Bl-istess serjetà kullimkien għaliex l-istituzzjonijiet għandhom jipproteġu liċ-ċittadini. Il-Kummissjoni Ewropea wkoll għandha tipproteġi liċ-ċittadini. M'għandniex nipproteġu, le, lill-politiċi korrotti u lil min hu kompliċi magħhom għaliex ħadd m'għandu jkun 'il fuq mil-liġi.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Chloé Ridel, au nom du groupe S&D.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, je me félicite que nous adoptions une résolution contre la corruption qui envoie des messages forts, des règles de prévention plus strictes sur les activités parallèles des députés, par exemple, sur le financement des partis politiques, les conflits d'intérêts, le pantouflage et un renforcement du parquet européen pour accroître les moyens de tracer les réseaux de corruption sur lesquels s'appuient la mafia et le narcotrafic en Europe. J'appelle la Commission à s'en inspirer pour sa future stratégie de lutte contre la corruption.

Mes chers collègues, la vérité, c'est que nos propositions continueront de manquer de crédibilité tant qu'elles émaneront d'une institution, le Parlement européen, qui reste elle-même permissive à la corruption: affaire des assistants parlementaires du RN, Qatargate, Huaweigate, affaire Dati, et j'en passe. Comment expliquer que, malgré les scandales, le Parlement européen soit toujours à la traîne pour prévenir et sanctionner les détournements de fonds et les conflits d'intérêts en son sein?

Comment expliquer que, dans les faits, il soit toujours possible d'être député européen et lobbyiste? Comment est-il possible de siéger en commission de l'agriculture tout en travaillant pour une fédération agricole inscrite au registre des lobbies? Comment est-il possible de siéger en commission de la défense tout en travaillant pour une entreprise d'armement? Et tout cela sans être inquiété.

Ces exemples que je viens de citer, chers collègues, sont réels. Je peux aussi mentionner le cas d'une députée dont nous avons refusé de lever l'immunité parlementaire, alors que celle-ci était visée par une enquête du parquet européen pour détournement de fonds.

Plus nous continuons de baigner dans l'impunité en continuant à nous autoréguler – ou plutôt devrais-je dire à nous autoprotéger –, plus nos votes en faveur d'une société moins corrompue sonnent comme de l'hypocrisie. On ne peut pas demander aux autres ce que nous refusons de nous appliquer à nous-mêmes.

Alors, chers collègues, la première chose à faire, c'est de faire en sorte que tous les élus ici soient au service de l'intérêt général, irréprochables quand il s'agit des conflits d'intérêts. Il faut passer de la parole aux actes et établir de véritables règles pour prévenir et sanctionner la corruption et le détournement de fonds au sein de cette institution, et en mettant fin aussi à l'autoprotection et l'autorégulation, en cessant de bloquer la mise en place de l'organe éthique européen.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Fabrice Leggeri, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, en 1971, François Mitterrand dénonçait «l'argent qui corrompt, l'argent qui achète, l'argent qui écrase». Dix ans plus tard, il ajoutait: "Aux dirigeants de montrer l'exemple." Certains de ses héritiers européens auraient été bien inspirés de suivre ce conseil. Le Qatargate a révélé des soupçons de corruption au cœur même de ce Parlement, impliquant plusieurs personnalités issues de la famille socialiste européenne.

Alors oui, l'Europe doit lutter contre la corruption, mais elle doit commencer par être exemplaire. Nous attendons aujourd'hui une véritable transparence sur l'utilisation des fonds européens, sur leurs bénéficiaires et sur le fonctionnement de nos propres institutions.

En revanche, nous refusons que la lutte contre la corruption devienne le prétexte à un renforcement permanent de la conditionnalité liée à l'état de droit et un instrument de chantage politique sur les États membres. La lutte contre la corruption exige de la transparence, de la responsabilité et de l'exemplarité. Avant de donner des leçons à l'Europe entière, Bruxelles doit commencer par se les appliquer.

interventions.speaker_label: Mariusz Kamiński, w imieniu grupy ECR.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Unia Europejska ma poważny problem z korupcją. W ostatnich latach doszło do szeregu skandali korupcyjnych z udziałem ważnych europejskich polityków i wysokich urzędników. Mamy ciągle nierozliczone afery Katargate i Huawei, mamy afery z udziałem byłych komisarzy Reindersa, Avramopoulosa, Mogherini. Obywatele Unii mają dość tej degrengolady i oczekują zdecydowanych działań. Przyjęta w ostatnim czasie dyrektywa antykorupcyjna jest zbyt słabą reakcją na tę sytuację.

Panie Komisarzu! Strategia antykorupcyjna Unii musi się odnosić przede wszystkim do instytucji unijnych. Instytucje unijne są nietransparentne i potrzebują wprowadzenia nowych, twardych mechanizmów antykorupcyjnych. W szczególności istotne jest wprowadzenie obowiązku składania pod odpowiedzialnością karną jawnych i podlegających weryfikacji oświadczeń majątkowych. Dzisiejsze uznaniowe deklaracje o braku konfliktu interesów składane przez komisarzy są absolutnie niewystarczające.

Należy również zdecydowanie uderzyć w nielegalny lobbing i wyeliminować zjawisko drzwi obrotowych. Z punktu widzenia skutecznej walki z korupcją niezwykle ważne jest wsparcie dla wyspecjalizowanych i niezależnych organów antykorupcyjnych, takich jak polskie Centralne Biuro Antykorupcyjne. Panie Komisarzu! Jeśli Unia rzeczywiście chce walczyć z korupcją, musi zacząć od własnych instytucji.

interventions.speaker_label: Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, with many of you, I negotiated the new anti-corruption directive for the European Union – our new law. I can tell you my biggest frustration was national governments not wanting more mandatory measures to prevent corruption. Too much work, not necessary. So I am wondering, what would Daphne Caruana Galizia and Giorgos Karaivaz have said to this? Two journalists killed for investigating high‑level corruption in Malta and Greece. Still there is no justice for them.

Corruption kills, and not only in Malta and Greece, but everywhere in the in our Union. We owe it to them and to all of our citizens to be bolder. We need to prevent corruption before it can happen. We need to implement the anti-corruption directive as if lives depended on it, because they do. We need fully independent prosecutors and judges who can do their work free from pressure. We want a culture of integrity instead of a culture of impunity, for Giorgos, for Daphne.

interventions.speaker_label: Daniel Freund, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, the biggest success in the fight against corruption in the European Union that we have seen in recent years was that Hungarian voters threw out the most corrupt government that we have seen in the history of the Union. After 16 years of Orbán and his family and friends stealing billions of taxpayer money, this is now over – the king of corruption is out.

But Orbán was not only the king of corruption in Hungary, he was, unfortunately, also the king of corruption at the negotiation table in Brussels. Because, while the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom adopted Magnitsky regimes and allow that the most corrupt people in the world can be sanctioned and kept out, Orbán prevented that we did the same in the European Union.

To this day, we don't have this, and honestly, the most corrupt people should not enjoy our cities, our beaches, our universities. We should, now that he is gone, urgently introduce that sanction regime in the European Union as well.

interventions.speaker_label: Giuseppe Antoci, a nome del gruppo The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: a nome del gruppo The Left

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la corruzione non è un reato, è un furto di democrazia. La strategia anticorruzione deve avere un obiettivo di combatterla, certamente, ma anche prevenirla. Guardare anche agli Stati membri, quello che accade nei paesi, quello che è accaduto in Italia, dove il ministro della Giustizia Carlo Nordio ha pensato bene di cancellare l'abuso d'ufficio, un reato terribile.

L'Europa è più forte quando non lascia quei cittadini da soli, così come è accaduto in Italia. Non lasciarli da soli significa il lavoro che abbiamo fatto approvando la direttiva anticorruzione e l'articolo 7 sull'esercizio illecito delle funzioni pubbliche, proprio quell'abuso d'ufficio che in Italia era stato cancellato. Ha fatto bene la nostra relatrice a ribadire che l'Italia sarà obbligata.

Allora l'Europa più forte significa dimostrare che il potere pubblico non è un privilegio, non è una zona franca, perché chi esercita le funzioni pubbliche lo deve fare con disciplina ed onore. E invito la Commissione a vigilare affinché gli Stati membri adottino la direttiva con la stessa disciplina ed onore.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, con-rumpere: rompere, rovinare, distruggere l'integrità di qualcosa. Questa è l'origine del termine "corruzione" e questo effettivamente fa la corruzione: rovina la democrazia, mina la fiducia nelle istituzioni, viola uguaglianza e libertà di iniziativa, riduce la qualità dei servizi, costa centinaia di miliardi di euro e dà modo alle organizzazioni criminali di infiltrarsi nelle amministrazioni.

Un fenomeno così pervasivo e, come attesta l'Eurobarometro, così diffuso richiede una risposta globale che parta dalla prevenzione. Una prevenzione indirizzata anche all'informazione e alla sensibilizzazione dei cittadini, inclusi i più giovani, perché la corruzione in realtà è una grave violazione dei loro diritti.

Ci vuole cooperazione, maggiore cooperazione, scambio di informazioni, interoperabilità fra autorità nazionali, organi e agenzie dell'Unione, che vanno tutti sostenuti con adeguate risorse, perché corruzione, riciclaggio e crimine organizzato si intrecciano tra loro e travalicano ogni confine.

La strategia anticorruzione, per cui ringrazio la Commissione, deve poi fare sistema con la revisione dell'architettura antifrode e con le nuove norme contro la criminalità organizzata, a partire dall'adozione di una nuova e più moderna nozione di "organizzazione criminale", comune e condivisa, che rifletta la dimensione imprenditoriale assunta dalle reti criminali e già intravista da mio padre Rocco Chinnici, giudice ucciso dalla mafia nel 1982.

Un fenomeno così pervasivo e, come attesta l'Eurobarometro, così diffuso richiede una risposta globale che parta dalla prevenzione. Una prevenzione indirizzata anche all'informazione e alla sensibilizzazione dei cittadini, inclusi i più giovani, perché la corruzione in realtà è una grave violazione dei loro diritti.

Ci vuole cooperazione, maggiore cooperazione, scambio di informazioni, interoperabilità fra autorità nazionali, organi e agenzie dell'Unione, che vanno tutti sostenuti con adeguate risorse, perché corruzione, riciclaggio e crimine organizzato si intrecciano tra loro e travalicano ogni confine.

La strategia anticorruzione, per cui ringrazio la Commissione, deve poi fare sistema con la revisione dell'architettura antifrode e con le nuove norme contro la criminalità organizzata, a partire dall'adozione di una nuova e più moderna nozione di "organizzazione criminale", comune e condivisa, che rifletta la dimensione imprenditoriale assunta dalle reti criminali e già intravista da mio padre Rocco Chinnici, giudice ucciso dalla mafia nel 1982.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, corupția nu este o problemă abstractă. Are un cost direct pentru fiecare cetățean. Fiecare euro pierdut din cauza corupției este un euro care nu mai ajunge în școli, spitale, locuințe, infrastructură sau servicii publice mai bune.

Dar trebuie să vorbim și despre noile forme ale corupției și despre legătura tot mai puternică dintre corupție și criminalitatea organizată. Vedem rețele de trafic de droguri care folosesc corupția pentru a-și proteja activitățile. Vedem fluxuri financiare și active transferate peste granițe și ascunse prin structuri tot mai complexe. Vedem dezvoltarea platformelor ilegale de pariuri online care operează dincolo de frontiere și evită regulile naționale. În fața unor rețele care operează transfrontalier, răspunsul nostru nu poate rămâne exclusiv național.

Noua strategie europeană anticorupție trebuie să conecteze mai bine prevenția, combaterea criminalității organizate, lupta împotriva spălării banilor și protejarea fondurilor europene. Avem nevoie de schimb de informații mai rapid, de o justiție independentă, de cooperare între autoritățile naționale și cele europene și de capacitatea reală de a identifica, îngheța și recupera banii proveniți din corupție și criminalitate.

De aceea, în calitate de raportor, am solicitat și obținut sprijinul Parlamentului European pentru a cere creșterea bugetului dedicat justiției. Totodată, avem nevoie de transparență, reguli clare privind conflictele de interese. Așa cum au spus și colegii mei mai devreme, aceleași standarde trebuie să se aplice peste tot, inclusiv în instituțiile europene.

În calitate de vicepreședinte al Parlamentului European responsabil de transparență și combatere a corupției, cred că obiectivul nostru trebuie să fie clar: să protejăm banii europeni, să protejăm instituțiile democratice și încrederea cetățenilor. Și asta trece inclusiv prin aplicarea acestor standarde. Și structura care se ocupă de etică trebuie să fie sprijinită pentru a deveni realitate cât mai rapid cu putință.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Det är glädjande att kommissionen har lagt fram den här strategin mot korruption. Jag sitter själv i budgetkontrollutskottet och är föredragande när det gäller översynen av antibedrägeriarkitekturen, som det heter, där vi vill stärka arbetet med att just upptäcka den ekonomiska korruptionen. Och den juridiska är lika viktig att komma till rätta med, att bekämpa, med alla möjliga medel.

Jag tyckte den muntliga frågan var väldigt bra ställd om att prata om en kultur, om transparens. Tyvärr hörde jag ingenting av kommissionären i inledningstalet om transparens, för jag upplever att det är kärnan i bekämpningen av korruption och bedrägerier: att vi gör transaktioner med EU medel tillgängliga, synliga och offentliga ända ner till slutanvändaren. Då bekämpar man, förebygger man korruption på det mest effektiva sätt som finns, tror jag. Det borde vi jobba med mer.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, Commissioner, we have the Anti-Corruption Directive now. It's crucial. But the sharpest legal tool is useless if the hands holding the scales of justice are tied. And that dangerous squeeze is visible across the Member States, unfortunately – also including Slovenia, where under Janez Janša's new government, prosecutors' offices are being overhauled under the hollow guise of 'efficiency', while parliamentary inquiries are weaponised as political tribunals to intimidate independent voices. Different laws. Same principle.

Who watches those in power, and who controls the watchers? When politicians pick, who investigates also them, they don't increase efficiency of justice; they create impunity. And that's not fighting corruption. It's fighting investigation.

Therefore, the upcoming EU anti-corruption strategy cannot remain an exercise in legal cosmetics. Corruption doesn't fear another piece of paper. It fears prosecutors whose decisions cannot be controlled by those in power. And the new Slovenian laws show exactly why they call it an anti-corruption reform. Sure, it reforms, but the wrong side of the equation.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, komissaari, korruptio ei ole Venäjälle pahe, se on ase. Ennen sotaa se toimi diileillä, hunajalla ja rahalla. Entisiä pääministereitä toimi venäläisten energiayhtiöiden konsultteina ja istui niiden hallituksissa. Likaista rahaa pestiin eurooppalaisissa pankeissa sadoilla miljardeilla.

Kun hyökkäys alkoi helmikuussa 2022, moni Euroopan pääkaupunki oli jo valmiiksi pehmitetty. Sota ei lopeta tartuntaa. Raha liikkuu yhä, Moldovassa on ostettu ääniä ja pakotteita kierretään peiteyhtiöiden ja varjolaivaston kautta.

Raha ja hunaja eivät kuitenkaan enää riitä. Rikollismaailma tuntee tarjouksen: hopeaa tai lyijyä. Nyt Euroopalle näytetään lyijyä, pelkoja, fyysistä uhkaa. Päättäjien koteihin tunkeudutaan, autoja ja taloja sytytetään tuleen, nimiä kirjataan listoille. Kansio ihmisestä on sama kuin ennenkin, ennen siitä etsittiin hinta, nyt heikko kohta.

Siksi komission korruptionvastainen strategia on turvallisuuspolitiikkaa. Sen on katettava molemmat: raha, jolla ostetaan, ja pelko, jolla vaiennetaan. Todelliset omistajat on tuotava näkyviin. Pakotteiden kiertämisestä on seurattava rangaistus jokaisessa jäsenvaltiossa, ja niitä, joita painostetaan, on suojattava. Ostettu päättäjä, pelotettu äänestäjä ja päättäjä toimivat samalla tavalla. Demokratia ei kestä kumpaakaan.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Kollegor. Kommissionär. Korruption börjar där ansvarsutkrävande upphör. Kontroverserna rörande den moderate statsministern Ulf Kristersson i Sverige, från Fållöknastiftelsen till Landerholmsaffären och frågor om användning av statliga residens, påminner oss om att inget land är immunt.

Korruption har många ansikten. Det kan handla om pengar. Det kan handla om gentjänster, tillgång till makt eller missbruk av offentliga resurser. Men priset betalas alltid av medborgarna och i slutändan vår demokrati.

Mitt land, Sverige, tillhör fortfarande de länder i världen med lägst korruption, men vår position har försämrats de senaste åren, och det borde vara en väckarklocka för många. Därför måste EU agera – mer transparens, skarpare granskning och verkliga konsekvenser för dem som missbrukar allmänhetens förtroende. Och EU:s antikorruptionsstrategi måste vara ambitiös. Vi behöver bland annat striktare regler om intressekonflikter och politisk finansiering.
Demokratin kan inte överleva om människor upplever att det finns ett regelverk för dem och ett annat regelverk för oss som har makt att förändra.

paragraphs.text: Thank you, Mr President, I would like to put a question to you, Ms Incir. You spoke about your Prime Minister – the Swedish Prime Minister – but the corruption in Sweden is generally very low. But there are some other countries, like the Czech Republic, where the Prime Minister is in a conflict of interest, and the European Commission has decided that he is in a conflict of interest. Yet they still send him European money – the money of European voters. Do you think that this is a fair way to behave, or does the Commission have to take stronger measures and stronger actions against these people who are linked to conflicts of interest?

paragraphs.text: Thank you very much for the question. First and foremost, I believe that in all cases where there are indications or any kind of suspicions that there could be corruption, they need to be looked into. I also think that, on a European level, we need to look at the tools that we have. We need to strengthen it through, among other things, the anti-corruption strategy. But I would also say to link more closely the yearly report on democracy and the rule of law to the financing that we are providing the Member States with. So in the end, look into the cases where there could be some kind of suspicions, but then also ensure that we have the tools. But I also want to finalise what you're saying, that we should not use political games against each other, because sometimes, here in the European Parliament, I feel that things that shouldn't become political become political, so that when serious cases appear, they are not looked into thoroughly.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, cari cittadini d'Europa, un tedesco che parla in italiano di corruzione, vedo già arrivare i commenti arrabbiati. Molti deputati di partiti populisti, anche generali congedati dal servizio, accusano l'Unione europea di corruzione e, allo stesso tempo, spesso sono le stesse persone a produrre i più grandi scandali di corruzione.

La democrazia non appartiene a chi grida più forte, non appartiene ai generali, non appartiene ai giudici di Internet, appartiene alle persone e, in loro nome, sono i tribunali indipendenti a decidere chi è corrotto, non i politici. Chi vuole combattere la corruzione deve quindi proteggere soprattutto una cosa: lo Stato di diritto.
