paragraphs.text: Señor presidente:
Caso Koldo: el exministro de Transportes del Gobierno de Sánchez, condenado a 24 años de prisión por organización criminal, cohecho, malversación y tráfico de influencias —19 años para su asesor—.
Caso García Ortiz: el fiscal general Estado, condenado a dos años de inhabilitación por revelación de secretos contra la oposición política.
Caso David Sánchez: el hermano del presidente y el líder del PSOE en Extremadura, condenados por prevaricación.

Caso Cerdán: el secretario de Organización del PSOE, en prisión provisional por el presunto amaño de obra pública —la presidenta de la red pública de transportes y varios altos cargos de su ministerio, también imputados—.
Caso Plus Ultra: el expresidente Zapatero, padre político del señor Sánchez, imputado por el rescate de 53 millones de fondos NextGenerationUE.
Las joyas de Zapatero: imputación paralela al expresidente por fraude fiscal y contrabando.
Caso Leire Díez: presunta trama para desestabilizar causas judiciales contra dirigentes socialistas atacando a jueces, fiscales y fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad del Estado.

Caso Cloacas: la Audiencia Nacional investiga a la gerente del Partido Socialista, a la directora de la Guardia Civil y al director de la Policía por prevaricación y otros delitos contra la administración de Justicia.
Financiación irregular del PSOE: bajo secreto de sumario los pagos en metálico a este partido entre 2017 y 2024.
Mascarillas de Canarias: el actual ministro de Política Territorial, investigado por la Fiscalía Europea por posible malversación.
Caso Begoña Gómez: juicio oral a la esposa del presidente por tráfico de influencias y malversación.
Y podría seguir un buen rato, señor comisario.

Un Estado miembro, un solo Gobierno con más de 15 procesos judiciales abiertos o siendo juzgados, más de 120 personas imputadas y cero reformas contra la corrupción en ocho años, señor comisario. Y no será porque no lo venimos avisando a esta Comisión desde el inicio de su mandato. Por lo tanto, sí, la estrategia de la UE de lucha contra la corrupción no solo es necesaria: es imprescindible.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, la lotta alla corruzione passa innanzitutto dalla trasparenza. Per questo è importante che la proposta sugli appalti pubblici, presentata dalla Commissione il 9 settembre, punti a digitalizzare l'intero ciclo di vita dei contratti pubblici e a costruire una vera banca dati europea degli appalti.

Significa più efficienza e velocità, ma soprattutto più controlli, più tracciabilità e meno zone d'ombra. Ora il Parlamento deve rafforzare questa proposta e dobbiamo affrontare il tema dei subappalti a cascata. In nome della concorrenza abbiamo creato catene sempre più lunghe, dove aumentano l'opacità, il rischio di infiltrazioni criminali e lo sfruttamento dei lavoratori, mentre diminuiscono qualità e responsabilità. A pagarne il prezzo sono anche le piccole e medie imprese.

Infine, la prima strategia europea anticorruzione deve fissare regole comuni più ambiziose: trasparenza dell'amministrazione, prevenzione dei conflitti di interesse, responsabilità di chi esercita un potere pubblico. È anche una questione di democrazia e oggi l'Europa deve dare un segnale forte anche oltre l'Atlantico. Chi governa deve servire l'interesse pubblico, non confonderlo con il proprio.

In nome della concorrenza abbiamo creato catene sempre più lunghe, dove aumentano l'opacità, il rischio di infiltrazioni criminali e lo sfruttamento dei lavoratori, mentre diminuiscono qualità e responsabilità. A pagarne il prezzo sono anche le piccole e medie imprese.

Infine, la prima strategia europea anticorruzione deve fissare regole comuni più ambiziose: trasparenza dell'amministrazione, prevenzione dei conflitti di interesse, responsabilità di chi esercita un potere pubblico. È anche una questione di democrazia e oggi l'Europa deve dare un segnale forte anche oltre l'Atlantico. Chi governa deve servire l'interesse pubblico, non confonderlo con il proprio.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, vážené kolegyně, vážení kolegové, korupce nás stojí každý rok stovky milionů eur a až 6 % evropského HDP. Korupce je obyčejná krádež našich peněz ‒ peněz našich občanů. Jsou to peníze, které potom chybí na nemocnice, školy, bezpečnost a obranu. A já jsem ji viděl několikrát zblízka, třeba na Slovensku. Na misi, kde jsme byli s Výborem pro rozpočtovou kontrolu. Když jsme přijeli, tak jsme podali Evropské komisi a evropským institucím na 300 případů a podnětů možného zneužití peněz. Podezření přišla ze 76, potom ze 79 slovenských okresů, ale už ani toto číslo neplatí. Dokonce dneska máme podezření na korupci a na zneužití peněz z dalších třech okresů. A ta podezření neustále přibývají. Farmáři nám posílali důkazy o nátlaku, whistlebloweři mají strach, novináři mluví o klientelistických sítích a stále se vracela stejná jména a stejné struktury. Kauza Dobytkár ‒ miliony na úplatcích. Norbert Bödör ‒ obžalovaný v této kauze a v dalších kauzách. Člověk s dlouhodobými vazbami na slovenského premiéra Roberta Fica. Dámy a pánové, my chceme posílit EPPO, my chceme silný OLAF, ale hlavně chceme nulovou toleranci korupce bez ohledu na jméno, na kontakty a na to, kdo právě sedí ve vládě. A proto jsem rád, že chceme vytvořit novou protikorupční infrastrukturu.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señorías, los españoles llevamos ocho años sufriendo el Gobierno más corrupto de toda la Unión Europea; ocho años de deterioro democrático y de una demolición institucional orquestada por el Partido Socialista y ejecutada desde Moncloa. Tráfico de influencias, comisiones, contratos amañados, financiación ilegal, prostitutas enchufadas en empresas públicas, joyas millonarias ocultas en cajas fuertes para evadir el fisco, chantaje a los fiscales que investigan la corrupción e incluso contactos con sicarios para eliminar a jueces.

Señorías, no se trata de una película de gánsteres; se trata del Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez. La historia reciente de Europa no ha conocido un grado de corrupción semejante. España necesita urgentemente recuperar la ejemplaridad, la transparencia y la confianza en sus instituciones. Por suerte, en cincuenta días, España tiene la oportunidad de elegir un Gobierno limpio y decente, y dentro de cincuenta días, por fin, los españoles pondremos fin a estos ocho años de pesadilla.
Comisario, la estrategia de lucha contra la corrupción no puede esperar.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario McGrath, la estrategia anticorrupción es inobjetable: es coherente con la competencia legisladora penal de este Parlamento Europeo, con la Directiva anticorrupción que hemos puesto en vigor, con el paquete de lucha contra el blanqueo, con nuestro apoyo a la Fiscalía Europea y a la cooperación judicial penal. Pero la principal ventaja es que sienta un estándar europeo que hace innecesario e impertinente mancillar este debate con diatribas nacionales, como han hecho los diputados del Partido Popular insultando al Gobierno de España.

Ayer estuvo aquí el primer ministro portugués, Luís Montenegro, que convocó elecciones acuciado por acusaciones de corrupción en su entorno familiar, y no se escuchó jamás a ningún socialista portugués traer a este debate el nombre de Portugal ni de su Gobierno. ¡Qué diferencia con respecto de las mentiras, bulos, infamias y acusaciones sin fundamento que hemos escuchado esta tarde aquí contra el Gobierno de España, mezcladas con casos judiciales que no tienen ningún alcance europeo!
Por tanto, centrémonos en la legislación penal europea y hagámonos fuertes contra toda forma de corrupción.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, EU kylvää veronmaksajien rahoja korruptoituneisiin maihin miljardikaupalla. Vuoden 2024 tilastot ovat varmistuneet ja ne paljastavat, että EU ja sen jäsenvaltiot tuuttasivat lähes 90 miljardia euroa kehitysapuun yhden vuoden aikana.

Vain pari tuntia sitten tämä sali keskusteli eurooppalaisten elinkustannuskriisistä. Kun tätä rahan lapioimista ympäri maailmaa katsoo, niin ei tunnu paljon tavallisen kansalaisen elinkustannuskriisit painavan. Mihin nämä miljardit valuvat?

Kun Maailmanpankki tutki pitkän aikavälin tilastoja, havaittiin seuraavaa: kun apuriippuvaisille maille kilahtaa avustuksia, samaan aikaan tapahtuu jyrkkä nousu ulkomaisten pankkiparatiisien talletuksissa. Tältä näyttää korruptio. Kun halutaan ajaa korruptiota alas, on ajettava kehitysapu alas.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, 71 % des citoyens européens estiment que la corruption est répandue dans leur pays, et plus des trois quarts la jugent présente dans leurs institutions politiques. Cette défiance fragilise nos démocraties, car aucune démocratie ne peut vivre sans confiance.

Alors, comment accepter que des demandes de levée d’immunité de députés européens formulées par le Parquet européen soient rejetées par le Parlement européen lui-même? La crédibilité ne se proclame pas: elle se construit par des actes.
Mettons fin à cette anomalie. Les députés ne devraient pas être juges et parties lorsqu’il s’agit de leur propre immunité. L’immunité ne devrait-elle pas, tout simplement, disparaître?

Une majorité de nos concitoyens doutent de notre capacité à combattre efficacement la corruption. À nous de leur prouver le contraire. L’exemplarité des élus est une exigence démocratique car comme dit le proverbe: «Le poisson pourrit par la tête.»
Chers collègues, soyons intransigeants.

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, sigur, avem o directivă europeană anticorupție, dar se aplică diferit în cele 27 de state.

Se vorbea aici de transparență. Nu credeți că prima dată trebuie să dea dovadă de transparență Comisia și Consiliul? Am fost raportor pe descărcarea de gestiune a Comisiei. Doamna președintă a Comisiei a refuzat să-mi dea contractele de achiziție pe medicamente. Consiliul refuză să ne dea datele când noi vrem să facem descărcarea de gestiune. Avem comisari care au fost condamnați sau urmăriți penal pentru corupție.

Domnule comisar, eu cred că trebuie să gândim în mod foarte serios această strategie. Procesele durează mult, ajung să fie presiuni din partea Comisiei, cum a fost în țara mea. Pentru conflict de interese, Comisia a trimis o scrisoare României pentru că a fost un primar din arcul guvernamental condamnat pentru conflict de interese. În acest fel nu putem schimba percepția cetățenilor care, vedeți, 7 din 10 cred că este corupție. Se risipesc bani și avem instituții europene care trebuie să protejeze banii cetățenilor.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidente, vamos a ver, sanchista, ¿usted de qué cueva sale? ¿Cómo que la corrupción del Partido Socialista no tiene trascendencia europea? ¡Pero que habéis robado fondos europeos! paragraphs.text: Госпожо Председател, корупцията е реален проблем. Тя подкопава доверието в демокрацията и отклонява средства от болници, училища, инфраструктура и социални услуги. По най-песимистични оценки, цитирани в проекта за резолюцията, цената ѝ за Европейския съюз достига близо един трилион евро годишно и затова е важно, че ние не говорим само общо за борба с корупцията, ние настояваме за реално независими антикорупционни органи с достатъчно хора и средства и изрично предупреждаваме срещу тяхното отслабване или политизиране.

Необходима е и по-добра координация между Европейската прокуратура, ОЛАФ, Европол и националните органи. Поставяме специален акцент върху обществените поръчки, където слабият контрол става проблем в много държави, а за бъдещия европейски бюджет предлагаме националните програми да съдържат конкретни и измерими антикорупционни цели. Това е важно и за България. Не формално изпълнение на реформи, а институции, които работят, и европейски средства, които действително стигат до гражданите.
Пожелавам успех в писането на стратегията, господин комисар, но всички знаем, че предизвикателство е да бъде приложена и да даде резултат.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, your contributions are a reminder to me of the strong anti-corruption stance that the Parliament took in the recent negotiations on the anti-corruption directive. And when it comes to the anti-corruption strategy, I know that you want it to be meaningful. I share that ambition with you and I look forward to working with you.

It must have clear priorities and concrete actions, and I think it also has to look at the broader environment in which corruption can sometimes thrive. We have to seek to answer the 'why' question. Why is corruption happening so much in the European Union?
We need to be inclusive in our approach, involving not just public authorities, but also the private sector, the civil society and indeed our international partners.

I want to give you a commitment, on the back of you being a driving force behind the anti-corruption directive, of my full determination and resolve to work with you and ensure the full implementation and enforcement of that directive. And I know that I can count on this House to bring the very same level of ambition to this upcoming anti-corruption strategy.
We rightly asked Member States, public authorities and companies to uphold high standards of integrity. And of course, the same must also apply to all of us, including the EU institutions.

That is why the work of the EPPO, of OLAF, the full implementation of the financial regulation is so important, and I know I will work with you in the context of the ongoing review of the anti-fraud architecture. Because preserving public trust in democracy and in our institutions is absolutely crucial, and the upcoming strategy will provide us with another opportunity to show the citizens of the European Union that we take the fight against corruption very seriously at all levels of the European Union.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Members and dear Commissioner Jørgensen, renewable and clean energy are a clear priority for the Irish Presidency of the Council. This is all the more true now that the European Union's dependency on imported fossil fuels has caused another price shock. Sixty-seven per cent of the European Union's energy is coming from fossil fuels, nearly all of which are imported. This makes us all very vulnerable to price shocks, with huge repercussions for households and for industries. The Irish Presidency will therefore emphasise the need for accelerated electrification and deployment of renewable and clean energy to deliver decarbonised and affordable power for all European citizens. And we can rely on a solid legislative framework with legally binding targets and legal instruments to achieve them.
With the upcoming post‑2030 framework package, we will be looking at how to continue the energy transition in the next decade.

Closer to home, I would like to refer to the work conducted by the Irish Presidency. We are committed to reaching a compromise with you as the Parliament on the grids package by the end of the year. The package has the ambition to strengthen our European energy infrastructure and to contribute to the internal energy market by accelerating the permitting procedures. It is an important step to modernise our grids and to set the path towards clean energy.

Yesterday, indeed, we held our second trilogue on the Permitting Directive here in Parliament. And in a week we will have our second trilogue on the TEN‑E Regulation. Rest assured that we are committed to find the best possible solutions on these files.

The Irish Presidency is also committed to reaching a Council mandate on the Network Charges Regulation by the end of the year, so that the Council can start negotiations with you as soon as you are ready.

Finally, I would like to insist on the fact that the European Union will need every technology available on its soil to reach a full, clean energy system. With its electrification action plan, the Commission has set an indicative electrification target of 46 % in 2040. It means that we need to beef up our action on renewable energy to secure home-grown energy.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, EUR 180 billion – according to one estimate, that is how much extreme heat could cost the EU economies this year. That is enough to wipe out the entire economic growth that has been forecast for the EU in 2026 – and that's before we add our fossil fuel bill. Since the war in the Middle East began, we have paid over EUR 100 billion extra for imported fossil fuels without receiving a single molecule more.

Yet again, Europe is facing a fossil energy crisis. The lives of millions of Europeans are being negatively impacted by high energy bills, by skyrocketing prices at the filling stations. Our companies are struggling to stay competitive. We know what we must do to get out of this crisis and to avoid future ones: we need to pursue clean energy independence – that is why we are rolling out more renewables. Last year, for the first time, the EU produced more electricity from solar and wind combined than from fossil fuels.

At the same time, we are advancing the next generation of nuclear power. Earlier this year, I presented the Commission's strategy for small modular reactors, and by the end of the year I will present our fusion strategy. We are also accelerating innovation and expanding clean alternatives like geothermal energy, sustainable biofuels, clean hydrogen. Thanks to these efforts, we are producing more clean energy than ever before, but hundreds of gigawatts are still waiting to be captured, connected and deployed.

Between now and the end of the year, we will be advancing key pieces of legislation to unlock this energy and the Parliament has a vital role to play. There is our grids package: with this package, we aim to roll out our grids at a faster pace and we aim to plan our energy networks in a way that is more strategic, more rational and more cost-effective. I welcome the good cooperation of the Parliament on this file and I hope we can secure a strong and ambitious agreement by the end of the year.

Discussions on the next MFF are also progressing and the outcome of these negotiations will have a big impact on our energy system. The Commission has proposed a fivefold increase for the energy budget of the Connecting Europe Facility, and the national and regional partnership plans will also provide wide opportunities to promote clean energy. If we want to fully connect our grids and to finally complete our energy union, this funding is of paramount importance. It is therefore essential to maintain the ambition of the Commission's proposal.

Finally, let me also mention our electrification action plan. A key part of this plan – our proposal on network charges and energy taxation – is currently before the Parliament. This proposal also aims to bring down electricity bills, to encourage flexibility and to make clean electricity the most attractive options for homes, businesses and industries. I know that these priorities are shared by the Parliament and I look forward to working with you all to deliver on these priorities and to realise Europe's clean energy potential.

interventions.speaker_label: François-Xavier Bellamy, au nom du groupe PPE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, ce débat est fondamental au moment où, vous l'avez dit, Monsieur le Commissaire, notre continent connaît une crise énergétique absolument majeure. Et face à cette crise, notre devoir est d'utiliser tous les outils possibles pour reconquérir la souveraineté de notre approvisionnement, pour faire baisser les prix et pour décarboner les sources d'énergie nécessaires à la vie de notre économie.

La Commission a-t-elle une seule parole sur cette question? Bien sûr, nous l'avons entendu depuis le début de ce mandat, il y a enfin, enfin, une reconnaissance du fait que toutes les sources d'énergie, y compris l'électricité nucléaire, seront nécessaires – et vous l'avez dit à l'instant – pour affronter cette crise et pour reconstruire l'élan de l'économie européenne.

Mais comment ne pas voir que nous ne sommes pas encore sortis des discriminations du passé lorsque, dans quelques semaines, la Commission s'apprête à publier un prochain objectif pour 2040, qui fixerait de nouveau un impératif aux États d'énergie renouvelable uniquement. Le seul et unique but doit être de construire un maximum de sources d'énergie bas carbone. Tous les mix énergétiques qui ont privilégié le renouvelable ont montré qu'ils étaient condamnés à subir les conséquences de l'intermittence, de la dépendance aux importations gazières, parfois au charbon, qui sont nécessaires pour équilibrer l'intermittence des énergies éolienne et solaire.

Monsieur le Commissaire, notre message aujourd'hui est très clair: le seul et unique objectif que nous devons poursuivre ensemble, c'est celui qui consiste à décarboner notre énergie, y compris, bien sûr, avec l'énergie nucléaire. Un objectif renouvelable qui imposerait à un pays comme la France d'arrêter ses centrales nucléaires pour continuer de développer partout des éoliennes et des panneaux solaires serait totalement aberrant.

Et la vérité, c'est que ce débat d'aujourd'hui est en lui-même un symptôme. Nous avons tenté de mettre cette discussion à l'agenda du Parlement européen, en proposant que nous parlions ensemble de l'énergie bas carbone. Mais pour certains groupes politiques, sur la gauche, l'énergie bas carbone veut dire l'énergie nucléaire et c'était déjà scandaleux d'en parler. Nous nous trouvons donc à parler d'énergie propre. Énergie propre, énergie décarbonée: c'est tous les outils qu'il faut utiliser, avec enfin la neutralité technologique dont l'Europe a besoin pour pouvoir sauver la planète et sauver son économie.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, we hebben het gewoon lastig. Als Europa moeten we beseffen dat we het merendeel van onze energie importeren. Dan moeten we begrijpen dat het alternatief betekent dat we voor onze onafhankelijkheid en voor onze portemonnee meer Europese energie moeten gaan opwekken. Dat is, of je het nu wil of niet, windenergie, dat is zon, dat is waterkracht, dat is geothermie. Dat moet de basis zijn voor die betaalbare toekomst.

Want als gewone mensen hun energierekening niet kunnen betalen, dan verliezen we hun steun. Als mensen investeren in warmtepompen en in zonnepanelen en bijvoorbeeld in een elektrische auto, dan moeten we dat waarderen, want zij nemen hun verantwoordelijkheid om die vraag te veranderen, om de vraag naar fossiel te doen dalen.

In plaats van we hen te belonen, krijgen deze voorlopers te maken met stijgende netwerkkosten. Dat is niet goed. Dat is de omgekeerde wereld. Laten we die koplopers niet afremmen met hogere kosten, maar juist versnellen met een eerlijke energierekening. Ik heb er alle vertrouwen in dat onze commissaris dat gaat regelen.

Als mensen investeren in warmtepompen en in zonnepanelen en bijvoorbeeld in een elektrische auto, dan moeten we dat waarderen, want zij nemen hun verantwoordelijkheid om die vraag te veranderen, om de vraag naar fossiel te doen dalen.

In plaats van we hen te belonen, krijgen deze voorlopers te maken met stijgende netwerkkosten. Dat is niet goed. Dat is de omgekeerde wereld. Laten we die koplopers niet afremmen met hogere kosten, maar juist versnellen met een eerlijke energierekening. Ik heb er alle vertrouwen in dat onze commissaris dat gaat regelen.

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Paolo Borchia, a nome del gruppo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, partiamo dal presupposto, dal contesto che vede un'Unione europea fanalino di coda in termini di generazione di PIL tra quelle che sono le regioni economiche avanzate a livello globale.

Quindi, Commissario, mi sembra evidente che ci sia qualcosa che non vada. E in economia, quando qualcosa non va, si passa anche da politiche energetiche che magari non sono ottimali. L'obiettivo dell'elettrificazione al 46 %, ad oggi, è lontano dalla realtà per un tema di infrastruttura e anche per un tema di generazione. Ci sono tanti obiettivi ma pochi allacciamenti. Ricordiamo che, ad oggi, ci sono sedici Stati che hanno in coda dei progetti per 120 gigawattora, progetti in lista d'attesa, progetti fermi.

Io vedo un'autonomia energetica, quello che deve essere il nostro obiettivo primario, in pericolo, perché la dipendenza dalle tecnologie e dall'importazione di materie prime purtroppo è una fase che in questo momento storico non stiamo riuscendo a superare.

Poi, bene finalmente le aperture per quanto riguarda il nucleare, ma io vi invito ad evitare le guerre al gas. Noi abbiamo gli stoccaggi al minimo, almeno per quanto riguarda gli ultimi quindici anni e abbiamo pressione sui prezzi. Il rischio è che per questo inverno, paradossalmente, il tema non sia quello legato alla scarsità del gas, ma il prezzo a cui l'Europa lo dovrà pagare per averlo.

Mniej ideologii, więcej własnej, taniej, stabilnej energii.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, "erreur stratégique": ce ne sont pas mes mots, ce sont ceux d'Ursula von der Leyen sur son choix de tourner le dos au nucléaire. Aujourd'hui, nous traversons un nouveau choc énergétique. Les factures flambent à nouveau: après la guerre en Ukraine, le détroit d'Ormuz et peut-être demain un GNL américain transformé en arme politique.

N'avons-nous toujours pas retenu la leçon, chers collègues? N'opposons pas une technologie à une autre. Nous avons besoin de toutes les énergies qui décarbonent: renouvelables, nucléaire, sur un pied d'égalité. Le cadre post-2030 doit mettre fin à des années de discrimination contre le nucléaire, une discrimination qui a scellé notre dépendance. Il ne faut pas une énième cible renouvelable, mais une cible d'énergie décarbonée; et une priorité absolue: électrifier massivement. Notre électricité est déjà largement bas carbone.
La solution, elle est donc là, sous nos yeux. À nous de la rendre réelle. Ne répétons pas d'erreurs stratégiques, portons une directive énergie propre, une directive décarbonation.

Und Überraschung – die hohen Preise von Trump und Putin kommen bei denen nicht an. Die Uhr tickt. Jede Sekunde kommt uns teuer zu stehen.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, Consiglio, Commissione, credo che per promuovere davvero l'energia pulita dovremmo applicare, senza altri ritardi, le norme già vigenti.

Un decennio fa, nell'ottava legislatura abbiamo ad esempio introdotto la flessibilità per consumare quando le rinnovabili producono, remunerando cittadini e imprese per il servizio alla rete, e poi l'autoconsumo, le comunità energetiche e la partecipazione attiva dei consumatori. Ma troppe opportunità restano ancora bloccate negli Stati membri e a livello europeo.

Nel 2017 ero relatore del regolamento sull'etichettatura energetica. Vi inserimmo gli apparecchi intelligenti per favorire la flessibilità e l'uso delle rinnovabili. Nove anni dopo, quella previsione attende ancora piena attuazione.

Commissione e Consiglio dovrebbero dare risposte chiare a un calendario vincolante. Questa hybris, questa continua iperproduzione legislativa non è un vantaggio. Nuove norme e cambi di rotta contraddittori confondono cittadini e investitori.

Non possiamo lamentare i limiti delle rinnovabili lasciando inutilizzati gli strumenti già previsti per superarli. Le norme ci sono. Iniziamo a far funzionare quelle, mentre scriviamo le nuove. Lo avessimo già fatto con decisione, oggi non saremmo in questa situazione.

interventions.speaker_label: Markus Buchheit, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kollegen! Die Kommission will ihren Anteil von Strom am Endenergieverbrauch bis 2040 verdoppeln. Europäische Industriebetriebe zahlen schon heute ungefähr doppelt so viel für Strom wie ihre amerikanische Konkurrenz. Und was das bedeutet, das sieht man in der Chemie. Seit 2022 wurde die Schließung von rund 9 Prozent der europäischen Produktionskapazität angekündigt. 20 000 direkte Arbeitsplätze sind weg. Neue Investitionen gehen gegen Null.

Auch Ihr Vorzeigeprojekt, der grüne Stahl, scheitert. ArcelorMittal hat in Bremen und Eisenhüttenstadt auf 1,3 Milliarden Euro Fördergeld verzichtet, weil der Strom dort schlicht und ergreifend zu teuer ist. Neue Elektroöfen baut der Konzern dort, wo Strom planbar ist, etwa in Frankreich, wo Kernkraft im Netz ist. Mit diesem Vorstoß wollen Sie saubere Energie in jeden europäischen Politikbereich einbauen. Für die Betriebe heißt das: mehr CO2-Kosten, mehr Nachweise, mehr Auflagen. Chemie und Stahl gehen zuerst, Maschinen, Industrie und Autos hängen an ihnen. Die Schornsteine stehen dann in China. Die Arbeitslosen bleiben hier bei uns in Europa. Das ist Ihre missverstandene Klimapolitik.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Senast Sverige styrdes av socialdemokrater och miljöpartister valde man att aktivt stänga ner fullt fungerande kärnkraft. Resultatet blev mindre fossilfri el och högre elpriser. Tappet blev så stort att vi helt i onödan fick elda olja för att hålla igång elsystemet: 140 000 liter i timman helt i onödan.

Nu har Sverige, med den moderatledda regeringen i spetsen, vänt på den här skutan och lagt grunden för ny kärnkraft. Resten av Europa borde göra samma sak. Vi behöver teknikneutrala EU-fonder som gynnar all ren energi. Vi behöver en europeisk satsning på de små modulära reaktorerna, så att Europa leder utvecklingen i stället för att halka efter. Och vi behöver snabbare tillstånd så att reaktorer som har godkänts i ett land inte behöver börja om från noll i nästa.
Kärnkraften är ren energi. Det är dags att EU behandlar den som det.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Госпожо Председател, за европейската индустрия цената на електроенергията определя дали ще има нови инвестиции или затворени производства. Развитието на чиста енергия, която включва възобновяеми източници и ядрена енергетика, трябва да носи реално конкурентно предимство. Това лято България показа как се постига това. Системите за съхранение запазваха слънчевата енергия за вечерните часове, когато търсенето е по-голямо, а цените са по-високи. Включването на рекорден брой батерии към енергийната ни система намали цените на тока с близо 40% през летните месеци в региона ни. Българският опит доказва как чистата енергия и новите технологии създават условия за икономически растеж.

Като основен преговарящ по регламента за трансевропейската енергийна инфраструктура настоявам да подкрепим този потенциал с модерни мрежи и по-добра свързаност. Нашата задача е да гарантираме ниски цени, но това да не е сезонно явление, а трайно предимство за европейската индустрия и гражданите.

paragraphs.text: Madam president, Commissioner, clean energy is not only solar and wind, it is every low-carbon source, including nuclear. I welcome the fact that nuclear is now in Brussels taken into account, and we are speaking openly much more about nuclear nowadays.

Ursula von der Leyen even called the move away from nuclear a strategic mistake. I agree, but the rules are several steps behind the rhetoric. In the EU taxonomy, which is key for investors, nuclear is still only a transitional activity with a deadline in 2045.

So I call on the Commission to give nuclear exactly the same status as the other clean sources. Just like geothermal plants, nuclear power plants produce electricity here in Europe, day and night, in every weather. In a turbulent world, they help us defend our independence.

My question to you is, if we go down this path again, where do we put the power plants and where do we put the waste? I am aware that these problems are smaller than 20 years ago, but they still exist. Would you be willing to have a plant or a waste place in your own constituency?

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Minister, Herr Kommissar! Ja, wir müssen unabhängig werden als Europäer, denn es ist eine Frage von Freiheit – unabhängig von Importen, von fossiler Energie, aber unabhängig auch von kritischen Rohstoffen, die von China getrustet werden. Und ja, wir müssen schneller werden im Ausbau von Energien, im Ausbau von Netzen. Und deswegen müssen unsere Genehmigungsverfahren deutlich beschleunigt werden. Ich unterstütze deswegen auch die Vorschläge der Kommission, dass wir hier richtig Gas geben an dieser Stelle.

Ich glaube auch, dass wir den Emissionshandel stärken müssen, denn der Emissionshandel ist das marktwirtschaftliche Instrument, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen, dafür, dass wir dekarbonisieren und dass wir unsere Energie fit machen für diese Zeit, wo wir nicht mehr abhängig sind von Importen, von fossilen Energien.

Ich möchte aber als Verkehrspolitiker auch sagen: Wir brauchen auch eine Strategie für flüssige Kraftstoffe. Warum? Weil wir sie brauchen im Luftverkehrsbereich, im maritimen Bereich, und ich habe den Eindruck, dass wir da manchmal etwas schwimmen in dieser Frage. Deswegen arbeiten Sie bitte daran, Herr Kommissar, dass wir eine Strategie für flüssige Kraftstoffe bekommen, damit wir resilient sind – auch in Fragen von Versorgungssicherheit. Und am Ende ist es auch eine Frage von Verteidigungsfähigkeit.

Frau Präsidentin, Herr Minister, Herr Kommissar! Ja, wir müssen unabhängig werden als Europäer, denn es ist eine Frage von Freiheit – unabhängig von Importen, von fossiler Energie, aber unabhängig auch von kritischen Rohstoffen, die von China getrustet werden. Und ja, wir müssen schneller werden im Ausbau von Energien, im Ausbau von Netzen. Und deswegen müssen unsere Genehmigungsverfahren deutlich beschleunigt werden. Ich unterstütze deswegen auch die Vorschläge der Kommission, dass wir hier richtig Gas geben an dieser Stelle.

Ich glaube auch, dass wir den Emissionshandel stärken müssen, denn der Emissionshandel ist das marktwirtschaftliche Instrument, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen, dafür, dass wir dekarbonisieren und dass wir unsere Energie fit machen für diese Zeit, wo wir nicht mehr abhängig sind von Importen, von fossilen Energien.

Ich möchte aber als Verkehrspolitiker auch sagen: Wir brauchen auch eine Strategie für flüssige Kraftstoffe. Warum? Weil wir sie brauchen im Luftverkehrsbereich, im maritimen Bereich, und ich habe den Eindruck, dass wir da manchmal etwas schwimmen in dieser Frage. Deswegen arbeiten Sie bitte daran, Herr Kommissar, dass wir eine Strategie für flüssige Kraftstoffe bekommen, damit wir resilient sind – auch in Fragen von Versorgungssicherheit. Und am Ende ist es auch eine Frage von Verteidigungsfähigkeit.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Herr kommissionsledamot. Politiker på högerkanten försöker hävda att de höjda levnadsomkostnaderna och höjda elpriser är klimatomställningens fel. Men inget kunde vara mer fel. Det är den förnybara energin som är den billigaste energin, och därför måste vi fortsätta bygga ut sol- och vindkraft snabbt.

Men det finns några som har förstått hur billig den här energin är och det är Google, Microsoft, Meta och andra stora techbolag som står på kö för att bygga stora datahallar där den billiga elen finns, bland annat i Sverige där jag bor. Den här utvecklingen måste vi ta på allvar i det här huset. För oss gröna är det självklart. Vi ska nå målet om 100 % förnybart och hushållen och industrin ska gå först. På så sätt håller vi nere elräkningarna, hjälper industrin i omställningen och säkerställer att jobben stannar kvar här.
Om vi tillåter techbolagen att etablera sig utan motkrav och utan hänsyn till hushållen och industrin, så riskerar vi en smäll längre fram. Och det är oacceptabelt för oss gröna.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Die Klimakrise erfordert radikale Klimaschutzmaßnahmen. Doch ein Wandel, bei dem die arbeitende Bevölkerung die Zeche zahlt, während die Umweltverschmutzer geschützt werden, ist kein gerechter Wandel und daher zum Scheitern verurteilt. Wir müssen die Emissionen tiefgreifend und schnell senken. Die Last darf jedoch nicht auf diejenigen fallen, die am wenigsten in der Lage sind, ihre Lebensumstände zu ändern. Ein Mieter kann seine Heizungsanlage nicht einfach austauschen. Eine Familie mit geringem Einkommen kann nicht einfach ein neues Elektroauto kaufen und ihr Haus sanieren. Wir müssen erschwingliche Alternativen bereitstellen und nicht nur einen Preis für Umweltverschmutzung festlegen.

Wenn der Industrie im Namen des Wandels öffentliche Gelder und kostenlose Emissionszertifikate gewährt werden, müssen die Beschäftigten im Gegenzug etwas dafür erhalten: echte und messbare Emissionssenkungen, gute Arbeitsplätze, Weiterbildung, Investitionen und eine bedeutende Rolle für die Gewerkschaften. Die Einnahmen aus dem Emissionshandelssystem sollten den Haushalten helfen, ihre Energiekosten zu senken und auf Elektroantriebe umzusteigen, und nicht einfach die Industrie subventionieren. Klimaschutz muss radikal sein. Deshalb muss er auch gerecht sein. Die Menschen, die am wenigsten zu dieser Krise beigetragen haben, dürfen nicht dazu gezwungen werden, dafür zu bezahlen.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, gasolio a 2,25 euro al litro e prezzi dell'energia elettrica ai massimi da anni. E noi stiamo ancora parlando di energia pulita? Ma l'unica cosa che avete pulito, signor Commissario, sono i portafogli dei nostri operai, agricoltori, pescatori e cittadini europei.

Ed è la stessa Commissione europea a certificare che, dal 1994, le emissioni globali di gas serra non hanno fatto altro che aumentare inesorabilmente. E l'Europa è l'unico continente che ha deciso deliberatamente di castrarsi in nome di un ambientalismo ideologico e aprendo le proprie porte alla Cina, svendendole la nostra sovranità industriale.

Avete fallito e continuate a fallire oggi, signor Commissario, concedendo flessibilità economica solamente per energia verde e armi, che non mi sembra siano tanto ecologiche. L'unica energia di cui abbiamo bisogno, signor Commissario, è quella disponibile e conveniente. Ed è proprio quella che ci chiedono oggi a gran voce i cittadini che ci hanno eletto.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, the government of my country, Cyprus, has failed its citizens, and now we are paying one of the highest bills of electricity. For years, the Cypriot Government has not managed to import natural gas and it has failed to get enough batteries for renewable energy. So basically we are now dependent on fossil fuels. This means that 20 % of electricity bills goes just to pay CO2 emissions through the EU emissions trading system.

Don't get me wrong – protecting the planet is extremely important. But during this crisis, we must protect first our citizens. I ask the EU to step in and try to fix this problem, made by our government, by giving us an emergency relief. We need to pay less for CO2 emissions during this energy crisis, because Cypriot citizens can just not afford it.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Ursula von der Leyen hat in diesem Haus zu Recht gesagt: „Wer fossile Energie importiert, importiert auch die Krisen und Preisschocks dieser Welt.“ Deswegen hat die Kommission wichtige Schritte auf den Weg gebracht. Aber unser Problem ist inzwischen nicht mehr nur die Richtung – auch wenn wir noch einen weiten Weg zu gehen haben – bei der Anerkennung von grünen Molekülen. Unser Problem ist insbesondere das Tempo.

Der Electrification Action Plan kam Monate später als angekündigt. Auf den neuen europäischen Rahmen für Versorgungssicherheit warten wir noch immer. Und bei Wasserstoff warten Investoren immer noch auf verlässliche Bedingungen. Und die europäische Fusionsstrategie ist angekündigt, während andere Weltregionen längst vorangehen. Und bei den Netzen sind wir immer noch in den Verhandlungen des Grids Package, und wichtige Networkcodes sind noch nicht fertig. Dabei warten bereits heute sechsmal mehr erneuerbare Kapazitäten auf einen Netzanschluss, als wir in einem Jahr neu bauen.

Europa hat also viele richtige Pläne. Aber jetzt müssen aus den Plänen endlich Leitungen werden und aus Strategien, Investitionen und aus Ankündigungen endlich bezahlbare Energie. Also: weniger ankündigen, mehr umsetzen und jetzt gemeinsam Gas geben – beim Tempo und nicht beim Gasverbrauch.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, we're looking at a very expensive winter. It's not only because we need to buy Christmas presents for our loved ones; it's because we're paying a high price in energy and a high price in electricity in particular.

Some colleagues here are saying that the solution is to start importing gas from Russia or start importing more oil and gas from the Middle East. It's absolutely crazy to my mind because we don't have the oil and gas ourselves. We need to import all of it – 98 % of the gas and oil that we consume in Europe we import from abroad. Why not invest in our own renewable energy? We should do that.

By the way, we should also make sure that the permitting, when you want to build a set up a wind turbine or transmission grid, becomes much faster than today. We are right now negotiating a permitting reform, making sure that we can get the wind turbines and the grids at a much faster pace. We need to work together on that on our own renewable energy, rather than sending the money abroad.

paragraphs.text: I don't know about the specific case in Poland that you are referring to, but I do know that Poland is investing a big amount in renewable energy, and I think that that is indeed a very wise decision.

I think that when you do this and you invest in renewable energy – when you build solar panels, wind energy, other forms of renewable energy – you need to make sure that the local communities get a share of the benefits. paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, Commissievoorzitter Von der Leyen was in haar State of the Union zeer duidelijk. Kernenergie is schone energie. En u, commissaris, trad haar daarstraks bij. De Europese bocht ten aanzien van kernenergie is eindelijk ingezet, maar hij is nog niet helemaal genomen, want het concrete Europese beleid blijft er nog een beetje achterop hinkelen.

Daarom vandaag drie oproepen: vooreerst, stel Europese fondsen ook open voor kernenergie. Het volgende MFK moet expliciet openstaan voor alle netzerotechnologieën. paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, 100 mil milhões de euros: foi este o preço que a Europa pagou a mais este ano em combustíveis fósseis por causa do conflito no Médio Oriente. Repito, 100 mil milhões de euros. Dinheiro europeu a financiar instabilidade que não controlamos, dependência que não queremos e uma fatura que as famílias não merecem pagar.

Mas é possível fazer diferente. Portugal mostra que há outro caminho. Até agosto, 74 % da eletricidade produzida em Portugal veio de fontes renováveis. O vento, o sol e a água, com o nosso conhecimento e inovação, estão a transformar a economia portuguesa, a baixar os custos e a criar emprego.

A energia produzida na Europa que poderia ser consumida não só em Portugal, se já tivéssemos as interconexões energéticas a funcionar. Numa Europa que demasiadas vezes chega tarde, na energia limpa somos ainda líderes globais. Não podemos desperdiçar esta vantagem. O eSAF, o combustível sustentável para a aviação, é o próximo passo.

Precisamos de uma autonomia estratégica que não dependa do Golfo Pérsico. Mas a transição energética não pode ficar nos discursos deste Parlamento, tem de chegar à fatura de cada família europeia. Cada euro investido em energia limpa é 1 € que fica na Europa, que cria emprego, que reduz a dependência e que protege os cidadãos da volatilidade dos mercados fósseis.
A escolha é simples: continuamos a pagar a fatura dos outros ou investimos no nosso próprio futuro?

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, ¿cuántas evidencias más necesitan los negacionistas climáticos o los vasallos de Trump? Nuestra dependencia fósil la pagamos doblemente: con miles de vidas perdidas por el cambio climático y con continuas crisis que destrozan nuestra economía y nuestra competitividad.

Europa necesita una trayectoria ambiciosa con un objetivo vinculante de renovables para 2040, acompañado de objetivos de eficiencia energética y electrificación. Hay que dar certidumbre a los inversores en tecnología verde. Las renovables son la opción más limpia, más barata y más rápida: el sol, el viento, el agua, la geotermia, el hidrógeno... —el hidrógeno verde, sí, el H2, no el nitrógeno, que el líder del PPE en mi país, Feijóo, la lía parda con esto—. Toda la energía limpia es bienvenida.

Pero nuestra prioridad debe ser clara: el criterio principal debe ser la eficiencia en costes, dar prioridad a tecnologías asequibles que podemos desplegar ya para hacer frente a esta crisis fósil —que no sabemos cuánto va a durar— y para abaratar la energía en un futuro cercano.
¿Objetivo de renovables a 2040? Por supuesto.

Energia curată nu este un scop în sine. Trebuie să fie curată, trebuie să fie accesibilă și disponibilă oricând. Altfel este doar o lozincă scumpă. Vrem o Europă curată, dar nu cu prețul distrugerii industriei europene. Lăsați fiecare stat să-și aleagă mixul energetic. paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Komisarzu! Jeśli nie wygramy konkurencji gospodarczej z Chinami i z Ameryką, to zamiast zielonej Europy będziemy mieć zielony skansen. Dlaczego tak mówię? Kilka faktów. 8 paneli fotowoltaicznych na 10 jest produkowanych w Chinach. Prąd dla fabryk w Europie jest dwa razy droższy niż prąd dla fabryk w Ameryce. Wszyscy wiemy, dlaczego tak jest, ale co z tym zrobić, to już nie bardzo.

Europejski przemysł alarmuje o nieuczciwej konkurencji z Chin i o potężnym wsparciu państwowym dla tamtejszych producentów. Więc pytam szanownego pana komisarza, jak europejskie firmy mają konkurować tu i teraz. Bo co do przyszłości, to z panem komisarzem się zgadzam, ale tu chodzi o wygranie konkurencji tu i teraz. Nie możemy dać się wykiwać Chińczykom. Chińska firma dostaje od państwa nawet 8 razy więcej pomocy niż firma z Zachodu. Jak z tym wygrać?

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, tutte le discussioni di questi mesi ci portano alla stessa conclusione: la decarbonizzazione, così cruciale per competitività, autonomia e sicurezza, non si può realizzare con 27 strategie nazionali separate.

Sono tantissime le cose che i singoli Stati avrebbero già dovuto fare e che possono fare da ora. Alcuni stanno andando nella direzione giusta, altri purtroppo no. Basta guardare chi paga le bollette più alte. Ma anche sommando gli sforzi nazionali, nel medio periodo non faremo il salto di qualità necessario per raggiungere gli obiettivi industriali e climatici al 2040, senza un salto in avanti nel processo di coesione.

Servono una strategia energetica comune, più interconnessioni, un vero mercato unico, una governance dell'Unione che funzioni anche contro le speculazioni. Reti rinnovabili e elettrificazione richiedono infrastrutture e investimenti con una dimensione europea. NextGenerationEU ci ha dimostrato che possiamo farlo. Dobbiamo aprire una stagione permanente di investimenti comuni. La dichiarazione è chiarissima: non abbiamo bisogno di meno Europa, ma di un'Europa più forte, più coesa e più determinata.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor comisario, defendemos las renovables, y Europa debe seguir avanzando. Pero instalarlas no basta; hay que poder llevar esa energía donde se necesita. Miren a España: somos líderes en renovables, pero cerca del 90 % de la red está saturada. Fábricas y viviendas piden conexión y la respuesta es no.

Mientras, este verano tiramos la electricidad que consumen 4 millones de hogares y, cuando cae el viento, en España hay que parar a la industria electrointensiva para salvar el sistema siete veces en diez semanas.

Esto no es una transición, señor comisario, es un sistema descoordinado. Se ha invertido en generar, pero no en conectar. Y se quieren cerrar las nucleares justo cuando más falta hacen, cuando necesitamos todas las tecnologías. Europa no necesita más objetivos. Lo que necesita es poder construir lo que ya ha decidido: redes e interconexiones como prioridad; permisos rápidos; una electricidad que no pague más impuestos que el gas, y una energía nuclear que cuente como lo que es, energía limpia. Por tanto, hay que dar marcha atrás en el cierre de las centrales nucleares en España.

paragraphs.text: Efectivamente, hay que encontrar ese equilibrio entre más renovables y más agricultura y respetar nuestro medio ambiente. Ese es el equilibrio que hay que encontrar.

Pero el ejemplo claro es en España, donde tenemos capacidad de energía solar y eólica; donde tenemos capacidad instalada y no somos capaces de llevar toda esa energía a nuestras plantas y viviendas y hacer que la energía sea más barata. Por lo tanto, sí, tenemos que avanzar en renovables siempre que sea encontrando ese equilibrio, respetando el medio ambiente y a las comunidades locales, pero sobre todo invertir en red, porque es lo que necesitamos. Si no, nunca vamos a tener energía limpia, barata y segura como la que estamos pidiendo aquí hoy.

paragraphs.text: Cara Presidente, caros colegas, ao contrário do que diz a extrema‑direita, a culpa dos preços da energia não é das energias renováveis, é do amigo que tanto defendem, Donald Trump. Como a União Europeia importa hoje mais de 50 % dos combustíveis fósseis, a transição verde não é o problema. Já teria sido a solução se já tivéssemos avançado. Por isso, senhor Comissário, precisamos, sim, de eletrificar, de eletrificar rapidamente, e de levar os benefícios aos cidadãos. Isso significa acelerar o licenciamento para a produção eólica e solar, mas não só.

Hoje, em Portugal, muitas famílias deparam-se com uma crise dos combustíveis, como em toda a Europa, e nós precisamos de avançar com soluções para aqueles que mais precisam. É por isso que eu gostava que a Comissão propusesse um plano europeu de leasing. Significa utilizar os apoios públicos para que o cidadão comum possa ter um carro elétrico a prestações acessíveis. Seria uma vitória a toda a linha, uma vitória para a nossa indústria, uma vitória para a Europa produzir menos emissões e uma vitória para os portugueses e para os europeus, que pagariam muito, mas muito menos, agora e no futuro, na conta energética.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, Mario Draghi caused a bit of a panic when he proposed to build a competitive European economy based on energy independence, because he priced it at a cost of around EUR 800 billion of annual investments. But at current prices, we will be spending at least EUR 500 billion this year alone in buying fossil fuels outside of Europe, and probably another EUR 100 billion to subsidise them in several Member States, so there are people who can actually afford to drive their cars and heat their homes. And still, while reality stares them in the face and money bleeds from our citizens' pockets, some in this Parliament rail against the dying of fossil fuels and would rather buy more gas from Vladimir Putin. They are like the 15th century scribes in Paris who actually blocked the introduction of the printing press for two decades. They fight the inevitable, and so in the end, they will lose.

But the question is, how much longer will it take for a broad majority in this Parliament to choose the obvious and clean way out of this dead end? Because, colleagues, it's not the technology that we lack. It's not the money that we lack. What we need most of all is to stop hesitating, do the inevitable, speed it up, build these new networks, build these new opportunities and offer a better future to our citizens.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Vad kostar torka? Vad kostar översvämning? Vad kostar skogsbrand efter skogsbrand? Vad kostar stormar? Vad kostar extremvärme? Vad kostar det att sitta i knä på diktaturer? Vad kostar förstörda skördar? Vad kostar en förlust i kapplöpningen om de nya jobben i industrin?

Jag hade ett annat tal förberett, men så hör jag extremhögern här inne prata om kostnader för att bygga saker, för att investera. Men vad är kostnaden för att avstå? Djup arbetslöshet, högre matpriser, högre elpriser, ökat beroende av stater som inte delar vår syn på demokrati. paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, geschätzter Herr Kommissar! Beim Thema Energie war Europa viel zu lange in der Zuschauerrolle. Wir haben es uns bequem gemacht und die Abhängigkeiten von fossilen Energieträgern einfach akzeptiert. Die Folgen dieser Politik sind nach dem russischen Angriff auf die Ukraine und zuletzt durch den Krieg im Iran für alle schmerzlich spürbar geworden. Es ist höchste Zeit, dass sich Europa endgültig aus diesen Abhängigkeiten löst und damit nicht nur Versorgungssicherheit, sondern auch eine verstärkte Preisstabilität im Energiebereich anstrebt.

Was brauchen die Menschen und die Unternehmen in Europa? Nämlich einen langfristigen Schutz vor neuen Teuerungswellen und vor neuen Wettbewerbsnachteilen. Das alles kann aber nur gelingen, wenn wir uns endlich richtig auf den Ausbau erneuerbarer Energieträger fokussieren. Denn das ist der einzige Weg und die einzige Form der Energiegewinnung, die Europa unabhängiger machen kann. Deshalb muss unser gesamter Gestaltungswille in die weitere Elektrifizierung aller Sektoren, den Ausbau der europäischen Energienetze und natürlich den Ausbau erneuerbarer Energieträger fließen.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, qui est responsable de la hausse critique du prix de l'énergie? Qui oblige les Européens à choisir entre travailler et remplir le frigo? Qui pousse les PME à la faillite? Qui va empêcher des millions de familles de se chauffer cet hiver? Poutine, Trump, Khamenei? Bien sûr, mais il y a aussi dans cet hémicycle des coupables. Ce sont ceux qui, texte après texte, empêchent l'Union européenne d'accomplir sa transition énergétique, sacrifiant les générations futures au profit, et dans l'esprit de gains électoraux mesquins, en retardant le solaire, l'éolien, les véhicules électriques, les voitures propres, en refusant l'arrêt des subventions aux énergies fossiles, en supprimant la responsabilité sociale et environnementale des entreprises.

Tant que nos modes de consommation, de production et de déplacement ne seront pas décarbonés, nous continuerons de subir de plein fouet les conséquences de la dépendance du pétrole. Alors nous nous battrons pour que le prochain budget européen dégage des moyens pour la transition. Et pour financer le mur d'investissements à venir, nous ne connaissons pas d'autres solutions qu'un nouvel emprunt commun sur les décennies à venir. Cette option viendra sur la table tôt ou tard, parce que c'est la seule réponse à la hauteur des difficultés que connaissent nos concitoyens.

Ce sont ceux qui, texte après texte, empêchent l'Union européenne d'accomplir sa transition énergétique, sacrifiant les générations futures au profit, et dans l'esprit de gains électoraux mesquins, en retardant le solaire, l'éolien, les véhicules électriques, les voitures propres, en refusant l'arrêt des subventions aux énergies fossiles, en supprimant la responsabilité sociale et environnementale des entreprises.

Tant que nos modes de consommation, de production et de déplacement ne seront pas décarbonés, nous continuerons de subir de plein fouet les conséquences de la dépendance du pétrole. Alors nous nous battrons pour que le prochain budget européen dégage des moyens pour la transition. Et pour financer le mur d'investissements à venir, nous ne connaissons pas d'autres solutions qu'un nouvel emprunt commun sur les décennies à venir. Cette option viendra sur la table tôt ou tard, parce que c'est la seule réponse à la hauteur des difficultés que connaissent nos concitoyens.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, quand on parle d'énergie propre comme vient de le faire M. Germain, on parle prioritairement ici, malheureusement, d'éolien ou de solaire. Alors l'Allemagne a fait ce pari jusqu'au bout, en abandonnant carrément le nucléaire. On va faire le bilan: leur production électrique émet jusqu'à huit fois plus de gaz à effet de serre que la France, et ils ont une électricité presque deux fois plus chère, parce qu'ils compensent l'intermittence de leurs éoliennes par du gaz et du charbon ultra-polluant.

En France, des idéologues comme M. Germain ont commencé à faire la même chose il y a 25 ans. On va faire le bilan: on a mis près de 100 milliards d'euros sur la table pour le renouvelable. L'électricité coûtait 0,11 € le kilowattheure en 2005, 0,20 € en 2025: deux fois plus. On produisait 569 térawatts-heures avec 80 % de nucléaire en 2005. En 2025, on est descendu à 540 térawatts-heures. Et encore, heureusement qu'on a gardé 70 % de nucléaire. Ce qui n'empêche pas les macronistes de continuer de manière absurde à soutenir les éoliennes. Et je ne parle même pas de LFI, des Verts et encore à l'instant du PS avec M. Germain qui, eux, s'opposent carrément au nucléaire.
On veut tous électrifier la France. Vous avez raison. Mais certains veulent donc le faire en produisant moins d'électricité et en la rendant plus chère. C'est un suicide énergétique. C'est...

paragraphs.text: Si vous n'aviez pas abandonné le nucléaire depuis 25 ans, on aurait eu beaucoup de réacteurs, s'il n'y avait pas eu ce plan de descendre à 50 % la part du nucléaire – sous, justement, François Hollande –, s'il n'y avait pas eu un abandon des investissements, eh bien nos réacteurs auraient pu être prolongés, Fessenheim n'aurait pas été abandonnée et nos centrales nucléaires seraient plus efficaces. Donc effectivement, on a pris du retard.

Il faut maintenir les réacteurs actuels en investissant encore pour qu'ils soient en capacité de produire comme ils l'ont fait dans le passé. paragraphs.text: Poštovana predsjedavajuća, dobar dio ove rasprave odnosio se na nuklearnu energiju, da je ona na neki način bila diskriminirana u odnosu na obnovljive izvore energije. I ja se slažem da se treba ići i tim putem i da je bila doista strateška greška odustati u nekim zemljama od nuklearne energije, ali bih se želio opet vratiti na to da nije samo nuklearna energija, da su i neki oblici obnovljivih izvora energije isto tako bili zanemareni.

I zato ću se vratiti na važnost geotermalne energije. Mislim da nam i ona treba, pogotovo ako gledamo da ona može biti rješenje za grijanje i hlađenje. Kada gledamo da se baš u tome oko 50 % naših energetskih potreba odnosi u Europi, a imamo geotermalnu energiju koju nismo dovoljno iskoristili.
Zato još jednom pozivam Komisiju da objavi taj akcijski plan. Znam da su puno radili na tome i u dobrom smjeru. Vrijeme je da se to objavi.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, kalliit energian hinnat kurittavat kansalaisia. Yksi suuri raipanheiluttaja kansalaisille on viime vuosina ollut vihervasemmisto ja heidän energiapolitiikkansa. Olisiko teidän vihdoin aika myöntää tuuli- ja aurinkovoiman mahdottomuus toimia vakaana energiakivijalkanamme?

Todellinen energiakivijalka on olemassa, mutta sitä te olette iät ja ajat halunneet murentaa ja jopa konkreettisesti purkaa. Puhun ydinvoimasta. Se on varmaa ja säästä riippumatonta energiantuotantoa. Suomessa ydinvoimaan on nojattu jo noin 50 vuotta, ja se tuottaa lähes 40 prosenttia Suomessa käytettävästä sähköstä. Ydinvoiman elinkaaripäästöt ovat jopa pienemmät kuin aurinkovoimalla, joten aletaan vain edistämään puhdasta energiaa EU-politiikassa, niin kuin nyt vaaditaan. Edistetään ydinvoimaa.

paragraphs.text: Vážená pani predsedajúca, vy snáď nevidíte, že máme najdrahší benzín a naftu na celom svete? Naozaj nevidíte ten prudký nárast energií? Nevidíte to, že ľudia majú extrémne drahé bývanie, extrémne drahé potraviny? Nežijete v Európe? Nevidíte migračnú krízu, energetickú krízu, ekonomickú krízu, vojnovú krízu? Veď to všetko sú výsledky vašich zelených progresívnych ľavicových politík. A potom sem prídete a poviete: musíme pokračovať, odstrihnúť sa od fosílnych palív, zaviesť úplne čisté energie, nové emisné normy, zakázať autá so spaľovacími motormi, zdaniť naše bývania, ľudí, ešte viac zaviesť systém ETS 2, aby ľudia platili ďalšie emisné dane za svoje vykurovania. A potom tu všetci budete asi lietať na nejakých automobiloch alebo jazdiť bicyklom. Veď vy žijete v rozprávkach. Vy nežijete v realite, vy ničíte Európu a jediné, čo si ľudia aktuálne prajú, je zastaviť vás konečne, vrátiť do Európy zdravý rozum a vrátiť sa k tomu, čo funguje v normálnej technologickej neutralite. Využívajme to, čo funguje a čo tu po stáročia budovali naši predkovia.

paragraphs.text: Fru Formand! Der kører en eller anden helt vild højrefløjs smædekampagne. Som om det er sol, vind og de vedvarende energikilder, der er dyre eller ustabile.

Men ved I, hvad der virkelig er dyrt og ustabilt? Det er da at lade benzinprisen styres af om Hormuzstrædet er åbent eller lukket. Det er ingen i Europa tjent med. Det er dyrt, og det er ustabilt at være dybt afhængig af Putins gas for at varme boligerne i Europa op. Det er ingen af os tjent med.

Så hvis man virkelig vil vores kontinent det godt, skal man kæmpe for mere grøn energi, mere europæisk produceret energi, og at vi kan gøre det til gode priser både for virksomheder og for borgere. Hvis vi vil styrke vores konkurrenceevne, skal vi ikke gå højrefløjens vej. Nej, vi skal gå den vej, vi godt kender. Vi skal have et elektrificeringsmål. Vi skal investere i vores grid. Vi skal investere i den industrielle dekarbonisering, og så skal vi sørge for at stå vagt om vores ETS og bruge det til at investere i det, vi ved, der er nødvendigt: at gå den grønne vej. Det er den vej, der kommer til at sikre både Europas borgere og vores konkurrenceevne.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you so much for a very good debate. No doubt, energy prices in Europe are too high – Professor Draghi also showed us that in his famous report. I like to joke that in some political offices on this planet you swear on the Bible when you start, but when I assumed my office, my colleagues and I had to swear on the Draghi report. And, of course, I'm joking, but also not joking. The Draghi report sends a very clear message to us: we need to bring our energy prices down, otherwise we cannot compete.

But it is also important to have a nuanced look at what that means, because just saying that our energy prices are two to three times higher than China and the US doesn't really give us the full picture. The fact of the matter is that energy in some Member States is quite cheap, while energy in others is very expensive. So saying that we have too high prices on average doesn't really make much sense. It's like saying if you have one foot in ice‑cold water and one foot in boiling‑hot water that actually you have your feet in lukewarm water. It does not make sense.

What we can see is that the countries in our Union that pay the least for their energy are the countries with the highest penetration of renewables, and, as a general rule, the ones that are best connected to neighbouring countries. The International Energy Agency estimates that we save more than EUR 30 billion per year on newly deployed renewables, so that is what comes on top of what we already have. Approximately the same amount, according to ACER, is what we save on being as connected as we are. So yes, we pay too much for our energy, but had we not had the energy union that we have and been as connected as we are, we would have paid far more.

So the answer for us is to deploy more renewables as fast as possible, help deploy more nuclear – this will take us a little bit longer, but new technologies like small modular reactors can become a part of the future solutions, especially if it's fourth generation and the waste problems and the safety problems are not the same as they may be today – and energy efficiency, which can help us, of course, bring down our consumption of fossil fuels already tomorrow, because these technologies can be deployed fast.

Now, another thing that's not 100 % correct is when people talk about an energy crisis. Yes, we do have an energy crisis, but actually it would be more correct to say we have a fossil energy crisis, because the main reason for us paying so much for our energy – and the main reason for us being in the middle of a huge crisis right now – is our dependency on fossil fuels. In an average year, we pay more than EUR 370 billion for imported fossil energy – in an average year. This year is unfortunately not an average year. Already now, since February, we've paid EUR 100 billion more for our energy than we normally do, without receiving one extra molecule of gas.

So whether you think the main purpose of our energy policy in Europe is to fight climate change, or you think it is to make sure that we are competitive, or you think it is to make sure that we have security of supply and thereby security as such, the answer is the same. We need to get rid of our dependency. We need to stop importing expensive polluting molecules, fossil molecules and instead use our own home-grown cheap, clean electrons.

Approximately the same amount, according to ACER, is what we save on being as connected as we are. So yes, we pay too much for our energy, but had we not had the energy union that we have and been as connected as we are, we would have paid far more.

So the answer for us is to deploy more renewables as fast as possible, help deploy more nuclear – this will take us a little bit longer, but new technologies like small modular reactors can become a part of the future solutions, especially if it's fourth generation and the waste problems and the safety problems are not the same as they may be today – and energy efficiency, which can help us, of course, bring down our consumption of fossil fuels already tomorrow, because these technologies can be deployed fast.

Now, another thing that's not 100 % correct is when people talk about an energy crisis. Yes, we do have an energy crisis, but actually it would be more correct to say we have a fossil energy crisis, because the main reason for us paying so much for our energy – and the main reason for us being in the middle of a huge crisis right now – is our dependency on fossil fuels. In an average year, we pay more than EUR 370 billion for imported fossil energy – in an average year. This year is unfortunately not an average year. Already now, since February, we've paid EUR 100 billion more for our energy than we normally do, without receiving one extra molecule of gas.

So whether you think the main purpose of our energy policy in Europe is to fight climate change, or you think it is to make sure that we are competitive, or you think it is to make sure that we have security of supply and thereby security as such, the answer is the same. We need to get rid of our dependency. We need to stop importing expensive polluting molecules, fossil molecules and instead use our own home-grown cheap, clean electrons.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you. This has been an excellent debate, and the Commissioner has set out many of his objectives and given us an overview of where things are going. We have heard different views across the Chamber, but I am confident that, together, we can deliver on many of the items that we are working on, and that will then result in an impact on citizens.

On the cleanliness of our energy supply and on the cost of our energy supply, we can deliver on an ambitious European Grids Package. This allows us to modernise our grids; it allows us to have faster permitting procedures. The European Council has expressed support for an ambitious electrification, using all net‑zero and low‑carbon solutions alongside investment in grid storage and interconnectors. Again, the Commissioner spoke very clearly about the impact on costs that they have, but also recognising different national characteristics. That has been a feature of the debate today, that there are different characteristics to this debate in different Member States.

The European Council's view on all of this accommodates those Member States that view nuclear energy as an important component of their own energy security. So, I am convinced of our ability to achieve the successful energy transition, to achieve electrification and, therefore, energy sovereignty. It has been a political wish for several years; now it is an urgent necessity.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, Commissioner Brunner, thank you very much for the invitation to take part in this debate. From the outset, we stand united in the fight against terrorism and all forms of violent extremism that promote radicalisation, hatred or values contrary to those enshrined in Article 2 of our Treaty.

The threat of radicalisation and Islamist extremism continues to be a priority for the European Union and its Member States. In this context, the Muslim Brotherhood organisation is clearly under growing scrutiny, even fuelling wider concerns in Europe about the role of foreign funding in supporting Islamist organisations and institutions. As of today, the Muslim Brotherhood is not listed as a terrorist organisation under Council Decision 2026/455 and is therefore not subject to the specific restrictive measures that apply to designated groups.

Nevertheless, the EU has various means to address the ways in which any network, whether formally designated as a terrorist organisation or not, can exploit financial channels to impose its agenda: the Anti-Money Laundering Authority Regulation, the Transfer of Funds Regulation, aligned with the dedicated Markets and Crypto Assets Regulation, to name just a few. For online terrorist content, the Terrorist Content Online Regulation requires any identified terrorist content online to be removed within the hour.

The EU also addresses radicalisation through its ProtectEU agenda, in particular by providing targeted support for those most at risk through a whole‑of‑society approach. For example, the EU Knowledge Hub on the Prevention of Radicalisation, with EUR 60 million in funding, connects over 6 000 practitioners and policymakers and provides guidance, tools, training and tailored operational support.

Other measures which require a joint effort include: to curtail undesirable foreign funding that may flow to extremist actors; to increase transparency of fund allocation by expanding the EU‑wide register of external funding for NGOs and civil society organisations, to strengthen information and intelligence‑sharing mechanisms between Member States and EU agencies.

In concluding, we should keep in mind that radicalisation in Europe is a multidimensional phenomenon. It spans a wide spectrum – from jihadist‑inspired violence to right‑wing, left‑wing and nihilistic violence – and each strand demands the same level of vigilance and response.
I look forward to the discussion.

interventions.speaker_label: Magnus Brunner, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Minister, honourable Members, before I start with the topic of the debate, let me say a few words on the meaning of this day, of 7 October. On this very day three years ago, Hamas terrorists carried out brutal terror attacks on Israel. Around 1 200 people lost their lives, and hundreds were taken hostage. Today we remember them. The European Union stands with all the people whose lives have been shattered since that fateful day – the victims and their families, the survivors, the hostages and those who waited for them. But remembrance also carries a responsibility. In the years since, we have seen anti-Semitism rise in Europe, and Jewish communities have felt less safe in places they have called home for generations. We cannot accept this. Jewish life belongs to Europe and it is our duty to protect it.

But, honourable Members, to the topic of the debate. Terror and violence, so often fuelled by extremism, are against everything this House stands for. Extremism advances gradually, and often also unnoticed, fuelled by online echo chambers and the rapid spread of false narratives. It also undermines the credibility of key institutions that are central to our democracies. It drives people to the fringes, one injustice, one video, one false certainty at a time.

It rarely begins with violence; it actually begins with the poisoning of the language, with the erosion of trust, and with the slow teaching of hatred. So, honourable Members, extremism is not to be confused with the legitimate exercise of freedoms, including the freedom of religion, including the freedom of thought and the freedom of expression. These are fundamental values at the core of the European Union, enshrined in our Treaties and in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. It is these values that make our continent more attractive than many others, because we have learned from our history and have created something better, but this is something extremists are trying to exploit.

Extremism begins where these freedoms are called into question or even rejected, where the equality of men and women is denied, and where the values of democracy are being called into question. That is where those who try to abuse these freedoms must be stopped. And let us be very clear – extremists cannot rely on freedom of expression to protect hate speech and incitement to hatred.

Honourable Members, in recent years, the terrorist threat linked to Islamist extremism in Europe has been associated with jihadist actors and ideas, and this also includes movements such as the Muslim Brotherhood and the networks surrounding it. We have to and we do take these concerns very seriously. Today, unfortunately, Member States still reach different conclusions on the role that the Muslim Brotherhood plays, because there are different standards applied in their assessment. Some focus on explicit links to violence or terrorism; others also examine activities considered potentially harmful to democratic resilience, to social cohesion, or to fundamental rights, even where they do not amount to criminal conduct. Yet, there is a broad agreement. You also mentioned, Minister, among Member States, the European Union can actually add value in preventing and in countering violent Islamist extremism and terrorism.

We set out the relevant measures in our recent ProtectEU agenda to prevent and counter terrorism, specifically measures for the prevention of radicalisation and violent extremism, measures against terrorist financing and undesirable foreign support, and measures against illegal content online. When it comes to the prevention of radicalisation and extremism, the EU Knowledge Hub on Prevention of Radicalisation supports Member States' practitioners with materials, on the one hand, and with expertise on the other hand. It also provides a forum for discussions. On terrorist financing, we are preparing the ground for a European financial transactions retrieval system to have a better possibility of identifying and preventing terrorist financial flows.

When it comes to the online dimension, when it comes to illegal content online, we have stepped up our work in the EU Internet Forum on identifying and removing content constituting radicalisation and violent extremism, with a special focus on better protecting children.

So, honourable Members, a strong Europe is not one that closes itself off. A strong Europe is confident in its values; it protects the believer and confronts, on the other hand, the extremists. It guarantees religious freedom and refuses, at the same time, to let that freedom become a cover for those who despise it. It defends its way of life, not by becoming less free, but by being firm and unflinching in the defence of freedom. So let us honour those we remember today by the way we act, by standing firm against hatred in all its forms, by building societies in which no child grows up believing that violence is actually a path to meaning, and by ensuring that never again is faith turned into a weapon.

interventions.speaker_label: Céline Imart, au nom du groupe PPE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Ministre, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, trois ans jour pour jour après les massacres du 7-Octobre, une question devrait nous hanter: combien de visages l'islamisme devra-t-il encore nous montrer avant que l'Europe cesse de lui opposer le même aveuglement?

L'entrisme islamiste ne commence pas toujours par le bruit des armes. Il commence par le sourire, la cravate bien nouée, le langage des droits de l'homme détourné. Il tue lorsqu'il le peut, mais il infiltre lorsqu'il ne le peut pas. Le rapport sur les Frères musulmans déclassifié par Bruno Retailleau a tiré la sonnette d'alarme. À l'Europe de l'entendre et de cesser de prendre sa complaisance pour de la tolérance.

Le FEMYSO incarne ce cheval de Troie élégant. On les a crus fréquentables. On a ouvert les salles, les financements, les institutions. Là où la violence fracasse les portes, l'entrisme attend qu'on les lui ouvre. Qui d'autre de mieux que la gauche pour tenir la poignée, au nom d'un antiracisme dévoyé et paralysé par le chantage et la stigmatisation? Cette semaine encore, dans ces murs, alors que notre Parlement préparait l'hommage aux victimes du 7-Octobre, Rima Hassan a profané les drapeaux israéliens et européens dressés pour cette mémoire. Ce n'est plus supportable.

Cessons d'appeler «dialogue» la naïveté. Cessons d'appeler «partenaire» celui qui cherche notre caution. Cessons d'appeler «représentative» une association parce qu'elle ponctue ses demandes de subvention par «diversité et inclusion». Pour la première fois, notre Parlement est appelé à regarder en face l'entrisme et l'influence des réseaux des Frères musulmans.

Je porte cette résolution pour défendre l'Europe, pour ceux qui ne reviendront pas, mais aussi pour la génération qui arrive et qui aura à vivre avec nos choix. L'Europe leur laissera un continent qui tient encore debout lorsqu'elle cessera d'être cette belle endormie qui croit que tous les loups arrivent en hurlant. À ceux dont la mémoire nous oblige, à ceux dont la promesse nous engage, nous le devons.

interventions.speaker_label: Chloé Ridel, au nom du groupe S&D.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, Madame Imart, une fois encore, vous vous alliez avec vos amis d'extrême droite pour nous imposer vos discours islamophobes – je n'ai pas d'autres mots –, cette fois sous couvert d'une résolution sur l'entrisme islamiste en Europe.

Les fondamentalismes religieux, soyons clairs, représentent tous une vraie menace. Leurs ingérences doivent être combattues, d'où qu'elles viennent. Mais, Madame Imart, vos arguments flous, votre obsession pour une seule forme d'entrisme et votre silence – ou devrais-je dire votre complaisance – face aux autres, ne sont que la traduction de votre volonté de désigner toujours les mêmes boucs émissaires. Où êtes-vous lorsqu'il faut combattre l'entrisme des organisations intégristes catholiques anti-avortement? Lorsque vos amis les invitent ici au Parlement pour y répandre des contre-vérités scientifiques et combattre l'une de nos libertés les plus fondamentales? Où êtes-vous lorsqu'il faut dénoncer l'entrisme trumpiste dans nos systèmes politiques, destiné à faire gagner des partis nationalistes en Europe?
