paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, a 1 de septiembre, veinte de los veintisiete Estados miembros no habían presentado su plan de restauración de la naturaleza, pero Pedro Sánchez sí, el alumno aventajado de Bruselas. ¿Y para qué tanta prisa? Pues para dictar desde un despacho a la gente del campo cómo deben de gestionar nuestros montes y nuestros ríos y, eso sí, asumir una factura que el propio MITECO cifra en casi 600 millones de euros al año hasta 2050.

Y yo me pregunto: entre tantos millones, ¿dónde están los millones de euros para infraestructuras hídricas? ¿Dónde están los millones de euros para políticas de desbroce y cortafuegos, pastoreo extensivo y gestión forestal que realmente protejan a nuestros pueblos de los incendios? ¿Dónde están las acciones concretas de apoyo a quienes sostienen el territorio y lo mantienen vivo? Porque, para obligaciones, restricciones y burocracia, sí que vemos páginas y páginas y páginas. Pero eso sí: cuando toca pagar la factura de todos sus delirios, ahí sí que tiran del bolsillo de la gente del campo y de fondos como, por ejemplo, la Política Agraria Común.

Señorías, yo creo que nuestros agricultores, ganaderos y pescadores no necesitan ni más burócratas, ni más legislación, ni que les expliquen su oficio. Necesitan una PAC fuerte, acceso al agua, señora Roswall, rentabilidad y libertad para producir.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, de natuur in Nederland herstelt. De otter, bever en zeehond zijn terug. Houtwal en patrijs sieren ons landschap. Dit komt niet door Brusselse decreten, maar door rentmeesterschap van boeren, vissers, jagers en gemeenschappen zelf.

De omstreden verordening natuurherstel zet ons platteland verder op slot. Deze wet stapelt zich bovenop de habitatrichtlijn, die dringend aan herziening toe is. Sinds 1992 is de juridisering tot in het absurde doorgeschoten. Nederland zit in de knel door zijn eigen stikstofdoelen, terwijl uw Commissie toekijkt. Ook elders in Europa zitten de landbouw, visserij, jacht, industrie, woningbouw en energievoorziening beklemd. De doelen voor 2030, 2040, 2050 vergen 150 000 tot 850 000 hectare extra, hetgeen ten koste gaat van Neerlands boeren, tuinders, burgers en familiebedrijven. Verplichtingen die straks pas in de rechtszaal vorm krijgen.
Red ons platteland, commissaris, herzie de verordening natuurherstel en de habitatrichtlijn met spoed voordat de economie en de democratie het onderspit delven.

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci, toto leto nám jasne ukázalo, že voda je limitom nášho prežitia. Nemáme jej dostatok a ak viem niečo povedať 100 percentne o obnove prírody a prírodných riešeniach, je to, že vracajú vodu do krajiny. Ak neveríte, choďte sa pozrieť na obnovené bobrovisko. Nielenže tam budete stáť po pás vo vode, ale tá voda bude hýriť životom, to bobrovisko bude voňať, spievať a bzučať. A nestálo to ani euro. Štáty naozaj zúfalo hľadajú tú vodu, kde ju nájsť, no akoby sa pozerali opačným, opačným smerom. Len 9 krajín si splnil svoju povinnosť a predložilo národné plány na obnovu prírody. To je nielen obrovská hanba. To je škandalózne. Túto krízu nedokážete vyrokovať za rokovacím stolom alebo v sálach pléna, plenárnych sálach. Túto krízu môžete vyriešiť len vo fyzickom svete. Preto vyzývam všetkých zúčastnených, začnite s obnovovaním. V opačnom prípade začnite s vysťahovaním. Destinácia Planéta B.

paragraphs.text: You mentioned that the beaver population is also increasing, but we see also, in fact, that with the increasing beaver population may also be a problem with already existing dams, because also due to our weather, we will have more floods.

paragraphs.text: The solutions to tackle the problems with beavers are already on the table. There are experts who can do that. You can lower the level of water. You can replace the beavers. In extreme cases, you can even cull the beavers. That's all possible. But these are no reasons for us to not see the benefits of beavers being present in our country and recovering all around Europe, because it's not only about reproducing the amounts of water, but also preventing the floods that you mentioned, and they are doing it in a multifunctional way, supporting biodiversity, storing carbon and creating a beautiful space that is not able to be there without beavers. So, go on beavers!

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Naturrestaurering, det här är det enskilt viktigaste vi kan göra för att begränsa den globala uppvärmningen, givetvis tillsammans med att skapa ett fossilfritt samhälle. Det handlar exempelvis om att skapa våtmarker som blir kolsänkor och faktiskt försvagar växthuseffekten. Det handlar också väldigt mycket om klimatanpassning, resiliens, och för Sveriges del, återigen, inte minst, våtmarkerna som ser till att följder av både skyfall och torka blir betydligt lindrigare.

Naturrestaurering, biologisk mångfald. Det är naturens eget försäkringsbolag, och försäkringar brukar vi vara villiga att betala för. Det är antagligen den bästa insatsen vi kan göra för att begränsa hotet av kommande torka och skogsbränder.

Men då måste verkligen naturrestaurering implementeras i alla länder. Än så länge är det bara nio länder som har svarat, och flera av dem, tyvärr är mitt hemland Sverige ett av dem, levererar dessutom alldeles för lite. Vi måste sätta fokus på detta, för det här är kärnan i hela klimatfrågan.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, collega’s, commissaris, Nederland heeft niet voor niets tegen de verordening natuurherstel gestemd. Nederland is na Malta het dichtstbevolkte land van de Europese Unie. Er moet ruimte en flexibiliteit zijn voor nationale omstandigheden. We hebben ruimte nodig voor defensie, wonen, onze economie, voedselzekerheid en water. De fysieke ruimteclaims die voortvloeien uit de verordening natuurherstel concurreren met onze voedselvoorziening, woningbouw en brede economie. De bindende percentages staan op gespannen voet met onze industrie en landbouw.
Daarom blijven wij als CDA pleiten voor flexibiliteit voor lidstaten om een gebiedsgerichte aanpak en benadering te kiezen.

We kunnen niet zonder gezonde natuur en we willen werken aan natuurherstel, maar wel binnen realistische en haalbare doelen. Als de doelen niet realistisch uitvoerbaar zijn, dan kunnen we deze wet onmogelijk implementeren in Nederland of juridische zekerheid bieden aan ondernemers, landbouwers en woningzoekenden.

De deadline van 1 september voor het indienen van natuurherstelplannen is door veel lidstaten niet gehaald. De volgende deadline van 1 september 2027 voor het indienen van definitieve plannen is dan ook erg krap. Daarom zouden wij willen pleiten voor een verlenging van de deadline en aan de Commissie willen vragen of flexibiliteit mogelijk is, zodat er kan worden gesproken over maatwerk en wat haalbaar is in een lidstaat.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, arvoisa komission jäsen, luonnon monimuotoisuuden edistäminen on tärkeää, mutta ennallistamisasetuksen toimeenpanossa on pidettävä järki mukana. Euroopan metsäisimmässä maassa tulee olemaan lähes miljardin euron kustannukset vuosittain.

Suomessa valtaosa metsistä on tavallisten kansalaisten yksityisessä omistuksessa. Meillä on sukupolvien kokemus metsien vastuullisesta uudistamisesta niin, että ne tarjoavat hyvinvointia myös tuleville sukupolville. Ennallistamista ei pidä tehdä metsänomistajien kustannuksella eikä omaisuuteen kajoamalla. Lähtökohtana on edelleen oltava vapaaehtoisuus, riittävä rahoitus ja yksityisen omaisuuden kunnioittaminen.

Jos puun saatavuutta rajoitetaan liikaa, seurauksena voi olla vähemmän työtä ja vähemmän arvonlisää. Liialliset rajoitukset hidastavat myös fossiilista irtautumista. Viimeistään nyt on löydettävä kustannustehokkaammat ennallistamistoimet ja tehtävä ne yhdessä maa- ja metsänomistajien kanssa. Onko komissio valmis tähän?

Uważam, że najlepiej to zrobią państwa członkowskie ze swoimi ekspertami, specjalistami i leśnikami, którzy najlepiej znają specyfikę swoich ekosystemów, wiedzą, jak je chronić i jak nimi zarządzać. I po prostu trzeba ich wspierać, im na to pozwolić.

Jak można stosować jedno podejście do wszystkich krajów członkowskich, skoro różnią się one zarówno warunkami przyrodniczymi, strukturą własności, jak i sposobem gospodarowania. Szefowa Komisji Europejskiej powtarzała: mniej biurokracji. A co państwo robią? Proponujecie jeszcze więcej biurokracji i nie wiadomo, kto za nią zapłaci. Pytanie do Komisji: w jaki sposób Komisja będzie oceniała krajowe plany, na podstawie jakiej metodologii, na podstawie jakich danych, skoro część metodologii dotyczących poziomów ustalania nie została jeszcze przyjęta? Proszę państwa, ani nie wiecie, jak to zrobić, ani nie wiecie, jak za to zapłacić...

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Madame le Commissaire, cet été l’Europe a séché sous des chaleurs inédites, et les incendies ont ravagé des dizaines de milliers d’hectares de forêt. Bien sûr le réchauffement climatique est la source principale de ces épisodes extrêmes, mais pas seulement.

En excluant l’homme de la nature, en le présentant comme un prédateur plutôt que comme un gestionnaire, la philosophie de ces réglementations se trompe. Elle se trompe, interdisant parfois les réserves d’eau nécessaires à l’irrigation en été. Elle se trompe en s’opposant au nettoyage des forêts ou à la mise en place de coupe-feu. Elle se trompe si elle considère l’homme comme une menace.

Le chasseur, le paysan, le berger ont façonné et entretenu depuis des siècles des paysages de notre nature dont on veut les exclure depuis quelques années. Ce sont pourtant eux qui aiment, chérissent et connaissent le mieux ses bruits et ses odeurs, ses fureurs et ses fragilités, ses cycles et ses habitudes.
La restauration de la nature doit commencer par la restauration de la place de l’homme au sein de celle-ci, pour la recevoir, la conserver, la contraindre, parfois, et enfin la transmettre.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Frau Kommissarin, geschätzte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Mit 1. September mussten die Mitgliedstaaten ihre nationalen Wiederherstellungspläne nach Brüssel schicken. Österreich hat hier vorbildlich gearbeitet und hat einen ersten Plan geliefert. Die Europäische Kommission hat nicht geliefert, wenn es darum geht, einen Finanzierungsbericht zu liefern, und dafür hätte sie schon über ein Jahr Zeit gehabt.

Und jetzt stehen wir in dieser Lage, dass wir mit einer Umsetzung beginnen sollen, aber absolut keine Idee herrscht, wie hier Finanzierung stattfinden wird. Ich bin viel unterwegs in unserem Land, und ich werde viel gefragt, wie hier Maßnahmen umgesetzt werden sollen, wie hier erreicht werden soll, dass nicht unsere Bäuerinnen und Bauern die Maßnahmen zahlen müssen, wo ohnehin schon von der Europäischen Kommission Pläne vorgelegt wurden, wo ein Agrarbudget eher gekürzt wird als hochgerechnet oder besser aussieht.

Sie haben jetzt die Chance, vielleicht noch einmal klarer darauf einzugehen, wie die Finanzierung wirklich ausschauen wird – wird es von Ihnen noch einen klaren Plan geben? – bzw. wie Sie auch dazu stehen, was mein Kollege Herbert Dorfmann angesprochen hat, ob man es nicht besser um ein paar Jahre verschieben sollte, bis hier Klarheit herrscht. Es wird schon Natur wiederhergestellt. Viele Programme gibt es schon, aber ich glaube, das ist nicht unbedingt das Richtige dazu.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Allein angesichts von immer mehr Dürren, Hitzewellen und Überschwemmungen muss der Natur wieder mehr Raum gegeben und ihr höchste Priorität eingeräumt werden. Deshalb ist es kurzsichtig, wenn Mitgliedstaaten sagen: Die Umsetzung der Wiederherstellungsverordnung ist uns zu teuer. Denn wenn wir heute unsere Wälder, Moore, Flüsse und Wiesen nicht erhalten, werden die Folgekosten durch Hochwasser, Hitze, Dürre und Ernteausfälle um ein Vielfaches höher sein. Und diese Kosten können wir uns nicht leisten.

In zwei Wochen trifft sich die Welt zur Biodiversitätskonferenz in Armenien. Wenn Europa dort eine Führungsrolle beim Schutz der biologischen Vielfalt einnehmen möchte, kann ich nur sagen: Leadership beginnt zu Hause. Wir können von anderen keine ambitionierten Maßnahmen verlangen und gleichzeitig unsere eigenen Beschlüsse verzögern. Deshalb: Der Schutz der Natur muss jetzt konsequent umgesetzt werden. Denn Naturschutz bedeutet nicht nur, Pflanzen und Tiere zu schützen, sondern auch unsere Gesundheit, unsere Landwirtschaft, unsere Wirtschaft und die Lebensqualität kommender Generationen.

paragraphs.text: Господин Председател, Регламентът относно възстановяването на природата е един от ключовите стълбове на Европейския съюз не само за опазването на биологичното разнообразие и за предотвратяването на най-тежките последици от климатичните промени. Той е от съществено значение за продоволствената сигурност, здравето и общото благосъстояние на европейските граждани.

За България правилното прилагане на този регламент е от изключителна важност, тъй като 44% от територията на страната е защитена, има 92 защитени местообитания. Освен това България е една от малкото страни членки, които вече са изготвили национални програми за възстановяване съгласно изискванията на регламента. В тази връзка оценката на Комисията за финансовите нужди за пълното прилагане на регламента закъснява с повече от година. В същото време в предложението за новата бюджетна рамка на Европейския съюз отсъства целта 10% от бюджета да се отделя за биологично разнообразие и не предвижда програмата LIFE като инструмент за финансиране на дейности в областта на околната среда и климатичните промени.
Призовавам Европейската комисия да предприеме необходимите действия, за да гарантира, че поставените цели няма да останат само на хартия.

Той е от съществено значение за продоволствената сигурност, здравето и общото благосъстояние на европейските граждани.

Призовавам Европейската комисия да предприеме необходимите действия, за да гарантира, че поставените цели няма да останат само на хартия.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, vorige maand presenteerde mevrouw Von der Leyen hier in de plenaire met heel veel bravoure een heus pact tegen goldplating, d.w.z. onnodige nationale eisen bovenop Europese voorschriften. Vandaag gaat het over de Europese natuurwetgeving. Als er ergens sprake is van goldplating, dan is het wel hier.

Mijn land, Nederland, heeft in het verleden onnodig veel versnipperde natuurgebiedjes aangemerkt als Natura 2000-gebieden. Ik voorzie dat Nederland ook nu in zijn definitieve natuurherstelplan allerlei extra’s gaat inbouwen.

Mijn oproep aan de Commissie is eigenlijk heel eenvoudig: ga daadwerkelijk aan de slag met dat aangekondigde pact tegen goldplating. Ga met lidstaten om de tafel. Bied lidstaten bijvoorbeeld de mogelijkheid om terug te komen op eerdere aanwijzingen van Natura 2000-gebieden. Help lidstaten om met realistische natuurherstelplannen te komen. En houd daarbij ook voldoende rekening met de verschillen tussen lidstaten qua bevolkingsdichtheid.

paragraphs.text: Not funding the Nature Restoration Law, Minister, would be a fundamental breach of trust, and it would be a fundamental betrayal to the aims and principles of what the Nature Restoration Law is trying to do, which is repair nature across Europe. I am very concerned that there is no real recognition of the need to fund this particular programme. If you look at the MFF and the national and regional plans from across the country and the proposals put forward by the Commission, it simply doesn't give me any confidence that there will be funding in place to ensure that the voluntary aspects of this particular worthy law will be implemented.

We sold this on good faith across this particular House – right across – on the view that first it would be voluntary, but it also would be funded, so it is now an obligation on the Council to come forward with proposals in the MFF that will underpin what this is about, which is restoring nature.

Commissioner, just very briefly on Article 8, which provides flexibility for urban areas, I hope that you look at this again to make sure it doesn't inhibit house developments during a time of crisis.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, foreste, pascoli, zone umide e impollinatori sono alcuni di quei soggetti naturali che ci offrono servizi ecosistemici essenziali, che generano un risparmio concreto sui costi delle istituzioni, delle imprese e dei cittadini e un potenziale reddito aggiuntivo anche per gli agricoltori e i territori.

Ma per beneficiarne dobbiamo investire nella loro conservazione e nel loro ripristino, non nell'ennesima gettata di cemento per un supermercato di cui non c'è bisogno. Questo significa fare scelte concrete di bilancio. Garantire risorse dedicate a strumenti come LIFE che sostengono progetti di riqualificazione e ripristino della natura.

Dal 2025, quasi cinquanta sono state le iniziative sottoscritte da migliaia di rappresentanti di istituzioni, regioni, imprese, ricercatori e cittadini che hanno difeso quei fondi. Una mobilitazione che non potete ignorare, nemmeno dopo gli attacchi vergognosi dei colleghi delle destre contro di loro. Le imprese, grandi e piccole, si sono già rese conto di quanto preziosi fossero questi fondi, i fondi LIFE. Quando aprirete voi gli occhi?

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, go raibh maith agat as ucht an t-urlár a thabhairt dom.

As one who was centrally involved in ensuring the Nature Restoration Law was passed in Parliament, withstanding a lot of opposition – that is now in the past – I welcome this debate. But I am not happy that the Member States are not playing their part. I would ask the Commission to bring all pressures to bear on the Member States so they will submit their plans.

Secondly, one of the key elements in ensuring that it was passed in Parliament was that funding for farmers would be outside of the CAP and the measures would be voluntary. This has to be done and we have to ensure that they are incorporated in the Member States' plans, but also in the next MFF and the next CAP. It would be a betrayal of the promises made to ensure it was passed if that doesn't happen. So that is key.
We want to see this happening as soon as possible. The public want it. Farmers are willing to play their part, but we have to deliver.
Agus chomh luath agus is féidir linn é sin a dhéanamh, is luaithe a bheidh muid in ann an nádúr a athchóiriú.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, EU:n ennallistamisasetus on yksi tämän vuosisadan kaameimpia EU-politiikan virheitä. Metsiä koskevan laajamittaisen suojelun skenaario sahaisi Suomesta yli 20 000 työpaikkaa. Jos 20 000 suomalaiselta lähtee työ alta, työttömyyskortistoon lähtee pitkä jono perheenisiä ja -äitejä.

Vasemmisto, niin kutsuttu työntekijöiden puolustaja, iloitsi tällaisen tappomoukarin mennessä läpi. Samalla te haluatte hakata talouskasvumme. Luonnonvarakeskuksen arvion mukaan ennallistamisasetus voi sirkkelöidä jopa liki kolme miljardia euroa vuodessa pois Suomen talouden arvonlisäyksestä.

Valtion kassa on vasemmistolla tunnetusti loputon, mutta sanon tämän silti. Suomalaisen metsäjätin pääjohtaja varoitti jopa puolentoista miljardin vuosittaisesta lovesta valtion kassaan. Ennallistamisasetus on täysi katastrofi.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Minister, Members of Parliament, as I said in my opening remarks, this summer clearly showed what is at stake and what the cost of inaction is.
Minister Byrne, Jutta Paulus and Delara Burkhardt, all you mentioned this. It is worth repeating the economic impact: EUR 180 billion just this year. We cannot continue like this.

The Nature Restoration Regulation is not a silver bullet, I agree, but it is one tool to start building resilience and as this debate has also shown, successful restoration depends on getting the implementation right. We need to make it work in practice. The first crucial step is the submission of the national plans, as César Luena said, and we will do everything we can to support the Member States on a pragmatic implementation.
I just want to say that I am in contact with all the Member States, and the Minister will probably say, they are actively progressing in this work.

Many of you highlighted concerns over the costs, and as I said in the beginning, we have funds available. These must be used. But let me also agree that, of course, we need a long-term solution, which is why the next MFF will be an important milestone. The Commission has proposed an MFF with clear spending targets on this, and I really count on your support.

I also hear your concerns over what this law will mean for those who are closest to restorations in farms and forests. Jessica Polfjärd mentioned this, and this is the reason why we will continue to work closely with them, including to guide Member States on which areas restoration is needed and which flexibilities we have in place. I want to be very clear that restoration does not mean taking land out of production, but on urban development, yes, the regulation provides flexibility to accommodate housing developments.

Finally, we can only do this together. The Commission is committed. The Council is committed. Businesses – I met a lot of them – are committed. They recognise that economic and financial resilience depends on nature, water availability, soil fertility, and so forth. And maybe also most importantly, as Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy said, people are committed. The latest EU barometer reconfirmed EU citizens' large support for nature restoration. So I really count on you to support these goals.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Taraneh Rahimi's family says she can no longer walk. According to her cousin, a prison doctor ordered urgent hospital treatment and alleged torture worsened her condition. Therefore, it was refused, telling her that she would be executed anyway.

Taraneh, a young student, and Leila Abolhasani, a mother of two, face execution following prosecution linked to the January protests. Leila was reportedly filming a burning shop. Taraneh was arrested simply for taking part in the protest. This represents an alarming expansion of criminal liability. Its consequences reach into every family that hopes for a free Iran.
Iran must revoke both sentences and suspend all executions. Today, we can start with strong support for this resolution.

Iran must revoke both sentences and suspend all executions. Today, we can start with strong support for this resolution.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, how much more evidence must the victims provide before the world finally acts? Only in January, tens of thousands were murdered in the hands of the mullah regime in Iran. Four years after the killing of Jina Amini, the Iranian regime continues to answer courage with bullets, prison and execution.

Taraneh Rahimi and Leila Abolhasani and many others right now face execution simply for standing up against oppression. Their sentences must be overturned, execution must be halted and political prisoners must be freed.

This repression does not stop at Iran's border. The regime threatens dissidents here in Europe and has even with its tentacles – organised criminal gangs – carried out attacks. What are we waiting for? Enough. Europe must act, strengthen sanctions and hold the perpetrators accountable and end the gender apartheid.
To the courageous people in Iran: your fight for freedom continues being our fight.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, 'if you do not confess to your crimes, we will rape your twin sister in front of you.' These are the words used by prison guards against 19-year-old Taraneh Rahimi. She and her sister Romina have been tortured, dragged by their hair and beaten for months by the Iranian regime. And today, Taraneh faces a death sentence; Romina faces 25 years in prison.
Their alleged crime? Standing up for freedom during the January protests. Four years ago, in this very House, we stood with Iranian women and chanted 'jin, jiyan, azadi'.
Today, I want to say to my sisters in Iran: you are not alone. I am here with you. And I want Europe to be there for you.

Words are not enough and thousands of Iranian women need our help. Let us recognise gender apartheid for what it truly is: a crime against humanity. Let us maximise the pressure on the regime. Let us stand with Taraneh, Romina and so many others until they can hear these words in freedom.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Taraneh Rahimi and Leila Abolhasani are on death row, like so many others who demonstrated peacefully for freedom in Iran. They sang. They danced. They chanted for freedom. The regime shut down the internet and started to shoot. Tens of thousands were killed. Yet those responsible still enjoy power and impunity. But witnesses spoke. Human rights defenders documented. Names have been identified, chains of command traced. The evidence survived.

Dear colleagues, we cannot bring back those who were killed, but we can make sure that those responsible do not go unpunished. The regime may control the courts in Tehran, but it does not control the courtrooms in Europe. So if justice cannot be pursued inside Iran, it must be pursued elsewhere. I call on Germany, France, the Netherlands, Sweden: take up these cases under universal jurisdictions. Hold the perpetrators accountable. Iranian protesters should not fear the courtroom. Their oppressors should. Baraye Azadi.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, there is no question or discussion: Taraneh, Leila must not be executed. No one should.

But let us here tonight also mention Sima, 35 years old, a kidney patient. She had to visit seven pharmacies in Tehran to find life-saving medication. Why? Because Western sanctions are making medicines scarce and expensive. They are a death sentence for many Iranians today.

Your sanctions are killing, and your friends are killing too: Parnia, young Pilates instructor, dreamt of building her own Instagram page for her workout videos, killed by an Israeli strike on her apartment; Barnea, 23 years old, a teacher, a poet killed at home in Tehran by Israel; Hannah, eight years old; Zahra, seven; Athena, six; Nadia, nine; over 120 children killed by a US strike on a girls school in Iran.

Yet none of these received the empathy of this Parliament. Not even a mention of these names. Why? Because they were killed by your friends in a war that many of your governments supported. You invoke human rights of Iranians, but destroy their country and their lives with sanctions and bombs. The hypocrisy must stop tonight.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, dix exécutions par mois, c’est la cadence sinistre du régime iranien. En Iran, réclamer juste de quoi manger dans la rue peut valoir la torture, la prison, et, trop souvent, la peine de mort.

La guerre lancée en février par Trump et par Israël n’a pas non plus libéré le peuple iranien: elle a offert au régime un prétexte pour le réprimer davantage. Les Iraniens n’ont pas besoin qu’on fasse la guerre en leur nom: ils ont besoin de justice, qu’on arrête de les exécuter, qu’on sanctionne les responsables de cette terreur et qu’on obtienne justice pour les victimes et pour leur famille.

Nous sommes rassemblés ce soir pour demander la libération immédiate de Leïla, 43 ans, mère de deux adolescentes, condamnée à mort pour «guerre contre Dieu», et de Taraneh, une jeune Iranienne de 20 ans condamnée sur des aveux arrachés sous la torture. Nous ne pouvons pas, ici, détourner le regard, et nous continuerons de nous battre pour le mouvement «Femme, vie, liberté» et pour la liberté tout entière du peuple iranien!

paragraphs.text: Mr President, as we mark the World Day Against the Death Penalty this Saturday, we are still faced with the devastating reality of executions in Iran.

In this mandate alone, we have adopted seven resolutions on Iran. But what changes? The repression only gets worse. In 2025, Iran carried out at least 2 159 executions, the highest number since 1981. But we're not just talking numbers, we're talking about people: Taraneh Rahimi, Leila Abolhasani, but also Zahra Shahbaz Tabari and Arghavan Falahi, and so many others. They must be released.

So let us remember: the regime can hear us and so can the brave, silenced people of Iran, so let us keep speaking, keep naming, and keep standing with the Iranian people. And I call upon our national leaders: we must never, ever negotiate with a regime that exploits wars as a pretext to carry out executions of their own people.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Madam Commissioner, colleagues, the mullahs' regime in Iran remains as consistent as ever. The imprisonment, torture and execution of political opponents are everyday occurrences.

Taraneh Rahimi and Leila Abolhasani were given death sentences based on unfounded charges obtained through torture and other forms of coercion. The regime has also sentenced two other women – Zahira Tabari and Arghavan Fallahi – to death for alleged membership of the PMOI. Over the past few months, 11 political prisoners have been executed on charges related to the PMOI. The rulers of Tehran fear the PMOI and extend their oppressive policies.

The EU must urgently expand the list of Iranian officials subject to sanctions, step up restricting Iranian diplomatic representation in the EU, and abandon its policy of appeasement of the cruellest regime in the world.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, what is happening in Iran is not only a human rights crisis – it is not. It is a systematic campaign of repression against a people demanding only freedom and dignity. Let's not forget that Iran has the highest death sentence rate per capita in the world.

The cases of Taraneh Rahimi and Leila Abolhasani are a stark reminder of this reality. Taraneh, one of the Rahimi twins, faces the death penalty, while Leila Abolhasani has also been sentenced to death following the January protests. They are not alone: Arghavan Fallahi, Zahra Shahbaz Tabari and Verisheh Moradi are also among the women political prisoners at risk of execution.

These cases raise grave consequences and concerns about arbitrary detention, due process and the use of the death penalty to silence dissidents. We cannot remain silent. The European Union must continue to stand firmly with the Iranian people, particularly the women and young people who are courageously demanding freedom.
We have to call on the United Nations Security Council for the referral of Iran's regime to the International Criminal Court.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, Taraneh e Leila sono state condannate a morte in Iran. La loro colpa? Essere due donne che hanno avuto il coraggio di partecipare alle manifestazioni contro il regime che continua a sparare sulle persone.

Dall'inizio della guerra, in Iran sono stati giustiziati ventinove uomini e, dall'inizio dell'anno, almeno sedici donne, perché si sono ribellati al terrore. L'iter della giustizia iraniana è sempre lo stesso: minacce e torture durante gli interrogatori, procedure legali viziate, prove incomplete, divieto per la difesa di poter esercitare i propri diritti e pena capitale come soluzione finale.

Queste due condanne non devono restare invisibili. Teniamo alta l'attenzione sulla vicenda ed esercitiamo pressione sul regime iraniano, con ogni mezzo, perché vengano rispettate le vite e le libertà di queste due donne e di tutte le loro sorelle e di tutti i loro fratelli che subiscono condanne ingiuste e arbitrarie.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora comisaria, la política exterior de la Unión Europea está vinculada por el derecho internacional y por los derechos humanos al artículo 21 del Tratado de Funcionamiento de la Unión Europea, lo que exige estar a favor de la paz y en contra de la pena de muerte. Eso explica que los mismos que criticamos una guerra ilegal contra Irán por el estrecho de Ormuz con el pretexto de liberar a su pueblo —lo que no solo no ha sucedido, sino que además ha reforzado el régimen de los mulás y los ayatolás y ha encarecido exponencialmente la vida de los europeos— denunciamos el insoportable balance de penas de muerte y de ejecuciones injustas cometidas por ese régimen tiránico de los ayatolás, que se ensañan con los miembros de la oposición y con la resistencia.

Por tanto, este debate es necesario y no solamente oportuno para denunciar esa nueva condena de muerte de una mujer inocente perseguida por sus ideas, en Irán y en todas partes. Merece la atención del Parlamento Europeo y merece una Resolución contundente con la aspiración de que algún día los culpables se sienten en el banquillo de la justicia internacional.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, on 16 September, we marked the anniversary of the death of Mahsa Amini, a young and brave Iranian woman who was killed only for dreaming of a country where her rights are respected. Today, we raise the cases of two other women, Taraneh Rahimi and Leila Abolhasani, who, like many other Iranians, risk their lives for the simple aspiration to have their universal human rights and fundamental freedom respected, protected and fulfilled. This is unacceptable.

The high rate of executions in Iran is appalling. According to some sources, at least 932 cases have been reported so far in 2026. We are especially alarmed by the use of harsh sentences and executions to intimidate, suppress dissent, restrict civic space and freedom of expression, and target ethnic and religious minorities.

Since 2011, the EU has imposed targeted sanctions against individuals and entities responsible for serious human rights violations in Iran. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' designation as a terrorist organisation in February sent a clear message: there can be no impunity for the repression of peaceful protests. This approach will continue as long as necessary.

Together with the Member States, we strongly support accountability, including through the UN fact-finding mission, Special Rapporteur on Human Rights in Iran and the Human Rights Council. We are also mindful that, as the Nobel Prize winner Narges Mohammadi recently reminded us in her moving interview, 'the Iranian population is caught between the government's domestic repression and the war'.

The EU deeply regrets the loss of innocent lives in Iran, including many children. We have urged all sides to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians in all circumstances. The EU is redoubling efforts towards diplomatic solutions, as sustained engagement remains the only way to address our concerns with Iran.

Honourable Members, through multiple channels, the EU calls on Iranian authorities to immediately end the practice of imposing and carrying out death sentences, in particular those targeting protesters, dissidents and political prisoners, who are simply standing up for the respect of their basic rights.

We urge the release of Taraneh and Leila and all of those unjustly detained for exercising their legitimate right to freedom of expression. The Tehran authorities must understand that it is time to change this behaviour towards their own people and the world. Until that moment, the EU will spare no efforts in supporting the legitimate aspiration of Taraneh, Leila and all Iranian women, children and men who seek to live in a country where their rights are respected, protected and fulfilled.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, first, I want to thank the S&D Group for initiating this resolution and debate.

Some think Georgia is a lost cause. They say: 'Accept the situation. Let's be realistic.' Many thought that we Lithuanians were lost too, but we were not. Georgians have not given up. People are still protesting. The majority still wants to have a European future. That is why our message today is also important to them.

The regime wants to ban the opposition parties. It pushed the German political foundations to close their offices in Tbilisi. It puts in prison those who work for democracy and the rule of law. This is not strength; this is fear. Ivanishvili's regime chooses Russia by refusing the will of the Georgian people. Putinism will be defeated. The Bidzinasation of Georgia will be defeated. Russia is not the future for anyone. Ukraine is still standing and fighting. Armenia also made its choice despite pressure from Moscow. So hope is not lost.

That is exactly why we must act now. Sanctions are a must on Ivanishvili and all those responsible. Member States should not wait. The desire for freedom is stronger than fear. We should stand with the Georgian people.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, how desperate must a government be to ban every political party but its own? How terrified of its own people must it be to beat up peaceful protesters, arrest journalists and use chemical agents against its own population? But this is what we are witnessing in Georgia, where the Georgian Dream regime seems to have entered a bizarre Soviet revival mode: abroad, by dragging Georgia away from its European future and back into the orbit of the Kremlin; and at home, by trying to build a Soviet‑style one‑party state.

But Georgian Dream has one problem, and that is that Georgians themselves don't want to be Homo Sovieticus again. They don't want to just keep their heads down and their mouths shut. No, Georgians have tasted freedom, they have tasted Europe and they will not give up on either.

That is exactly why we must not give up on Georgia, why we must stand with imprisoned journalists like Mzia Amaglobeli, why we must sanction Georgia's de facto leader Ivanishvili, and why we must send Georgian dreams, Soviet fantasies, back to where they belong, into the darkest pages of our history books, because Georgia's future belongs in Europe.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Bidzina Iwaniszwili niszczy demokrację w Gruzji i prowadzi ten kraj w stronę rosyjskiej dyktatury. Przejął państwowe instytucje, podporządkował sobie wymiar sprawiedliwości, prześladuje opozycję i chce zdelegalizować partie polityczne swoich przeciwników. To nie jest już zwykły kryzys polityczny. To jest próba ustanowienia oligarchicznej dyktatury.

A ofiarą tej politycznej zemsty jest Michael Saakaszwili – były prezydent Gruzji, człowiek, który walczył o europejską przyszłość swojego kraju i przeciwstawiał się rosyjskiej agresji jest więziony przez ludzi, którzy chcą wyrwać Gruzję z europejskiej drogi. Mówię to jasno: uwolnić Michaela Saakaszwilego natychmiast, bezwarunkowo. Uwolnić wszystkich więźniów politycznych. I do Unii Europejskiej: przestańmy tylko potępiać, czas na zdecydowane, skoordynowane działania wobec Iwaniszwilego, jego majątku i całej sieci ludzi, którzy utrzymują ten system represji. Gruzja należy do narodu gruzińskiego i do Europy, nie do Iwaniszwilego, nie do Putina.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, the Georgian dream became a nightmare for the Georgian people. Georgia's oligarch is banning opposition parties. We have seen this before – in Belarus. Two dictators, two regimes loyal to Putin, two peoples taken as hostages. Both regimes jail political opponents, both on Moscow's orders, both killing the future of their own nations. Like Putin, they are just afraid of freedom. They are afraid of free speech.

And now, like Putin and Lukashenko, they are also expelling European foundations like the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung and the Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung. Those organisations contributed to Georgia's success in the last decades, and ironically, some of them worked and learned in this organisation, so they learned democracy to destroy it later on.

Colleagues, the people of Georgia is nothing like this regime. They are Europeans through and through, like we are, continuously fighting for freedom and for a European future. So I am also optimistic – because all bloody regimes fall. All political prisoners, including Elene Khoshtaria, will walk free. Those who served Russia instead of Georgian people should pay a high price for their treason.

One more sentence: very interesting that the so-called Patriots are not here. When we are talking here about freedom, about united Europe and fighting the dictatorships of Putin, they are just not here. We know why.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Commissaria, la Georgia sta vivendo un drammatico declino democratico, mentre migliaia di cittadine e cittadini riempiono le piazze per rivendicare diritti e libertà. Il partito Georgian Dream, risultato di maggioranza dopo elezioni caratterizzate da brogli e violenze, sta sistematicamente eliminando ogni opposizione per divenire l'unico partito presente in Parlamento.

Centinaia di arresti senza alcuna motivazione giuridica e tra questi Mikheil Saakashvili, da anni in carcere senza motivazione, che, sin dalla sua elezione nel 2004 come Presidente della Georgia, aveva contrastato l'occupazione militare russa, aveva combattuto la corruzione e chiesto formalmente al presidente Prodi l'ingresso in Unione europea. Io ero presente quel giorno a Tbilisi a quella manifestazione.

Georgian Dream è diventato non un sogno ma l'incubo dei georgiani, l'incubo georgiano. Un partito del tutto subalterno alla Russia, che continua peraltro ad occupare, anche in maniera militare, Abkhazia e Ossezia del Sud.

Con queste scelte antidemocratiche e con questo condizionamento da parte della Russia viene da anni bloccato il processo di ingresso della Georgia nell'Unione europea. Commissione europea e Stati membri devono usare tutte le leve disponibili e anche le sanzioni per sostenere il diritto del popolo georgiano di vivere in un paese democratico e per chiedere la liberazione dei detenuti politici ingiustamente carcerati.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Mehr Doppelmoral geht nicht. Sie sorgen sich um mögliche Verbote von Oppositionsparteien in Georgien? Warum wollen Sie dann in Deutschland die AfD verbieten oder auf europäischer Ebene die ESN-Partei? Merken Sie überhaupt diesen intellektuellen Widerspruch? Wer die Demokratie im eigenen Land angreift, hat kein Recht, sich über mutmaßliche Demokratiedefizite anderswo aufzuregen. Sie machen sich komplett unglaubwürdig. Und dieser Mangel an Glaubwürdigkeit zeigt sich auch in Ihrer selektiven Empörung. Als in der Ukraine über 20 Parteien verboten wurden, gab es keinen Aufschrei. Im Gegenteil, Sie belohnten Selenskyj mit noch mehr Milliarden. Sie missbrauchen das Konzept der Menschenrechte aus geopolitischen Gründen für Ihren selektiven Moralimperialismus. Und dieser selektive Moralimperialismus kostet uns Glaubwürdigkeit auf internationalem Parkett. Auch deshalb verlieren wir global an Einfluss.

Was stört Sie überhaupt an Georgien? Das Land entwickelt sich doch ordentlich. Die Fakten: 8 Prozent Wirtschaftswachstum. Davon können wir nur träumen. Im Chandler Good Government Index schneidet Georgien besser ab als mancher EU-Mitgliedstaat. Und im Rechtsstaatlichkeits-Ranking des World Justice Project ist Georgien auf Platz eins in Osteuropa und Zentralasien.

Worüber reden wir hier eigentlich? Ich sage es Ihnen: Es geht Ihnen gar nicht um Demokratie und Partizipation. Es geht darum, dass Georgien den woken Wahnsinn und die LGBT-Propaganda ablehnt, weil es seine starke christliche Tradition bewahren möchte. Es geht darum, dass sich Georgien nicht am Sanktionsregime gegen Russland beteiligt, weil es nicht zu einer zweiten Ukraine werden möchte. Das müssen wir verstehen. Georgien ist ein kleines Land in schwieriger Umgebung – Russland, Iran, Türkei. Unter solchen Bedingungen muss sich Georgien anders verhalten, als Sie es gerne hätten. Wir sollten das berücksichtigen. Und wir sollten Georgien als wichtigen Partner, als Brücke nach Asien verstehen. Das ist Realpolitik. Ihr konfrontativer Ansatz hingegen treibt Georgien nur in die Arme fremder Hegemonialmächte. Und das ist nicht in unserem Interesse.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, a candidate country in name only – that is how the Commission depicted Georgia during the presentation of the 2025 enlargement report.

Unfortunately, almost a year later, the regime in Tbilisi was once more proving that this assessment was correct. In pursuing a ban on every major oppositional party, the regime has taken another callous step towards authoritarian rule.

Helmut Brandstätter already mentioned it: on 30 September, the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung and the Friedrich-Naumann-Stiftung were forced to close their offices due to a new regulation on foreign grants. It enforces far-reaching state control over international funding and in some cases even provides for criminal penalties. Both foundations have stood out through their decade-long contribution to political education, democratic pluralism and European integration. All the more, it is now important that we stand by the Georgian people, who, by an overwhelming majority, rally behind the goal of European integration.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señora comisaria, el futuro de Georgia pertenece a su pueblo, y solo a su pueblo.

Durante años, desde la Unión Europea hemos construido una relación política y parlamentaria muy estrecha con Georgia. Yo mismo lo he comprobado: el pueblo georgiano es un pueblo hermano. Pero hoy, sus autoridades persiguen a la oposición, asfixian a los movimientos sociales y acorralan a la prensa libre.

Por eso, desde esta Cámara, reclamamos la liberación de los presos políticos, exigimos sanciones al régimen y pedimos elecciones democráticas. Queremos a Georgia cerca de la Unión Europea, y eso exige elecciones libres y respeto al pluralismo.
La Unión Europea debe estar siempre del lado del pueblo georgiano, de su derecho a decidir y de su aspiración a vivir en paz y en libertad. Y no vamos a darle la espalda ahora.

paragraphs.text: Senhor presidente, George Steiner via a Europa como um mapa de cafés, lugares onde se conversa, se discorda e se pensa em liberdade. Traçou esse mapa de Lisboa a Odessa, e deixou Moscovo de fora. Tiblíssi, dizem, tem alguns dos melhores cafés do continente. Se Steiner tivesse atravessado o mar Negro até Batumi, teria posto Tiblíssi no mapa.

A Geórgia é cristã ortodoxa desde o século IV e guardou a sua língua e a sua fé contra todos os impérios. 70 % dos georgianos querem pertencer à União Europeia. Sabem de que lado do mapa querem estar. Não nos cabe escolher governos em Tiblíssi. Essa escolha pertence aos georgianos, em liberdade, com eleições livres, instituições sólidas e respeito pelo Estado de direito.

Cabe‑nos dizer com clareza que um quinto do território georgiano continua ocupado pela Rússia. Nenhuma nação soberana encontra a sua liberdade na órbita de quem a ocupa. A porta da Europa deve continuar aberta, e a mesa do café à espera.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, indeed, observing the attempt to ban political parties in Georgia, we must acknowledge that Europe's response to authoritarian consolidation in Georgia has been inadequate so far.

The US, UK and individual EU Member States have gone further than the Union in sanctioning those responsible for repression against Georgian people. We should close this gap. First, we should impose targeted sanctions and visa bans, including on especially judges enabling politically motivated repression. Second, engagement with Georgian authorities must depend on tangible steps to reverse this course and to implement Venice Commission recommendations, which are a roadmap for restoring judicial independence and political pluralism. Third, we should prevent policing equipment that could facilitate further repression from being sold or transferred to Georgia.
Finally, Europe must strengthen direct support for independent media, political parties and civil society, while demanding the release of those imprisoned for political grounds.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, it was in October 2024 when I observed with colleagues the elections in Georgia, and we raised at that time serious concerns about pressure on voters. Now, after two years, Georgian Dream is moving from pressuring voters to excluding parties that could challenge its power. And I want to underline also what my colleague David McAllister mentioned already: I, with colleagues, took the chance to work with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation several times in Georgia. Now it is over. It is finished. It was not possible anymore.

Together with these developments, Georgian Dream creates the conditions for a one-party dictatorship. Our responsibility is to stand with all defenders of democracy in Georgia, while their democratic power is systematically taken away. We have to fight and to support the democracy movement in Georgia.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, el Gobierno de Georgia, acosando y persiguiendo a su oposición, impone al país un camino inverso y contrario a los valores europeos. Pero es que Georgia contradice, también, los valores del Consejo de Europa —del que es uno de los 46 Estados miembros—, una organización cuyo propósito es la promoción del Estado de Derecho, la democracia y los derechos humanos.

Segundo, Georgia figura todavía en la lista de espera de países que han abierto negociaciones para una futura adhesión, lo que pone de manifiesto un problema que se ha debatido durante este período parcial de sesiones, cuando hemos confrontado al Consejo sobre la ampliación, instándole a que exija a los candidatos cumplimiento estricto de los valores de la Unión Europea consagrados en su artículo dos.

Y tercero, esto pone también de manifiesto que, en el caso de no cumplimiento, deberíamos tener algún dispositivo —y quizá una reforma institucional— que permita desclasificar, descatalogar finalmente a un Estado que camina en el sentido contrario a los valores de la Unión. Porque —reconozcámoslo— Turquía, a estas alturas, permanece todavía en la lista de espera a pesar de que la virtualidad de esa candidatura hace muchísimo tiempo que dejó de ser creíble.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Europe is on its way to having a new dictatorship.

The Georgian regime is tightening the screws even further on the nation. Foreign-funded organisations, activists and independent groups: for a leadership seeking a dictatorship, these have posed a threat, but what is even more frightening for a party reaching for a dictatorship is opposition. Now, the ruling party is aiming to ban opposition parties.
Time for everyone to wake up. The ruling party is called Georgian Dream. It has turned into a Georgian nightmare. That nightmare will not end if we just stand by as eyewitnesses.
Europe must be tough against this regime. Impose visa bans, place sanctions. Let's say no to a new mini-Russia.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear people of Europe, last week I was sitting together with a circle of friends, and one of them was a young woman from Georgia. She asked me, 'How long do you think it will be until Georgia joins the European Union?' And I said, '20 years, maybe 10, if things go well'. I fear that this is the case, because if we look to Georgia, the government forces its population far away from the path towards Europe, but it's just a matter of time.

So I say to the Georgian ruling party, I say to the Georgian oligarchs, I say to the Georgian puppets of Russia: enjoy your mansions, enjoy your luxury cars, enjoy your power, because eventually you will die.
And then the next generation of Georgians will take over and they will lead Georgia to their European future. So maybe we have to wait, but the end goal is certain.

interventions.speaker_label: Jessika Roswall, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members of the European Parliament, under Georgian Dream, Georgia continues to drift away from democratic norms and the European path chosen by its people. What we are witnessing is a systematic attack on democratic institutions, fundamental rights, political pluralism and the rule of law. The recent Constitutional Court lawsuit brought by the Georgian Dream parliamentarians to ban opposition parties ahead of the 2028 election is a part of this pattern. Such actions strike at the heart of democracy and they undermine Georgia's EU accession.

The scale of the democratic backsliding in Georgia is unprecedented for a candidate country. The Commission's enlargement report from 2025 made this clear. Instead of advancing reforms and moving closer to the European Union, the Georgian authorities have taken actions that undermine the rule of law and shrink civic space. They continue anti-EU rhetoric and disinformation, aiming to undermine the credibility of EU among Georgian citizens.

Distinguished Members of Parliament, the Georgian people have long aspired to be a part of the European family. We continue to stand with the Georgian people in the face of current challenges and in the face of the challenges, the European Union also responded with downgraded high-level political contacts with the authorities. We paused meetings of association agreement bodies and we stopped assistance directly benefiting the authorities. In March 2026, we suspended visa-free travel for holders of Georgian diplomatic services and official passports. At the same time, we remain strongly committed to supporting the Georgian people and their civil society.

The European Union calls on the Georgian Dream party to reverse its detrimental actions, amend anti-democratic legislation, and release arbitrarily detained opposition members. We urge the government to engage in meaningful dialogue with all political stakeholders to restore trust. Our door is open for constructive dialogue with Georgia based on a mutual respect, to find a way out of the current deadlock in our relations. The European Union stands with the people of Georgia and the democratic European aspiration.

paragraphs.text: Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos, Azerbaidžanas galėtų džiaugtis savo pagerėjusia tarptautine padėtimi regione ir atsigręžti į europines vertybes, o vietoj to tęsia karą prieš savo paties piliečius. Rugsėjį žymus Azerbaidžano žmogaus teisių gynėjas ir rinkimų stebėtojas Anaras Mammadli po akivaizdžiai ydingo proceso nuteistas trylikai metų kalėjimo. Opozicijos veikėjas Ali Karimli už grotų laukia teismo - jis apkaltintas tariamu bandymu įvykdyti perversmą. Todėl kreipiuosi tiesiai: prezidente Alijevai, paleiskite politinius kalinius. Jums nereikia demonstruoti jėgos prieš juos. Jūsų šalis turtinga energetiniais ištekliais, geopolitinė reikšmė regione išaugusi, aktyvus karas su kaimynais nebevyksta. Tikroji politinė jėga šiandien būtų parodyti, kad Azerbaidžanas nebijo laisvo žodžio ir yra pasirengęs sugrįžti prie europinių žmogaus teisių įsipareigojimų bei atviros politinės konkurencijos principų.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, não poderia começar esta intervenção sem manifestar a minha alegria pela libertação de Gubad Ibadoghlu, por ele e pela sua família. Não podemos sequer imaginar o sofrimento deste ativista anticorrupção nos calabouços de um regime que recorre cada vez mais aos métodos mais perversos para silenciar as diversas oposições.

Um dos casos que aqui nos traz é bem um exemplo dessa perversidade. Segundo relatos credíveis, Ali Karimli foi sujeito à privação do sono durante mais de 70 dias, com um barulho altíssimo a soar a cada 15 minutos junto à sua cela. Nos períodos de calor extremo, contou apenas com cinco litros de água por semana. Este tipo de sevícias, em combinação com o isolamento, torna incontornável a utilização de uma palavra: tortura.

Os opositores políticos no Azerbaijão são presos e são torturados. Perante isto, não temos apenas o dever de sancionar os responsáveis de uma vez por todas, como temos de nos perguntar seriamente se queremos, se podemos, aliás, manter algum tipo de parceria com este regime controlado pela Rússia.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! W Azerbejdżanie mamy do czynienia z systemowym tłumieniem opozycji, niezależnych mediów i społeczeństwa obywatelskiego. Ali Karimli, lider azerbejdżańskiego Frontu Ludowego, ugrupowania prouropejskiego, centroprawicowego i wywodzącego się z antykomunistycznego ruchu niepodległościowego, od listopada ubiegłego roku przebywa w areszcie. Postawiono mu zarzut próby siłowego przejęcia władzy, za które grozi dożywocie. Jego przypadek pokazuje, że represje dotykają tych, którzy opowiadają się za europejskim kierunkiem rozwoju Azerbejdżanu, za demokracją i odejściem od autorytarnego dziedzictwa postsowieckiego.

Z kolei Anar Mammadli, obrońca praw człowieka i szef Centrum Monitoringu Wyborów i Studiów Demokratycznych, laureat Nagrody Praw Człowieka im. Vaclava Havla, skazany na 13 lat więzienia po procesie, którego rzetelność jest poważnie kwestionowana. Ale więźniów politycznych jest znacznie, znacznie więcej. Dane mówią o 328 więźniach politycznych w Azerbejdżanie.

Europa nie może milczeć. Współpraca energetyczna i gospodarcza z Azerbejdżanem nie może odbywać się kosztem praw człowieka ani kosztem tych, którzy w kraju reprezentują wartości demokratyczne i proeuropejskie.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, we must acknowledge a stark reality. Earlier this year, Azerbaijan's National Assembly unilaterally suspended cooperation with the European Parliament, dismissing our human rights concerns as ungrounded. Yet, outrageous new cases prove otherwise.

While trade and connectivity projects with the EU flourish, democratic voices continue to fall victim to repression. Ali Karimli, a prominent opposition leader, has been detained since November 2025. Nine months later, he remains behind bars in deeply concerning conditions.

Similarly, a prominent human rights activist and government critic, Anar Mammadli, spent more than two years in pre-trial detention. This September, he was sentenced to 13 years in prison. This is already his second long sentence on politically motivated charges.

These are not isolated cases, but a broader pattern of repression against civil society. Many more human rights defenders, journalists, democratic opposition representatives are brutally persecuted. Our partnership with Azerbaijan cannot come at the expense of our foundational principles. We demand the immediate release of Ali Karimli, Anar Mammadli and all political prisoners.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, Commissioner, let me start by welcoming the fact that Dr Gubad Ibadoghlu, the 2024 Sakharov Prize finalist, has finally been allowed to leave house arrest and is now receiving essential medical care that he much needed. But his charges must still be dropped, and he was far from being the only person arrested for political motivations in Azerbaijan.

Look no further than the cases of opposition leader Ali Karimli and human rights defender Anar Mammadli: the first detained for nearly a year and subjected to inhumane treatment; the second just sentenced for 13 years in prison. Like them, there are at least 300 others in the country. Criminalisation is common practice towards opposition figures, human rights defenders, independent media and NGO workers.

As Azerbaijan's main trading partner, the EU cannot turn a blind eye. We should suspend energy trade relations with Azerbaijan until meaningful progress is made towards releasing all political prisoners and upholding democracy and rule of law. Breaking our reliance on fossil‑fuel‑rich authoritarian regimes must be a priority.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, j’ai le sentiment que notre Parlement excelle dans l’art de se donner bonne conscience. Depuis plusieurs mois maintenant, nous multiplions les résolutions pour dénoncer la situation politique en Azerbaïdjan – à juste titre –, mais sans que nos actes suivent nos mots.

Pourtant, sur le terrain, l’urgence est bien réelle. Elle frappe d’abord la société civile, les médias, les opposants politiques, tous broyés par le régime autoritaire d’Aliyev. Elle frappe aussi les anciens dirigeants arméniens du Haut-Karabakh, toujours enfermés dans les geôles azerbaïdjanaises, au terme de procès factices.

Mais alors, concrètement, que fait l’Union européenne? D’une main elle signe un nouvel accord de partenariat avec Bakou, de l’autre elle envoie nos représentants de l’Union européenne en visite guidée dans le Haut-Karabakh vidé de sa population après l’épuration ethnique de 2023 – quel cynisme!

Alors, évidemment, il faut exiger la libération immédiate et inconditionnelle de tous les prisonniers politiques azerbaïdjanais ainsi que la libération immédiate et inconditionnelle de tous les prisonniers arméniens détenus illégalement. Mais faire des résolutions ne suffit plus: il est temps de conditionner nos relations avec l’Azerbaïdjan au respect strict des droits humains et des libertés fondamentales. Si nous ne le faisons pas, l’Union européenne perdra ce qu’il lui reste de crédibilité.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Kommissionen! Att säga sin åsikt är inte ett brott. Att kritisera regeringar, kungar, presidenter är inte ett brott. Att klä sig som man vill är inte ett brott. Trots det är det i land efter land sådana saker som är en av de vanligaste orsakerna till att människor berövas sin frihet, fängslas, torteras, till och med avrättas.

Respekt för demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstat är en ledstjärna för Europeiska unionen, både här hemma i EU men också i våra relationer till omvärlden. I dag riktar vi oss till Azerbajdzjan, som villkorslöst måste frige alla politiska fångar och lägga ner samtliga politiska åtal – samtliga politiskt motiverade åtal. Det finns ingen annan väg framåt om vi ska kunna ha en hållbar, långsiktig relation med Azerbajdzjan.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, the persecution of Ali Karimli and Anar Mammadli is yet another reminder of the brutal totalitarian nature of Aliyev's regime. Behind a facade, it systematically silences political opposition, independent journalists and civil society.

Its repression also targets foreign nationals. We must not forget Ruben Vardanyan and the other Armenians still held hostage in Baku, who are subject to sham trials. That is why the EU must take a principled and considered approach towards Azerbaijan and defend our values over economic gains.

I therefore call on the Commission to demand the immediate and unconditional release of all political prisoners, including Armenian hostages at every meeting with the Azerbaijani representatives and put human rights at the centre of our foreign policy.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, hace un momento hemos hablado de Georgia y, ahora, de Azerbaiyán, Estado también miembro del Consejo de Europa en manifiesta contradicción con los valores fundamentales de esta organización con sede en Estrasburgo: Estado de Derecho, democracia y derechos humanos.

Un país que mantiene un viejo conflicto con Armenia por sus respectivos enclaves de Nagorno Karabaj y Najicheván, sobre los que negociaron y llegaron a un acuerdo fuera de Europa, nada más y nada menos que en el despacho oval del presidente Trump. Y, sin embargo, la cúpula de la Comisión, la presidenta Von der Leyen, ha saludado al dictador Aliyev —dictador hereditario, porque también lo fue su padre en tiempos de la Unión Soviética— en búsqueda de aliados estratégicos energéticos en la vecindad de las antiguas repúblicas soviéticas.

Pues bien: es el momento de que la Unión Europea emplee toda su energía y capacidad diplomática para hacer valer los derechos humanos de los prisioneros políticos en Azerbaiyán, pero también de los armenios desplazados de Nagorno Karabaj cuando Azerbaiyán recuperó su soberanía.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, there are over 300 political prisoners in Azerbaijan, some sentenced to 13 years in prison. Hate to say it, but it is the EU's business partner that imprisons opposition figures and journalists. What message is the EU putting out by not acting? Does it mean that violations can be bought at a certain price? Can values be ignored when the benefits are big enough?

The EU has been giving Israel moral lectures. For what? For defending itself. Ursula von der Leyen, the President of the European Commission, even wanted to suspend the EU's trade agreement with Israel. But when Azerbaijan imprisons political opponents, business just continues. 'Nothing to see here.'
Europe must speak clearly: partnership with us cannot include political repression.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, this is not the first resolution of the European Parliament concerning Anar Mammadli – that was in December 2024, when this Parliament criticised his detention on bogus charges. And at that point he had already been in detention since April. He remained in detention until his recent conviction for illegal entrepreneurship and sentence of 13 years.

In the meantime, the European Union continued with trade as usual. In the meantime, the High Representative, who claims to cherish human rights, went to Azerbaijan and praised them for being a valuable partner. To say the very least, that is unfortunate. One could go and say a lot more.

His conviction in September arose from the non-registration of his election observation group. That in turn had been criticised by the European Court of Human Rights as politically motivated, and he was convicted previously in connection with that, and that conviction was an aggregated factor. So his recent conviction flies in the face of previous resolutions of this Parliament, previous judgements of the European Court of Human Rights, and calls to address that judgement by the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe.

Azerbaijan is simply a rogue state when it comes to human rights, and it is not good enough that the European Parliament treats them as a good partner for any purpose whatsoever. This must be addressed and, in particular, political prisoners must be released.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear people of Europe, first of all, I would like to remind Mr Tynkkynen about the difference between certain geopolitical situations.

Second of all, I have a quite interesting thing in my life. I have an Iranian Azeri APA, and whenever I do a speech about Azerbaijan, he gets afterwards a WhatsApp message or a call from the Azerbaijani ambassador. And, every time, the Azerbaijani ambassador complains that I insulted the honour of his country and that I apply double standards for all the other things that happen in the world or inside the European Union.

The funny thing is that, when I then confront him with what happens, he says he is also in disagreement with his government. So he knows. Mr Ambassador – I will not say the name – you know. I think the Azerbaijani Government knows. Everyone knows what's happening there.
So, please, to all Azerbaijanis: don't be insulted by this debate. Don't be insulted by what we say. Maybe reflect and get yourself acquainted with the reality of the politics of your country.

interventions.speaker_label: Jessika Roswall, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, this debate has once again underlined why continued international attention on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan remains necessary. Like this House, we are following with great concern the arrest and continued detention of Ali Karimli, including reports of deterioration in his detention conditions. We are also closely following the case of Anar Mammadli and the 13‑year prison sentence recently handed down to him. These cases come against the backdrop of a wave of detentions and convictions since late 2023, affecting journalists, human rights defenders and other activists expressing their views critical of the authorities.

Mr President, honourable Members, let me also be clear: we value our relationship with Azerbaijan as a partner and key link between Europe and Asia. Its strategic importance has become even more evident in the current geopolitical circumstances, as war continues to affect regional energy, transport and transit routes. Azerbaijan plays an important role for regional stability. We welcome the progress achieved in the peace process between Baku and Yerevan. The two sides have taken important confidence‑building steps, notably by the release by Azerbaijan of four Armenians earlier this year. We encourage the parties to address all remaining humanitarian issues as part of their bilateral dialogue.

This year has also been marked by constructive steps in the relationship between the EU and Azerbaijan. Consolidating this relationship serves our shared strategic interests and our efforts towards peace. A closer and more trusted partnership also gives us a greater space to address difficult issues through dialogue and engagement. We will therefore continue to call on the Government of Azerbaijan to uphold its international obligations, including with regard to freedom of expression and association, due process and the right to a fair trial. I hear your concerns, and I will be very clear that VP/HR Kallas raised individual human rights cases during her visit to Baku last May. The EU delegation in Baku equally continues to raise such cases with the Azerbaijani authorities.

Mr President, honourable Members, this debate has once again underlined why continued international attention on the human rights situation in Azerbaijan remains necessary. Like this House, we are following with great concern the arrest and continued detention of Ali Karimli, including reports of deterioration in his detention conditions. We are also closely following the case of Anar Mammadli and the 13‑year prison sentence recently handed down to him. These cases come against the backdrop of a wave of detentions and convictions since late 2023, affecting journalists, human rights defenders and other activists expressing their views critical of the authorities.

Mr President, honourable Members, let me also be clear: we value our relationship with Azerbaijan as a partner and key link between Europe and Asia. Its strategic importance has become even more evident in the current geopolitical circumstances, as war continues to affect regional energy, transport and transit routes. Azerbaijan plays an important role for regional stability. We welcome the progress achieved in the peace process between Baku and Yerevan. The two sides have taken important confidence‑building steps, notably by the release by Azerbaijan of four Armenians earlier this year. We encourage the parties to address all remaining humanitarian issues as part of their bilateral dialogue.

This year has also been marked by constructive steps in the relationship between the EU and Azerbaijan. Consolidating this relationship serves our shared strategic interests and our efforts towards peace. A closer and more trusted partnership also gives us a greater space to address difficult issues through dialogue and engagement. We will therefore continue to call on the Government of Azerbaijan to uphold its international obligations, including with regard to freedom of expression and association, due process and the right to a fair trial. I hear your concerns, and I will be very clear that VP/HR Kallas raised individual human rights cases during her visit to Baku last May. The EU delegation in Baku equally continues to raise such cases with the Azerbaijani authorities.
